sessions.work_done: Built research_layer/step_A3_deseasonalization.py, applying Rule FF-27's procedure for real for the first time in this project. G-SELF known-answer test (own machinery, not reusing the sister scripts' IC-only KAT): injected a known synthetic seasonal shape, confirmed the S(t) estimator recovers it (corr=0.943) and that dividing by it flattens per-bin variance (CV 0.407 -> 0.022). PASS. Then estimated S(t) = normalized mean(|log_ret|) per (weekday, 5-min-bin) on the full held export (50,000 rows, 2025-11-25 to 2026-07-29), and re-measured the two ICs already on record (magnitude: |score| vs mfe_atr; directional: score vs 1-bar-forward log return) both raw and divided by S(t).

result.seasonal_shape_confirmed: Real, not spurious: hour-of-day |log_ret| ranges 0.64x-1.44x (broker-time hours 23 and 17 respectively) on the well-populated bins (~2000+ samples/hour pooled). This is a believable session-driven shape (afternoon/London-NY-overlap elevated, late-night depressed), consistent with the literature's U-shape claim even though this project's own data cannot yet attribute it to announcements specifically (Rule FF-29 unresolved, no macro calendar held). The raw 100.9x max/min figure is a per-cell artifact of thin extreme bins (e.g. Sun 23:00, n=3) -- reported honestly, not used as the headline number.
result.per_cell_sample_thinness: Median 35 rows/cell across 1,452 populated (weekday,bin) cells -- flagged as a real limitation, not glossed over. S(t) is a first-pass estimate on recent history only, not a converged multi-year seasonal curve.
result.magnitude_ic: RAW 0.0079 (does not survive eff-n) -> DESEASONALISED -0.0252 (DOES survive eff-n: CI [-0.0403,-0.0100], excludes zero). Gap = -0.033. Deseasonalising did NOT just shrink noise toward zero -- it flipped sign and became small-but-real. Read carefully, not overclaimed: this says higher |score| correlates with a SMALLER deseasonalised forward excursion, which is the opposite of the 'magnitude prediction' thesis WARRANT#213/#216 were testing, and the magnitude is tiny (|IC|~0.025, nowhere near the published ~0.25). Not evidence FOR the magnitude-IC thesis; if anything, additional evidence against it, now on a cleaner denominator.
result.directional_ic: RAW -0.0112 (does not survive eff-n) -> DESEASONALISED -0.0100 (still does not survive eff-n). Gap = +0.0012, essentially unchanged. Seasonality was NOT materially contaminating this specific directional measurement.
result.honest_reading: Real, measured seasonal amplitude exists in this data (contradicting nothing -- it's expected). Its effect on the two specific IC numbers already on record is small: directional barely moves at all; magnitude moves more (flips sign, gains significance under eff-n) but stays tiny in absolute terms either way. So A3 was a real, previously-untested contamination source -- Rule FF-26 was correctly cautious to name it -- but on THIS data, deseasonalising does not resurrect a hidden edge; if anything it slightly strengthens the case that magnitude-IC does not hold here, on a now-cleaner measurement.

findings.momentum: Enhanced has 3 adaptive layers CalculateScoreWithWeights/Ex both completely lack: (1) a correlation discount (macdScore *= 0.80 when it agrees with a strong MTF reading -- avoids double-counting correlated signals), (2) RSI-slope confirm/diverge (+-15%/-20%), (3) price-acceleration cross-check (0.85x). All three are bar-derived (f.rsiSlope, f.priceAcceleration, mtfScore -- no live trading history needed), so per WARRANT#212's own bar-derived-vs-adaptive-live-only distinction, these ARE closeable the same way MTF was. Not yet fixed.
findings.volatility: REAL BUG, not just missing richness. Enhanced has 5 branches (normal=+15, spike>1.5=-10, elevated 1.2-1.5=-5, low-vol 0.5-0.8=-5, dead<0.5=-10). CalculateScoreWithWeights/Ex only implement 2 of the 5 (normal=+15, spike=-10) -- the other 3 conditions (elevated/low-vol/dead, which together cover a wide, commonly-hit atrRatio range) silently fall through to volScore=0 instead of the intended penalty. This means calibration systematically treats non-ideal volatility conditions as NEUTRAL when live treats them as a real penalty -- a genuine formula defect (an omitted branch), not a deliberate live-only exclusion. Clearest, most actionable fix of the 5.
findings.volume: Enhanced blends the 20-bar ratio with a 5-bar feature-derived delta (70/30), applies a body-conviction multiplier (0.6x-1.3x based on candle close position vs signal direction) and a wick-trap/wick-penalty multiplier (down to 0.45x on a wick-dominant volume spike), plus a 4th score tier (blendedVolRatio>1.1 -> +5) the calibration versions don't have at all. CalculateScoreWithWeights/Ex use only the raw 20-bar ratio, 3 tiers, no conviction/wick adjustment. Largest adaptive gap of the 5 -- all bar-derived (f.closePosition, f.upperWickRatio/lowerWickRatio, f.volumeDelta), so also bar-derived-closeable in principle, but the richest to safely replicate.
findings.session: Two independent divergences: (1) the calibrated-WR-to-score mapping uses completely different tier boundaries -- calib is 3-tier (>=0.65->10, >=0.55->5, else -5), live is 5-tier (>=0.72->10, >=0.65->6, >=0.58->2, >=0.50->-2, else -8); (2) the static pre-calibration fallback differs too -- calib's NY window is hour 12-21 scoring 5, live's is 16-21 scoring 5, and calib's 'else' is 0 vs live's -5. (3) live also has an entire day-of-week WR multiplier layer (0.75x-1.20x) calib does not have at all. All bar/calibration-state-derived, not live-only.
findings.pattern: The deepest finding: Enhanced ITSELF already has two internal modes -- when g_Calibration.isCalibrating is true, Enhanced falls back to a simple bar-local candle-body-ratio formula (deliberately, per its own comment: 'no live state contamination' from g_PatternState, which only makes sense on a live tick stream). But CalculateScoreWithWeights/Ex use a THIRD, different formula: a fresh DetectMicroPatternAt(bar) call with confidence-weighted scoring and its own bearish-type list -- matching NEITHER of Enhanced's two modes. So pattern has 3 distinct formulas in the codebase, not 2 -- the calibration-time scorers should arguably be calling Enhanced's own calibration-branch formula (the simple candle-body-ratio one) rather than a third independent implementation, since Enhanced's authors already solved 'what should this component do when calibrating' once.

FPE_ResolvePending (wired at the same cadence as SOM_ResolvePending, inside RecordComprehensiveSignal) watches subsequent price action: if it later hits the original TP, entryCreditR (the full-path R) is computed as if the trade had been left alone; if it hits the original SL, entryCreditR is the negative equivalent; after a 20-bar horizon with neither hit (same convention as WARRANT#184's historical-export timeout handling), marks to market. residualR = actualR - entryCreditR isolates what the FORCED EXIT itself contributed, separate from the entry signal's own quality. Organic TP/SL closes are correctly excluded (comment explains why: a natural TP/SL close already IS the full path by definition -- there's nothing to compare it against). Classified into a 3x2 six-cell grid (won/lost/undetermined full-path outcome x helped/hurt residual direction) per the doc's own 'Six-cell counts' evidence bar -- the doc gives no further prose beyond that phrase, so the exact cell shape is a stated, documented interpretation, not an unstated guess.

sessions.why_it_mattered_here: Every bar's outcome resolves over the next exitHorizon bars, so an observation sitting just past a split boundary was scored using price action the other side of that boundary also contains. The search then reads the resulting agreement as generalisation. That is leakage, and it flatters the very overfit checks built to catch overfitting.
sessions.five_splits_treated: A: the in-array train/holdout split at trainEnd -- 7 holdout loops plus the coordinate-ascent train/validation partition, where the purged band now belongs to NEITHER side rather than silently counting as validation. B: the fit-check's bar-range holdout. B2: the two chronological halves of that holdout, which this file's own comment already called 'independent' -- they were not, until the bars whose labels straddle the midpoint came out of the second one. C: the CSCV block boundaries, where the combinatorial partitions train on some blocks and test on the rest, so a block's first observations leak into its predecessor exactly as a holdout's leak into training; a fully-purged block now reports no estimate rather than a fabricated one. D: the global train/OOS boundary.
sessions.THE_REAL_DEFECT_FOUND: Split D. TRAIN_START reserved a flat 120 bars from the OOS window and its own comment called that 'zero leakage'. Phase 3A picks each regime's exit horizon from a candidate list whose LARGEST entry is 150 bars, and the label resolves over that horizon -- so any regime calibrated above 120 bars had its TRAINING labels resolving inside the OOS window. That is the largest split in the system, leaking into the single measurement the whole arm decision rests on, behind a comment asserting the opposite. The gap is now derived from the longest possible label plus an embargo (150 + 30) instead of being a round number, and the check asserts the clearance is positive rather than trusting the comment.
sessions.MT4_indexing_stated_because_it_is_easy_t: LOWER bar index = NEWER. A label looks FORWARD in time, so it reaches toward LOWER indices. The regime arrays are ascending by bar index, which puts training at the newer end and holdout at the older end -- so the leak runs one way only: a HOLDOUT observation's label can reach back into training bars, never the reverse. Purging is therefore one-sided, applied to the test side of every boundary. Getting this backwards would have purged the wrong side and left the leak untouched while appearing to fix it.
sessions.the_assertion_output: research_layer/check_c35_purge_embargo.py -- 23 assertions in three sets, 23 passing. (1) The rule itself, known-answer: the unpurged split must REPORT leakage and the purged one must not -- a purge checker that cannot detect the leak it was built to remove would pass everything. Also checks the degenerate ends: a zero-length label purges nothing, a label longer than the data purges all of it. (2) The research layer on real export data through afml_tools' PurgedKFold, with a negative control: the same folds WITHOUT purging must show leakage (they show 80), or the clean result above is vacuous. (3) The EA's own splits, read from shipped source: no holdout loop still starts at the unpurged boundary (0 remain), 7 start at the purged one, the purged band is excluded from validation, the fit-check and fold split are gapped, CSCV blocks are purged, and the declared label span is asserted to cover the longest exit-horizon candidate the source actually contains -- read from `horizons[]` at run time, so the two cannot drift apart silently.

sessions.THE_NUMBER: 1,309 trades. At the P3B bracket's payoff (2.5 ATR target / 1.5 ATR stop, RR 1.667), break-even sits at 37.50% and the minimum tradeable rate at 41.25%, so the edge a reported win rate has to be able to see is 3.75 percentage points. Separating that from break-even at 95/80 needs 1,309 trades. This is deliberately the SMALLEST honest floor available -- it asks only that the rate distinguish a barely-tradeable edge from break-even, nothing finer.
sessions.WHAT_THAT_MEANS_FOR_THE_CODEBASE: Every floor this codebase currently guards a rate report with -- 5, 8, 10, 15, 20, 30, and the largest at 500 -- is below it. So at EVERY guard actually in the source, a reported win rate cannot tell a barely-tradeable edge from break-even. That is precisely the question C3.2 was asking, and this is the first time the project has had an answer to it.

sessions.THE_MATHEMATICS: If r = beta(z)*s + noise, the pooled IC this project has been measuring is proportional to E[beta] -- the MEAN local slope. Sign-flipping drives E[beta] to zero however large |beta| is anywhere. The edge, in that world, lives in Var(beta), and pooled IC is structurally blind to it. Under a true null the Fisher-z of a local IC over n independent observations is N(0, 1/(n-3)), so standardising each local z by its own sqrt(n-3) gives a collection with variance exactly 1. Excess variance is local structure; the mean staying at zero is the sign flipping.
sessions.WARRANT_258_RESULT: On the BLENDED score, at horizon 1 where forward returns do not overlap and the null is exact: variance ratio 0.86 over 100 time windows (permuted control 0.77, p 0.84) and 1.34 over 50 state cells (control 0.92, p 0.058). The pooled null is a real null in this representation. The state-cell 1.34 is the only reading above 1 and does not approach this morning's own deflated bar of 3.64.
sessions.A_CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_FIRST_RESULT: The first run reported 3.26 at h=5 and 7.27 at h=21 with clean permutation controls -- which would have been a spectacular confirmation of the thesis, and was an artefact arriving at exactly the size the artefact predicts. Overlapping forward returns inflate the variance ratio by precisely the overlap factor: 3.26/5 and 7.27/21 are both BELOW 1. The permutation control could not catch it and never could -- shuffling the score destroys the serial dependence in the score, and the inflation requires BOTH series serially dependent. A control that breaks the mechanism it exists to control for is not a control. Fixed at the source by standardising on the effective sample, which is what C3.6 built this morning. Corrected readings: 0.64 at h=5, 0.30 at h=21.
sessions.WHAT_258_DOES_NOT_SAY: It tests the BLEND, and that is a hole big enough for the whole thesis. If one component carries a positive local slope in a cell and another a negative one, the blend is flat in that cell AND flat pooled -- the cancellation happens before the score exists, so a test on the score sees a null manufactured by arithmetic rather than by the market. That is forge-indicate's standing thesis and SWORD III's W-1, and it has never been measured because the export carried only the blend.
sessions.WARRANT_259_THE_INSTRUMENT_FOR_THAT: Built research_layer/component_edge_test.py: the same Var(beta) test per component instead of on their sum, plus a CANCELLATION INDEX (sum of |local component slope| over |local blend slope| per cell -- 1.0 means the blend preserves what the components carry, far above 1 means summing them is destroying it) and the per-cell component correlation SC-15 asked for. Its known-answer test is the point: a synthetic frame with a sign-flipping local slope planted in one component and another built to cancel it exactly. The instrument recovers it -- blend 0.75 (invisible), planted component 70.4 (visible), unplanted control 0.95 (no false positive), cancellation index 28.8. It can find what Manuel is describing, if it is there.
sessions.WHY_THE_UNLOCK_WAS_NOT_DONE_TODAY_AND_WH: Switching live influence on today would buy an abstain-on-everything: no calibration has run, so every cell is empty and the design's own fallback cascade fires on all of them. It would look like a change and not be one. The decisive move is instead the component-level export -- and checking the source showed it is ALREADY WRITTEN. WARRANT#213 added the six comp_* columns, WARRANT#217 added organism_class and fwd_up_10, the row writer matches the 21-column header, and ExportHistoricalScoreOutcomes is already true. sessions.A_CONSEQUENCE_FOR_THE_ARM_GATE_WORTH_ACT: If edge is selective, the survivor's realised edge is E[beta(z)*s | acted] and the whole skill is in choosing the set 'acted'. P6 arms on a POOLED ghost win rate at 0.58/0.62, which averages the tradeable subset with everything else -- the exact operation that destroys a selective edge. A system required to clear a global win rate cannot express 'I trade two percent of bars and I am right on those'. That is a checkable claim about the code and it is not in any criterion; filed here because it follows from the reframing rather than from the queue.

sessions.WARRANT_263_the_two_capture_before_the_e: Shipped in SLS(181), both written at the verdict's true convergence point where every input is already computed. (1) THE LEARNING TREND ROW, one per completed calibration, armed or not -- a stand-down is a data point about learning, not an absence of one. Carries both error rates with their sample counts and the calibration's own forecast error (it predicted a win rate from training and measured one out of sample; the gap is how wrong the forecast was). Nothing in this system wrote those three numbers anywhere before, so C6.3/C6.4's three-calibration trend could never have accumulated -- the first two would always have been lost. (2) THE FORWARD PRE-REGISTRATION, written ONCE at the moment of arming, before a single forward trade exists: declared length, sample size fixed in advance from the frequency this calibration measured, the predicted win rate with its interval, the calibration's b, and the risk layer's OWN stated drawdown budget. Every one of C7's five criteria is a claim about what was committed to BEFORE the period started -- start the clock with no registration and the period is ungradeable however well it runs, because there is nothing to have been wrong about.
sessions.the_write_once_rule_is_C7_2s_teeth: The registration refuses to overwrite an open period. That is the entire anti-optional-stopping guarantee: the target cannot be moved once the period it judges has begun. A second arming logs that it left the existing registration untouched.
sessions.WARRANT_264_the_readers: check_c6_learning_trend.py and check_c7_forward.py, both self-tested against known answers before being trusted. The trend reader tests the SEQUENCE (rank correlation with calibration order, over three or more) rather than first-versus-last, which two noisy points can satisfy by accident; it excludes rows where a rate was not measurable rather than reading them as a perfect zero, which would manufacture a falling trend out of missing data. The C7 settler enforces two things its self-tests prove it does: it REFUSES to settle before the declared end (a settler willing to score early is optional stopping wearing an analyst's coat), and per Rule FF-5 it FAILS a wildly profitable period whose win rate lands outside the predicted interval -- tested explicitly with a case built to be profitable, because a settler that cannot fail a winner has not understood the rule.
sessions.WARRANT_265_C1_3_IS_NOT_RUN_GATED_AT_ALL: The criterion's evidence is 'an automated parity test passing on EVERY BUILD', and a test that only runs during a calibration cannot pass on a build that has not run one -- so it was read as a build-time question and checked structurally. All six are used exclusively by calibration-side functions and by the parity test itself. The live path computes every shared component through its own separate code, and identity between the paths rests on a sampled numeric comparison at run time rather than on structure.

sessions.type: ANALYSIS (WARRANT#266 -- the exit-geometry expectancy sweep). Opened by Manuel asking about a claim that edge is 'losing as little as possible, winning more often, losing less frequently'.
sessions.the_claim_taken_apart: It contains a double-count. 'Winning more often' and 'losing less frequently' are the same number -- p and (1-p) are complements. E = p*W - (1-p)*L has three levers, not four. Everything measured this campaign says p is the one that will not move. W and L are EXIT decisions, not prediction decisions -- so the claim, stripped of its muddle, points exactly where Manuel independently pointed earlier the same day: timing, not direction.
sessions.the_coupling_the_claim_ignores: p, W and L cannot be chosen separately. Widen the target and W rises while p falls; tighten the stop and L falls while p falls too. A bracket slides you along a curve rather than letting you pick three numbers. So the only answerable question is whether ANY point on that curve clears zero -- which the export can answer, because it records the favourable excursion, the adverse excursion, and the bars each took, for 50,000 bars.
sessions.TWO_ARTEFACTS_FOUND_IN_MY_OWN_ANALYSIS_A: First run: SL 3.0 ranked top at +0.1625R. Its average loss was 1.05R -- a 3.0 stop losing 1.05R on average is the arithmetic saying out loud that the stop was never hit. Checked: a 3.0 ATR stop is reached in 3.4% of bars. So the winner was not a wide stop, it was NO stop, and a no-stop strategy always wins over a bounded observation window because the window removes the left tail it would have paid for. Every such geometry is now disqualified from the headline by a stop-resolution share carried on each row. SECOND artefact, found on the next pass: bars_to_mfe and bars_to_mae are times to the EXTREME, not to a threshold crossing, so using them for first-touch ordering is systematically wrong -- and worst exactly where both thresholds sit well inside their extremes, which is where the surviving best cell lands. The sweep therefore CANNOT settle which bracket is best, and says so rather than ranking anyway.
sessions.THE_FINDING_THAT_SURVIVES_BOTH: It needs no ordering assumption and no window beyond the recorded extremes: the median adverse excursion is 1.55 ATR and the stop actually in use sits at 1.5 ATR. THE STOP IS INSIDE THE NOISE. 55.9% of all bars breach it regardless of direction, while the 2.5 ATR target is reached by 30.1%. The stop is hit almost twice as often as the target. And the bracket in use scores E -0.0503R with p 0.391 against a break-even of 0.406 -- just under water, ranking 63rd of the 80 tried.
sessions.what_that_says_about_the_video_s_claim: 'Lose as little as possible' is precisely the trap here. The stop is already tight enough to be triggered by noise more often than the target is reached by signal; tightening it further lowers L and lowers p faster. The claim is not wrong about where edge can live, it is wrong that the three quantities can be improved independently.
sessions.what_would_actually_settle_it: Phase 3B already replays candidate brackets against the real price path inside the EA -- the ordering problem this analysis hit does not exist there. Having it sweep and report the expectancy curve is the honest instrument, and it is a real buildable item rather than an analysis of recorded extremes.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: No EA source touched. Research layer only. The 80 brackets tried are registered in the multiplicity ledger, because an in-sample sweep that does not pay into it makes every earlier result look better than it is.

sessions.WARRANT_259_ANSWERED_THE_LOCAL_EDGE_THES: The question standing since 2026-08-30: is the blend destroying component-level local edge before anything can measure it. Answer: no, because there is no component-level structure to destroy. Every variance ratio sits at chance -- blend 0.92 and 1.13, comp_mtf 0.90/1.15, momentum 0.93/0.86, volatility 1.03/0.80, volume 1.02/0.96, session 0.91/1.14, pattern 0.99/1.06, across both partitions. Not one component shows local slopes dispersed beyond what sampling noise explains.
sessions.the_cancellation_index_looked_damning_an: It reads 5.9: the components carry 0.195 of absolute local slope while the blend carries 0.027, so summing them destroys about 86% of it. That is what averaging six INDEPENDENT NOISE series does, not evidence of real signal being cancelled -- and the correlation measurement confirms independence rather than redundancy: median pairwise |r| 0.08, with 0-2% of pairs above 0.6. So SC-15's question is answered NO in both directions: the 'more indicators' avenue is not closed by collinearity, and the blend is not destroying a real signal. It is averaging noise, which is what noise does.
sessions.WARRANT_269_THE_C4_RECORD_AND_ITS_VERDIC: Built check_c4_record.py -- the evidence type C4 names, 'full measurement record, per class, never pooled': one row per organism class x component x horizon, with the effective sample after overlap correction, the interval deflated against the multiplicity ledger, and the flatness test C4-NEGATIVE specifies. 196 rows produced. VERDICT: INCONCLUSIVE -- and this is the important part.
sessions.why_inconclusive_is_the_honest_answer_an: NOTHING clears the deflated bar (z=3.744 at 276 registered tests) in any class, component or horizon -- so there is no C4-POSITIVE. But the deflated intervals are not inside the +/-0.02 band C4-NEGATIVE requires either, so flatness cannot be asserted. The reason is visible in the record: after the overlap correction the effective samples collapse. Class 1 at h=8 holds n_eff 2,419 and an interval of +/-0.076; the smaller structural classes (expansion n=3,423, contraction n=2,363) fall to n_eff 112-684 at longer horizons, with intervals of +/-0.3. Those intervals cannot exclude a 0.02 effect and never could.
sessions.THE_FINDING_THAT_CHANGES_THE_CAMPAIGN_S_: This campaign has been treating the null as steadily more solid. The per-class record says something different and more precise: the POOLED null is solid, and the CONDITIONAL question is not answerable on 50,000 bars of one instrument. We cannot conclude the edge is absent per organism class -- we can only conclude we cannot see one. A null on a sample this thin is not evidence of absence, and C4-NEGATIVE's own wording (n at or above the floor in EACH class) forbids claiming it. That distinction has been blurred for most of the campaign and is now measured.
sessions.and_it_was_predicted_yesterday: The resolution budget (WARRANT#267) said this data affords roughly nine distinct conditions. C4 asks for 4 classes x 7 components x 7 horizons. The record is the budget's prediction arriving in practice, on real data, one day later.
sessions.what_makes_C4_answerable: More data, not more cleverness -- and it is already scoped as W-3, the breadth extension to six pairs and five years. That multiplies the effective sample directly and is the only route to a conditional verdict. It also answers 'per market', which one instrument structurally cannot.

sessions.WARRANT_270_THE_SIGN_TEST_AND_WHY_IT_FAI: The running calibration prints an IC per component per regime, and comp_mtf came back positive in every regime it had measured: +0.05, +0.06, +0.05, +0.11, +0.14, +0.12. Six for six. No campaign test had ever asked about SIGN AGREEMENT -- every test so far asked HOW BIG, deflated it, and found nothing. 'Never large' and 'always the same direction' are different claims and the second one was untested.
sessions.the_control_is_the_whole_point: Nine regimes are not nine independent confirmations; they partition ONE price series. If comp_mtf carries a single small global bias, every partition inherits it and all the signs agree for one reason, not six. So the test runs twice: RAW (6/6 positive, p=0.031) and CONTROLLED (each regime's IC minus the sample-weighted mean, then the same sign test). Controlled: 3/6, p=1.00. Volatility behaved identically -- 6/6 raw at p=0.031, 2/6 after control. The agreement was one global bias of +0.087 re-shown six times. The eye counted six, the data had one.
sessions.why_this_matters_more_than_the_result: The raw number was publishable-looking and wrong. Had the control not been written into the same script as the test, 'MTF is positive in every single regime, p=0.03' is exactly the kind of finding that would have survived into a decision. It was built with its own refutation attached, and the refutation fired.
sessions.WARRANT_271_TEN_EVIDENCE_LINES_SILENCED_: Chasing why C3.5's purge/embargo assertion had not appeared in the live log, found it gated behind if(!g_CalibSilent) -- and the orchestrator sets g_CalibSilent=true for the entire duration of a real calibration. sessions.type: BUILD. WARRANT#273 -- C5.3's persistence fix, shipped. The one item session 54 scoped and deliberately did not attempt.
sessions.THE_DEFECT: g_Risk.peakEquity is the high-water mark the drawdown fade divides by. It is monotonic within a run, and it appeared in NEITHER SaveSystemState nor LoadSystemState. So every restart reset the floor to current equity: an EA restarted while 8% down resumed sizing as though it were at its peak, with the fade fully released at exactly the moment the fade exists for. A ratchet that resets is not a ratchet. This is a live risk defect, not only a missing criterion.
sessions.WHY_IT_WAS_DEFERRED_AND_WHY_THAT_NO_LONG: WARRANT#231 traced it and declined to fix it, for a reason worth quoting: 'touching positional FileWrite/FileRead pairs at multiple sites in lockstep -- real risk of corrupting every field written after it if the write/read counts ever drift.' That caution is correct about editing the MIDDLE of a positional record. It does not apply to appending a new LAST tail after 0xD176, which is the convention this file already uses eight times over (0xA1F0, 0xC59A, 0xCA4E, 0xD520, 0xE210, 0xD176, plus the LE/PDB/Forge/Keys3 helper pairs). Nothing already written moves; an older file ends before the marker and skips it; no version bump.
sessions.WHAT_SHIPPED: New guarded tail 0xE9A0 carrying the account number and the peak. TWO GUARDS on restore, both load-bearing. (1) The account number is stored with the mark and checked -- restoring another account's peak would invent a drawdown that never happened and throttle sizing on a healthy account. (2) The restore takes MathMax(saved, current equity) -- a high-water mark must never come back LOWER than where the account actually stands, which is what a bare assignment does after the account grows while the EA is off. Both directions of error are silent and both are wrong.
sessions.THE_INSTRUMENT_IS_WORTH_MORE_THAN_THE_FI: Built check_c53_ratchet.py, which turns WARRANT#231's stated fear into a test that runs. It compares the FULL ORDERED FIELD STREAM of SaveSystemState against LoadSystemState, position for position, markers included -- because what matters for positional corruption is not section attribution but whether byte n on write is byte n on read. Result: 176 fields written, 176 read, agreeing at every position. All five helper tail pairs (LE/PDB/Forge SR/Forge Champion/Keys3) checked separately and symmetric. The persistence layer as a whole is now verified, which it never was.
sessions.A_FALSE_POSITIVE_I_CAUGHT_ON_MYSELF: The checker's first version compared fields PER SECTION MARKER and reported 0xCA4E as drift -- 12 written, 2 read. That was the checker being wrong, not the code: the write side appends the FIX25 fields straight after the candle-weights block with no marker of their own, while the read side takes them in a separate FileIsEnding guard outside the marker's braces. The fields are read. Rewrote it to the stream comparison rather than shipping the finding. A checker that reports a false drift on a correct file is worse than no checker, because the next real drift arrives into a report nobody believes.
sessions.THE_SELF_TEST_RE_PLANTS_THE_FAULT: 5/5 self-tests, including deleting a field from a synthetic read side every run and asserting the comparison reports it, plus an unguarded peakEquity assignment that must be caught. A symmetry checker that cannot detect asymmetry converts an unexamined risk into a false assurance.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: Append-only tail; the stream test proves nothing before it moved. The running calibration is unaffected -- it executes the pre-edit code from memory and its own artefacts stay clean.

sessions.type: THE FIRST RESULT THAT EVER CLEARED THE DEFLATED BAR -- and the honest limit on it. WARRANT#274 (moment profiles) and WARRANT#275 (six adversarial attacks). Prompted entirely by Manuel's correction mid-session.
sessions.MANUELS_CORRECTION_WAS_A_DEFECT_IN_THE_I: He said: 'the no edge found logs are problematic, the perspective is still rock -- edges are moment to moment, not a single value.' He was right, and it was not a framing complaint. EVERY test this campaign has run collapses a period into ONE SCALAR: an IC, a variance ratio, a sign count. If an edge lives in a minority of moments and is absent or inverted in the rest, a pooled IC of ~0.00 is EXACTLY what it produces. Averaging was not a neutral summary; it was the specific operation destroying the thing being looked for. 'No edge found' was never a conclusion these instruments were entitled to draw.
sessions.WHAT_WAS_BUILT: moment_edge_profile.py -- IC as a PROFILE across buckets of four properties OF THE BAR rather than of a period: AGREEMENT (how many of six components point the way the blend does -- Manuel's own framing, made measurable), CONVICTION (|score|), PERSISTENCE (consecutive prior bars holding the same score sign), DISPERSION (spread across components). The hypothesis is the SHAPE, not the best bucket: monotone rise, or concentration in an extreme bucket. Two named shapes, both registered, both paid for in the deflation. Picking the best of six buckets after looking is still not done anywhere.
sessions.THE_INSTRUMENT_CAUGHT_ITSELF_TWICE: First, the self-test planted an edge in the top bucket only -- exactly the shape 'moment to moment' describes -- and the monotonicity test MISSED it (rho +0.20, p 0.71), because the ranks of five flat buckets are noise that swamps one correctly placed extreme. Added the extreme-contrast test, which found it at z +21.2. Second, that contrast tested only the TOP bucket, and the real data put its structure in the BOTTOM one. A one-sided test would have walked straight past the only thing in the table. Both ends now tested, all three shapes deflated.
sessions.THE_FINDING: PERSISTENCE, lowest bucket -- bars at or within 4 bars of a score sign flip, 17.8% of all bars. IC -0.20 at h=1, -0.31 at h=3, -0.33 at h=5, against ~0.00 in every other bucket. Contrast z = -19.1, -17.6, -14.7 against a deflated bar of 3.95. The sign is INVERTED: in the moments just after the score flips, the score predicts the opposite of what it says.

SIX_ATTACKS_ALL_SURVIVED.conviction confound: REJECTED, and the opposite is true -- the effect STRENGTHENS with conviction: band 0 -0.175, band 1 -0.262, band 2 -0.411, band 3 -0.578, while non-flip bars sit at ~0.00 in every band. The more confident the score is at a flip moment, the more wrong it is.
SIX_ATTACKS_ALL_SURVIVED.time split: SURVIVES. Older half -0.315, newer half -0.289 at h=3; same sign, both halves clearing the bar independently.
SIX_ATTACKS_ALL_SURVIVED.direction: present in both, stronger on sells (-0.22 vs -0.11 at h=3).
SIX_ATTACKS_ALL_SURVIVED.overlap: the effect is STRONGEST at h=1 where there is no overlap at all, which runs opposite to an overlap artefact.
SIX_ATTACKS_ALL_SURVIVED.measure: an apparent sign reversal against r_continuous turned out to be a convention difference -- direction is ALWAYS sign(score) (checked: share 1.000), so that IC mixes magnitude with sign. The economic statement resolves it cleanly and agrees: mean of sign(score) x forward return is negative at every horizon on flip bars and positive on the rest.
SIX_ATTACKS_ALL_SURVIVED.mechanical reversion: PARTIAL. Removing the component of the score explained by the preceding bar's return takes IC from -0.312 to -0.238 -- about a quarter of it. Not separable further with this export; needs tick data. Stated as the biggest single reason not to act.

sessions.THE_MECHANISM_IS_THE_WIN_RATE_ALONE_AND_: E = p*W - (1-p)*L decomposes as: flip bars p=0.312, W=+1.304, L=0.946 -> E=-0.2432R. Non-flip p=0.411, W=+1.435, L=0.942 -> E=+0.0357R. The payoff geometry is essentially IDENTICAL between the two groups; the entire difference is the hit rate. That is precisely the 'winning more often, losing less frequently' framing Manuel brought back from the video, arriving from the data rather than from the claim.
sessions.AND_THE_LIMIT_THAT_MATTERS_MORE_THAN_THE: Across ALL bars the rule looks transformative: declining flip moments takes pooled expectancy from -0.0140R to +0.0357R, which over 900 trades is +32R against -12.6R. That number does NOT apply, because the system does not trade all bars. At the threshold Phase 1 actually chose this run (40), flip bars fall from 17.8% of all bars to 2.7% of TRADED bars -- the score threshold is already filtering most flip moments implicitly. Declining the remainder improves expectancy by +0.0153R and leaves it NEGATIVE (-0.0298 -> -0.0145). Out of sample it is worse: older half delta +0.0318, newer half +0.0031, essentially nothing.
sessions.so_what_is_actually_true: The moment-level effect is real, large, and statistically unambiguous at bar level. It does not rescue the system, because the operating threshold has already absorbed most of it. Those 2.7% remain genuinely toxic -- 16.9% win rate against 38.9% -- so declining them is a free improvement, just a small one. Anyone reading only the first half of this entry would be misled, which is why both halves are in it.
sessions.WHAT_THIS_CHANGES_ABOUT_THE_CAMPAIGN: Two things. (1) The lens was wrong and is now fixed -- there is a working instrument for moment-level structure, with planted-edge self-tests proving it can see what pooled tests cannot. (2) Every prior 'no edge' statement in this ledger needs reading as 'not detectable under the partitions tried', and the partitions were all windows imposed from outside. This one asked what the MOMENT looked like and immediately found something at z=-19. That is a strong argument that the remaining search should be over moment descriptions, not over more periods or more cells.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: Analysis only, read-only over the export. Nothing was wired into the EA: acting on an in-sample-selected rule before the pre-registered forward period is exactly what FF-5 forbids, and the mechanical-reversion attack is only partially answered.

sessions.type: THE OPERATIONAL BLOCKER, FOUND BY THE RUN ITSELF. WARRANT#276. This is the most consequential finding of the campaign and it did not come from any instrument I built -- it came from letting the EA finish a calibration and reading what it said.
sessions.WHAT_THE_RUN_REPORTED: Phase 3B ended 0 of 9 regimes validated -- the standing outcome. The all-regularized fallback then set every regime threshold to 'the P1 baseline 70'. Immediately after, the EA's own portal-audit compared the calibration scorer against the live scorer at that threshold over 500 sampled bars: linear qualifies 110, ENHANCED QUALIFIES 0, agreement 0.0%.
THE_CHAIN_TRACED_AND_VERIFIED: Phase 1's threshold grid measured thr 40 (41.2% WR, 97 trades) into a LOCAL variable, baselineThreshold.
That local is never assigned to g_BaseThreshold. g_BaseThreshold is a hardcoded 70.0 set at init and touched only by an adaptive raise path.

The all-regularized fallback sets all nine g_RegimeOptimalThresholds to MathMax(g_BaseThreshold, 50.0) = 70, while its own comment calls this 'the P1 baseline'. It is not P1's baseline; it is a constant P1 never writes to.
The live scorer's |score| over 50,000 exported bars has a MAXIMUM of 52.07 -- and 6.54% of all bars sit at EXACTLY 52.0700, so this is a saturation ceiling, not a thin tail.
70 > 52.07. The threshold is not strict, it is unreachable. DEFAULT_REGIME_THRESHOLD is 55.0, also above the ceiling -- even the safe-default path cannot qualify a bar.
sessions.WHAT_IS_VERIFIED_AND_WHAT_IS_NOT: VERIFIED: the hardcoded constant, the missing assignment, the fallback arithmetic, the 52.07 ceiling with its 6.54% saturation mass, and the EA's own audit reporting 0 of 500 qualifying bars at the configured thresholds. NOT FULLY TRACED: that every live entry path gates solely on |enhanced score| >= g_RegimeOptimalThresholds -- this is a 63,000-line file with several threshold variables (g_CurrentThreshold, Phase 5 adjustments, DEFAULT_REGIME_THRESHOLD) and I did not walk all of them. So the claim made is 'entry is blocked wherever that gate applies, and the EA's own audit says zero bars qualify', NOT the stronger 'it is proven no trade can ever open'. The distinction is kept because the stronger claim is the one worth being wrong about.
sessions.WHY_THIS_MATTERS_MORE_THAN_ANY_EDGE_RESU: A system that cannot open a trade is indistinguishable from a system that has chosen not to. The project's standing outcome has always been STAND DOWN, and this campaign has spent sixty sessions asking whether the edge is real. If entry has been structurally impossible, then the stand-downs were never a verdict about edge at all. That does not make the null wrong -- the bar-level expectancy work stands on exported scores, not on trades -- but it does mean the LIVE record has been measuring a different thing than anyone thought.
sessions.AND_IT_HAS_BEEN_SAYING_SO: The portal-audit was shipped 2026-08-05 and fires on every completed calibration. It printed CONFIRMED and 'This is the main thing to fix' today, and presumably on every run before. The information was not missing; it was unread. That is the same shape as WARRANT#271's ten silenced lines and WARRANT#272's parity test that never ran, except worse: this one was not silenced at all.
sessions.WHAT_SHIPPED_AND_WHAT_DELIBERATELY_DID_N: Added a REACHABILITY check that samples the live scorer's actual maximum and compares it against every regime threshold, emitting an explicit UNREACHABLE verdict plus a human line when the lowest threshold exceeds the highest achievable score, and a DESYNC line when P1's measured value differs from g_BaseThreshold by more than 5. Published g_P1MeasuredThreshold so the desync is visible rather than inferred. THE THRESHOLD WAS NOT LOWERED. At a reachable threshold of 40 the measured bar-level expectancy is -0.0298R; 'fixing' the number would convert a silent halt into a losing system. The defect being fixed here is the SILENCE, not the number.
sessions.THE_OTHER_THING_THE_RUN_SAID: P3B's own synthesis: 8 of 8 powered regimes carry measured non-stationary substrate structure -- sign flips or |t| past 3.0 -- and it concluded in its own words 'Not an absent signal; a moving target. A single fixed-window linear search cannot capture this by design, not evidence the signal is absent.' That is the EA arriving independently, by a completely different measurement path, at both Manuel's reframing and WARRANT#274's flip finding from the same afternoon. Three independent routes to the same conclusion is the strongest thing this campaign has.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: The guard is diagnostic: it samples scores and logs. It sets no threshold, opens no trade, and changes no weight. Compiled 0 errors 0 warnings, deployed byte-identical to all four locations. It takes effect on the next attach; this run's remaining phases are untouched.

sessions.type: ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED, and my own session-61 claim RETRACTED. WARRANT#278 (the score scale) and WARRANT#279 (an armed order path documented as disabled). Two subagents used, both read-only; one found the root cause, the other proved me wrong.
sessions.THE_ROOT_CAUSE_OF_THE_52_07_CEILING: 52.0710059... = 100 x (88/169). CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore ends with a normaliser -- _refMax = 42*wM + 25*wMo + 18*wV + 14*wVo + 10*wS + 22*wP + 20 + 18, which is exactly 169.0 at unit weights, then _norm = totalScore * (88.0/_refMax). It was written to map a raw score that its own comment says 'routinely reaches 250-350 under alignment' onto 0..100. But totalScore is hard-clamped to +/-100 FOUR times upstream of it: at 18207, at 18290 (the binding one on the export path), inside GetPatternAdjustedScore, and inside ApplyProbabilityIntelligence. The normaliser was dividing an already-flattened number, so the achievable range was +/-52.071, never +/-100.
sessions.the_comment_that_makes_it_unmistakable: The normaliser's own note says it was added because 'raw score routinely reaches 250-350 under alignment while the old saturation knee sat at 80 -- so the top 3 aligned components already pinned the score to ~100, destroying all resolution between a decent and an excellent setup.' The author diagnosed the pathology correctly and added the cure, but left the clamps above it. The defect was not fixed; it was rescaled. p95 = p99 = p99.9 = p100 = 52.07, and 6.54% of all bars sit on that single value carrying no ordering information at all.
sessions.what_it_silently_broke: Score bins 53..100 were permanently empty, so EVERY threshold expressed on the nominal 0..100 scale was unreachable: the all-regularized fallback's 70, and DetermineOptimalThreshold's uncalibrated floor of 60 -- two independent sources of the same impossibility. The soft-knee above |92| and the final +/-100 clamp were unreachable dead code. And the top 6.5% of bars, the ones any threshold selects first, were a single repeated number.
sessions.THE_FIX: The four pre-normalisation clamps are RAISED to a named SCORE_PRECLAMP_LIMIT of 400 -- above the observed raw range -- so they act as the safety rails they were meant to be instead of a binding constraint, and the normaliser plus its soft-knee do the range mapping exactly as documented. Raw 100 -> 52, raw 169 -> 88 (the stated target), raw 250+ compressed toward 100 by the knee that finally becomes live. Added an UNREACHABLE assertion to DetermineOptimalThreshold so a floor above the observed distribution says so instead of silently selecting nothing. NO THRESHOLD VALUE WAS CHANGED: making the scale correct is what makes the existing thresholds mean what they say, and picking a number is a separate decision that belongs to the account owner and should be made against a re-exported distribution.
sessions.I_WAS_WRONG_IN_SESSION_61_AND_THIS_IS_TH: Session 61 said the system 'has not been able to open a trade' and that every STAND DOWN may have been reporting structurally impossible entry. A second subagent traced every live order path and that claim is FALSE. A live entry can occur three ways: (1) TryPlaceSignAgnosticBracket places real stop orders with NO unified-score threshold check of any kind, and it is armed by default; (2) ExecuteRangeTradeIfValid likewise has no score gate; (3) the main gate's threshold is not a fixed 70 -- roughly twenty downstream adjusters plus a CEO relax bounded at -8 and an ATR-ratio floor of 0.85 can pull the effective bar to about 42.9, which 52.07 clears. A fourth gate compares (score+100)/2, so 52.07 becomes 76.04 against a threshold clamped to [58,85], and passes comfortably.
sessions.why_I_got_it_wrong_and_what_to_carry_for: I generalised from ONE instrument -- the portal-audit's 'enhanced qualifies 0 of 500' -- to a claim about the whole system. That audit compares raw |score| against the UNADJUSTED array value and knows nothing about the adjusters or the two bypass paths. I even wrote in session 61 that I had not traced every entry path and was keeping the weaker claim; then the summary sentence made the strong one anyway. The verified facts stand (the constant, the missing assignment, the ceiling, the audit's own numbers); the conclusion drawn from them did not.
sessions.WARRANT_279_AN_ARMED_ORDER_PATH_DOCUMENT: EnableSignAgnosticEntries has been TRUE since WARRANT#27, while three separate comments still said 'default false' and one said the calls are 'no-ops unless explicitly turned on'. This is the path that places orders WITHOUT consulting the unified score or any threshold, so a stale 'it is off' comment on it is the most expensive kind of stale comment in the file. Comments corrected to state the truth; the behaviour was NOT changed, because WARRANT#27 enabled it deliberately and silently reversing that would be a trading decision wearing a documentation fix.
sessions.AND_A_FINDING_I_MUST_WITHDRAW: Session 60's threshold-band table showed expectancy falling monotonically as |score| rises, which read as 'conviction is anti-predictive'. That was measured on a scale whose top band is 100% clamped blob -- 76% of bars above threshold 50 sit on the single pinned value. The out-of-sample split already disagreed with itself there (the older half reversed at 52+). The relationship is NOT evaluable until the scale fix is live and the export is regenerated. The flip-moment finding (WARRANT#275) is unaffected: it conditions on sign persistence, not on score magnitude, and its strongest horizon has no clamped mass in it.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: The scale fix is a material change to live gating on a system that CAN trade -- that is the point of the retraction above. It is shipped because the prior state is provably broken (dead code, empty bins, a defeated normaliser, two unreachable thresholds), on a demo account, under Manuel's explicit instruction to fix problems at their roots. It must be verified against a regenerated export on the next attach before anything is concluded from it. Compiled 0 errors 0 warnings twice, deployed byte-identical to all four locations. The running calibration is untouched -- it executes pre-edit code from memory.

sessions.WARRANT_277_THE_C2_2_AUDITOR: C2.2 asks for zero sequence gaps in a full run, evidence 'a block sequence audit', and no such audit existed. Built one. The point is not formatting: the EA numbers its log blocks from a counter, so if a block is composed and never emitted -- an early return between open and emit, a branch that drops it -- the counter still advances and the log shows a GAP. A gap is therefore direct evidence that the EA took a decision path whose reasoning was never recorded, which is the exact failure C2 exists to forbid, and it is invisible unless someone counts. This cannot be checked against source: whether every composed block reaches its emit is a property of which branches actually ran. Current state on the live run: 11 blocks, zero gaps, zero duplicates, all on the shipped build -- CLEAN, and deliberately NOT awarded, because the criterion says 'a full run' and a prefix is not one.
sessions.WARRANT_281_VERIFYING_MY_OWN_BIGGEST_CHA: WARRANT#278 edited four clamps on the LIVE scoring path on the strength of an arithmetic argument (100 x 88/169 = 52.071). That is a belief, not a measurement. Built check_c278_scale.py, which turns the claim into four falsifiable predictions about a regenerated export: the maximum must exceed the old ceiling, the 6.54% saturation mass must be gone, p95/p99/p100 must separate, and no new single value may hold an implausible share. Ran it against the CURRENT pre-fix export and it correctly returned NOT CONFIRMED on all three counts -- so the instrument can fail, which is the only thing that makes a later pass worth anything. Its self-tests judge a broken scale, a fixed scale, and a fix that escapes one ceiling only to re-saturate at another.
sessions.the_rule_it_states_in_its_own_output: A failure here is a revert-or-diagnose result, not one to explain away: the clamp argument was arithmetic, so if the export still tops out at 52.07 the arithmetic missed a site -- the market cannot be blamed for it.
sessions.STATIC_COMPLETENESS_CHECK_ON_THE_FIX: Verified no residual +/-100 clamp on totalScore or adjustedScore survives anywhere between CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore's opening brace and the normaliser, and that the final +/-100 clamp correctly sits AFTER it, where it belongs. A first attempt at this check was vacuous -- the line-range grep matched the WARRANT#278 comment block rather than the code, giving an empty span and a meaningless pass. Caught and redone against the actual statement.
sessions.C3_1_SCOPED_PROPERLY_FOR_THE_FIRST_TIME: The rate linter said 24 of 118 rate-reporting sites carry a realised net b. It counted the failures but never NAMED them, so nobody could tell a site where the local payoff is in scope from one where adding it would mean appending a GLOBAL net b beside a LOCAL rate -- which would look compliant and be wrong, the exact failure mode this campaign keeps finding. Made the linter list them, then asked where they live: ZERO are in the human-facing layer, all 94 are machine/TLog lines. The human layer is structurally exempt, because the Layer-2 rule forbids numbers outright so it cannot report a rate at all. C3.1's remaining work is therefore 94 analyst-layer format strings, it does not touch what Manuel reads, and it is a bounded mechanical pass rather than a design problem.
sessions.and_a_temptation_declined: Several 'absent' sites visibly contain P&L, and loosening the detector to accept a cumulative P&L would have moved the count sharply toward compliance in one edit. It was left strict: a cumulative P&L is not a per-trade payoff, and a rate beside a running total still does not tell you whether the rate is worth anything. Inflating a compliance number is the dangerous direction.

sessions.THE_CORRUPTION_I_CAUSED_AND_HOW_IT_WAS_C: The first attempt spliced the file using a global s.index() for the block's end anchor. That anchor -- '_ccaRaw[0] = MathAbs(mtfScore);' -- also appears in an EARLIER function, so the end index landed BEFORE the start index and the splice deleted roughly 629 KB of the file. The compiler returned 191 errors beginning at line 7878, thousands of lines above the intended edit, which is what made it obvious rather than subtle. sessions.the_lesson_is_specific_not_general: The rule that would have prevented it: an edit bounded by two anchors must be bounded WITHIN the enclosing function, found by brace matching, never by a global search for a string that occurs more than once in a 63,000-line file. The second attempt extracted the 56,734-byte function body first, asserted each anchor occurred exactly once INSIDE it, asserted start < end, and spliced only that region. That is the version that shipped.

sessions.THE_CHECKER_WAS_LOOKING_FOR_THE_WRONG_FU: check_c13_parity.py's canonical map named CalculatePatternScore as the pattern component's shared implementation. It is not: that function is defined once and called exactly once, by a telemetry assignment, and sits on neither scoring path. The real canonical is PATTERN233_Score, which WARRANT#233 extracted for exactly this purpose -- and the LIVE scorer already calls it at both branch ends while calibration calls it too. Pattern has been structurally SHARED for some time and this checker had been reporting it DIVERGED against a name that was never the shared one.
sessions.AND_THEN_IT_WAS_STILL_WRONG_FOR_A_SECOND: Correcting the name did not fix it -- pattern still reported DIVERGED. Printing the resolved callers showed the owner of its call site was a function named 'if'. The function-index regex matches `else if(cond) {` as a definition with type='else' and name='if', inserting a phantom function into the index; every call site after such a line is then attributed to the phantom rather than to the real enclosing function. Pattern's call sits after an `else if` inside the live scorer, so it was mis-owned. MTF and momentum escaped only because no shallow-indent `else if` happened to precede THEIR call sites -- so this checker was returning correct answers there for the wrong reason, which is not the same as working. Control-flow keywords are now excluded from both the type and the name position.
sessions.the_pattern_this_keeps_making: Two separate defects in one instrument, both of which made the system look WORSE than it was, found only by reading the source rather than trusting the verdict. sessions.WARRANT_286_VOLUME_ROUTED: The parity test measured volume at 0 mismatches over 200 bars. Worth being precise about what the zero proves: the helper recomputes the 5-bar volume delta and the full candle geometry (close position, body ratio, both wick ratios) directly from indicators, where the inline block read them off the precomputed feature struct. The zero is the evidence those two routes agree; it was not assumed. All six intermediates were checked for later readers before removal -- none had any.
sessions.A_DOCUMENTED_ASYMMETRY_KEPT_VISIBLE: The live pattern branch applies a micro-pattern overlay on top of the shared formula when a strong live pattern is active; calibration cannot, because it scans bars out of order and that state is a sequential live indicator. sessions.type: WARRANT#288 -- the C3.2 instrument was over-reporting compliance by 30 sites. No criterion earned; a number corrected downward.
sessions.THE_DEFECT: The floor-guard check was a pure proximity heuristic: bool(GUARD_PATTERN.search(window)), true if ANY comparison against ANY number appeared anywhere near the call. A loop bound, an array index, an unrelated >= 0, an hour-of-day test -- every one of them counted as a sample-size guard. It reported 112 of 118 rate-reporting sites floor-gated.
sessions.THE_CORRECTION: A real floor guard tests the sample count THAT THIS CALL REPORTS. The check now requires the guarded variable to also appear in the call's own argument list, in either comparison order. Result: 82 of 118, not 112. Thirty sites were being credited for a numeric comparison that had nothing to do with the rate beside it.
sessions.the_direction_matters: This moved the number DOWN. An instrument that over-reports compliance is the dangerous kind, and C3.2 was never claimed on the inflated figure, so nothing has to be retracted -- but had 118/118 been reached by fixing the six sites the old check named, the criterion would have been awarded on an instrument that could not see thirty of its own failures.
sessions.WHAT_IT_STILL_CANNOT_DO_STATED_PLAINLY: It cannot tell a floor of 5 from a floor of 1000, and a guard could gate on the correct variable with a meaningless bound and still pass. It removes the claims that were never checkable at all; it does not verify that the floors are adequate. Recorded as a tightened heuristic, not as a verifier, and the printed label was changed from 'heuristic proximity check' to what it now actually does.
sessions.the_six_sites_reconsidered: The old check named six ungated sites. sessions.type: C6.2 EARNED. WARRANT#289 -- the fifth instance of a report that existed and had never once been written down.
sessions.WHY_ALWAYS_TOGETHER_IS_THE_WHOLE_CRITERI: Type I is executing a signal that loses; Type II is rejecting one that would have won. Reported alone, each drives the correction that makes the other worse -- a Type I rate on its own argues for a stricter filter, a Type II rate on its own argues for a looser one, and a system tuned on either in isolation oscillates between them forever. The requirement is not that both are computed. It is that neither is ever reported without its opposite in the same call.
sessions.THE_DEFECT: LogTypeIAndTypeIIReport has existed since WARRANT#239 and was PrintFormat-only, so it reached the terminal and vanished. A grep across every live log this project retains -- the current one, the pre-SLS(181) archive, and today's completed run 1 -- found ZERO occurrences of 'TYPE-I/II'. C6.2's stated evidence is the RUN SUMMARY, and the report had never once landed in one. Routed through TLog for file-write parity, both rates kept in a single call.
sessions.the_pattern_is_the_finding: Fifth instance today of the same shape after WARRANT#182, #200, #202 and #271: a correct diagnostic that only reached Print, or was gated off, and therefore reported on nothing. Four of the five were found by asking 'has this ever actually appeared in a log?' rather than by reading the code that produces it.
sessions.THE_CHECKER: check_c62_type_pair.py extracts every logging call by paren matching and asserts no call mentions one type without the other, that at least one paired report uses a permanent emitter rather than Print, and that the trend row carries both RATES and both COUNTS -- the counts being what lets a reader tell a real rate from a placeholder. Self-tests plant a one-sided call in each direction and require both to be caught.
sessions.WHAT_THE_PASS_DOES_NOT_MEAN: The values are still -1.0, the project's sentinel for 'no marginal fill or near-miss has resolved yet'. The reporting discipline is correct while the measurement is empty. sessions.C3_2_CANNOT_BE_CLOSED_BY_ADDING_GUARDS: I was about to add floor guards at 36 sites. rate_floor.py stopped it: the DERIVED floor is 1,309 trades, and at every floor this codebase actually uses -- 5, 8, 10, 15, 20, 30, even 500 -- the 95% interval around the minimum tradeable rate cannot separate it from break-even. Adding `n >= 20` guards would have satisfied the linter while leaving the defect entirely intact: rates reported on samples that cannot distinguish a tradeable edge from nothing. That is compliance theatre, and it would have converted an honest NOT MET into a dishonest MET.
sessions.THE_THREE_ARE_ONE_FINDING: C3.1: at 85 of 94 sites the payoff is not computed where the rate is, so it cannot be printed. C3.2: the floor that would make a reported rate meaningful is ~1,309 and nothing in the system reaches it. C3.7: 629 registered tests have already searched every bar of the only export, so no untouched segment exists. Three criteria, three different evidence types, one underlying fact -- THE SYSTEM REPORTS NUMBERS IT DOES NOT HAVE THE SAMPLE TO SUPPORT. None of them is a tidy-up pass. All three are answered by more data, not by more code.
sessions.THE_NUMBER_MANUEL_SHOULD_SEE: His own framing has been 10-plus trades a day for 90 days -- roughly 900 trades -- as the horizon over which a small mathematical advantage compounds into something real. The floor required to tell a barely-tradeable win rate apart from break-even at 95% confidence is 1,309 TRADES. So 900 does not reach it, for a SINGLE pooled rate, let alone per regime or per organism class. That does not make the plan wrong -- compounding a real edge over 900 trades still pays -- but it does mean the 90-day run cannot by itself PROVE the edge was real. Proving and profiting need different sample sizes, and this campaign has been asking for the first while the plan was sized for the second.

sessions.type: THE NULL MODEL THIS CAMPAIGN NEVER HAD. WARRANT#297 (Heston state) and WARRANT#298 (barrier geometry). Prompted by Manuel asking about Heston, Black-Scholes and the Greeks -- and the useful part turned out not to be any Greek.
sessions.WHAT_THE_OPTIONS_FRAMING_ACTUALLY_GAVE_U: Not delta, gamma or zomma -- the system holds no options, so there is no value function to differentiate and those have no referent here. What it gave us is a REFRAME OF THE OBJECTIVE. The system does not predict a return; it opens a bracket and the outcome is decided by which barrier is touched first, take-profit at 2.5 ATR or stop at 1.5 ATR. That is a FIRST-PASSAGE problem, and first-passage has a null: a driftless walk hits +a before -b with probability b/(a+b). Every edge test in this campaign has measured rank correlation with forward return, which is a different quantity from the one the system is actually paid on.
sessions.THE_FINDING: Calibrated null win rate 0.4212. Observed 0.3951. The system's entries win LESS OFTEN than a coin flipped through the same bracket, by 2.6 points, and the null lies outside the 95% interval on the effective sample. The implied drift is -0.0127 ATR per bar: the score is selecting moments that move AGAINST the position it takes.
sessions.and_the_part_that_is_stronger_than_the_a: The gap widens monotonically with conviction across the first five bands: -0.016, -0.021, -0.022, -0.034, -0.042. Six bands, all on the same side of the null, ordered. The aggregate test is marginal; six ordered bands is not what noise looks like. This is the same fact as session 64's conviction inversion, now measured against a proper null instead of against zero.
sessions.what_it_reframes: Fourteen sessions of null edge results were not a failure to find something that should have been there. Against this null they are the expected outcome -- and worse, the sign is negative. C4's INCONCLUSIVE verdict, the flat moment profiles, the flat Heston states: all consistent with a system whose entry selection is actively counter-productive rather than merely uninformative.
sessions.THREE_WRONG_NULLS_CAUGHT_BEFORE_REPORTIN: This result took three attempts and each wrong version was caught by its own check. (1) b/(a+b) = 0.375 is exact only for infinitesimal steps; the self-test simulated unit steps and got 0.407, a 3-point error larger than every effect this campaign hunts. (2) Estimating the step by inverting mean MFE gave 0.470 ATR and a null of 0.4591 -- but that null left 41.2% of paths unresolved against the data's actual 14.5%, so it was a null for a different dataset. Caught by validating against the export's own resolved flag. (3) The implied drift inverted the CONTINUOUS null and reported +0.021 ATR/bar while the aggregate, correctly inverted, was negative -- two numbers in one table disagreeing about the sign of the same quantity. Final version calibrates the step until the null reproduces the observed resolution rate, and asserts the match rather than assuming it.
sessions.HESTON_WARRANT_297: Estimated kappa 0.131 (variance half-life 5.3 bars), theta 7.8e-8 (long-run vol 0.028% per bar), and a leverage proxy of -0.021. The FELLER CONDITION IS VIOLATED: 2*kappa*theta - xi^2 is negative, meaning this series' variance is more erratic than any well-posed Heston process with these parameters can support. The four variance-state moment conditions -- level, innovation, gap from the long-run mean, leverage -- all returned flat. Its own self-test forced three corrections: a fixture that violated Feller by seven orders of magnitude, a theta estimator that exploded when kappa collapsed under window overlap, and a rho estimator that recovered +0.00 against a simulated -0.40 because a 20-bar window dilutes the correlation by exactly 1/20. The vol-of-vol claim was WITHDRAWN rather than tuned: no Feller-valid xi is separable from sampling noise at this window, and raising kappa*theta until the test passed would have been choosing a fixture for the answer it gives.
sessions.WHAT_CANNOT_BE_DONE_AND_WAS_NOT_PRETENDE: Dealer gamma positioning, implied risk-neutral distributions via Breeden-Litzenberger, and vanna/charm flows around the NY cut are all real and all need an option chain MT4 does not carry. They are named as unavailable rather than approximated.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: Analysis only. No EA change. Two research agents dispatched on validation-under-tiny-samples and on microstructure measures computable from tick volume; their findings are not yet in and nothing here depends on them.

sessions.and_run_2_corroborates_the_breakeven_fin: 40.0% win rate producing -0.39R per trade is only arithmetically possible if the realised payoff is far below the 2.5:1 the display assumes. The run contradicted its own headline without anyone needing to compute anything.
sessions.WARRANT_299_THE_NUMBER_THE_OPERATOR_READ: A commissioned research pass returned, and its first recommendation was to check the break-even win rate before building anything else. It was right. The system prints 'breakeven is 28.6% WR (RR 2.5:1)' beside its verdict. That 2.5 is g_P6_AvgRR, which falls back to 2.5 whenever the ghost ledger yields no wins or no losses -- and 2.5 is ALSO that variable's initialiser, so a defaulted value has been indistinguishable from a measured one everywhere downstream.
sessions.the_size_of_the_error: breakeven = 1/(1+RR). At the printed RR of 2.5 that is 28.6%. Run 1 reported a profit factor of 0.39 over three ghost trades, which for one win and two losses implies a realised RR near 0.78 and a breakeven near 56%. The bar-level export says the same thing from a completely different direction: average win 1.417R against average loss 0.943R is a realised reward:risk of 1.50 and a breakeven of 40.0%, against a measured win rate of 39.5%. Read against 28.6% the system looks comfortably clear of break-even. Read against its own realised payoff it is AT or BELOW it. The error runs in the direction that makes a losing configuration look passable.
sessions.what_was_fixed_and_what_deliberately_was: The fallback itself is reasonable -- something must be reported when there is nothing to measure. What was wrong is presenting it as a measurement. g_P6_RRMeasured now records whether the reward:risk was actually observed, Phase 6 logs which of the two happened with the win and loss counts behind it, and the stand-down line appends 'ASSUMED -- reward:risk was not measurable this run' when the number is a default. No threshold and no fallback value was changed.

THE_RESEARCH_RETURN_ITSELF.cost_scaling: Cost as a fraction of the move falls only as 1/sqrt(holding bars): at spread/ATR 0.6 that is 60% at one bar, 30% at four, 20% at nine, 10% at thirty-six. No configuration of component weights fixes a one-bar horizon. This is the highest-leverage lever available and it is not a statistical one.
THE_RESEARCH_RETURN_ITSELF.the_45_point_gap_is_too_large_for_ordina: E[max of K standard normals] is about sqrt(2 ln K), so at a per-regime SE of 3.5pp, selection-on-noise explains at most 15-18pp of optimism even at a million candidates. The observed fitted-to-resampled gap is 45pp and the resampled rate of 25% is BELOW chance. That combination points to either badly understated standard errors from dependent overlapping trades, or weights that are actively anti-correlated with the resample -- the signature of fitting a moving target. Those two diagnoses have opposite remedies and the ambiguity should be resolved before any shrinkage machinery is built.
THE_RESEARCH_RETURN_ITSELF.hierarchical_shrinkage_has_a_trap_here: A correctly specified hierarchical model would discard 55-80% of the per-regime differences the weight search optimises against. But with only NINE groups the between-group variance -- which sets the shrinkage intensity -- is not reliably estimable; the multilevel literature puts the floor at 30 groups and prefers 50. Worse, regimes defined by volatility and session are almost certainly NOT exchangeable, and naive partial pooling across non-exchangeable groups has been measured producing type I error rates of 21.6-42.1% against a nominal 5%. The basket-trial literature's EXNEX and multi-source-exchangeability designs exist precisely for this and work at 5 groups of 13 observations, which is smaller than our cells.
THE_RESEARCH_RETURN_ITSELF.the_cheapest_structural_fix: Replace nine discrete regime LABELS with the continuous COORDINATES that define them -- realised volatility, spread/ATR, trend strength, session -- and fit a smooth varying-coefficient surface. That uses every trade for every estimate, pools automatically across boundaries, and restores conditional exchangeability. It reframes 9 cells of 100 trades as ~900 trades for a low-dimensional surface.
THE_RESEARCH_RETURN_ITSELF.detection_delay_is_a_hard_bound: CUSUM's expected delay is log(ARL0)/KL. At 500-trade ARL0 a 55-to-45 point win-rate collapse takes ~309 trades to detect; a 20-point collapse takes ~77. Any drift smaller than about 20 points is undetectable at our trade rate BY ANY DETECTOR -- that is the optimal detector's delay, not an implementation shortfall.
THE_RESEARCH_RETURN_ITSELF.sequential_inference: For the fixed 90-day horizon, group-sequential testing with alpha spending dominates always-valid methods on power (0.93 against 0.72 in a published head-to-head). For the open-ended live kill-switch, betting-based confidence sequences are the right tool and cost roughly 2x the sample for the right to look continuously. Wald's SPRT is the one method that REDUCES required sample -- 50-70% of the fixed-sample plan -- and it needs a stated null, which the break-even rate now supplies.

sessions.THE_BUG: The persistence feature compared sgn[i] to sgn[i+1]. Its own docstring justified that by MT4's newest-first FILE order -- but load_export() SORTS ASCENDING, and says so in its own docstring: 'the sort is not cosmetic -- reversed, forward would mean backward'. So i+1 is the NEXT BAR IN TIME. 'Low persistence' meant 'the sign is about to flip', and conditioning on that selects bars where price is about to move against the score. WHY_EVERY_CHECK_I_RAN_PASSED.the self-tests: They planted a synthetic edge USING THE SAME persistence function they then tested. A fixture that shares the bug cannot expose it -- the test correctly verified that the estimator recovers what was planted. Self-tests validate ESTIMATION. They have no power over CAUSALITY, and no amount of planted-structure testing ever will.
WHY_EVERY_CHECK_I_RAN_PASSED.the time split: Look-ahead is a deterministic identity, not a fitted parameter, so it survives every split, fold and year. An out-of-sample test detects DATA-MINING. It has no power at all against using the future. Treating a passed split as general validation is what let this stand for several sessions.
WHY_EVERY_CHECK_I_RAN_PASSED.the six adversarial attacks: All six attacked the wrong axis. Conviction confound, direction split, overlap, measure, mechanical reversion -- every one presumes the feature is causal and asks whether the EFFECT is real. None asked whether the FEATURE was legitimate.
WHY_EVERY_CHECK_I_RAN_PASSED.and the three properties I cited as conf: A -0.33 IC is 4-10x larger than real signals produce, which is itself diagnostic of a bug rather than a discovery. It strengthened with conviction because a bigger score needs a bigger adverse move to reach zero within 4 bars. It survived the split because identities do. I read all three as corroboration; each was a symptom.

sessions.WARRANT_300_THE_CHECK_THAT_CATCHES_IT: causality.assert_causal: compute the feature, corrupt every input row after index k, recompute, and require the first k values to be bit-identical. If any moved, the feature read the future. It names the offending index. Cheap, statistics-free, decisive. Its own self-test contains the exact WARRANT#275 bug and requires it to be caught. Both affected scripts now assert causality, and persistence_flip_probe's expected-value test was ALSO corrected -- it asserted [2,1,0,0,0], the look-ahead answer, so the test had been defending the bug.
sessions.HOW_IT_WAS_FOUND: A research agent commissioned on microstructure and barrier-crossing methods flagged it unprompted, reasoning from the shape of the claim rather than from the code: a two-sided window around a future event is look-ahead; the magnitude is implausible; and OOS survival tests for mining, not for peeking. It predicted all three symptoms correctly before seeing a line of the implementation.
sessions.WHAT_SURVIVES_AND_WHAT_DOES_NOT: GONE: the flip-moment inversion, and with it session 60's claim that anything in this campaign has cleared the deflated bar. NOTHING has. For a short the exits should trigger on the ask and are detected on the bid, flattered again. At 0.56-0.63 ATR the barrier table shows the cost-adjusted null falling to 0.22-0.24. sessions.WHY_A_SWEEP_AND_NOT_A_FIX: WARRANT#300 fixed the two functions already known to be broken. Fixing the ones you found is not the same as checking the rest -- the bug that produced a -0.33 IC was a single index sign that survived six adversarial attacks and a time split, and there was no reason to believe it was unique.
sessions.RESULT: Seven per-bar features checked. PASS: moment agreement, conviction, dispersion, persistence; the flip probe's persistence (the repaired one); and the Heston variance path v. FAIL: heston_features.innov.
sessions.THE_REAL_LEAK: innov subtracts a prediction built from theta -- the sample mean of the WHOLE variance series -- and phi, fitted by regression on the whole series. So the innovation at bar t is measured against parameters estimated from data after t. Three of the four Heston conditions inherit it: v_innovation and leverage directly, v_gap through theta. Only v_level is clean.
sessions.why_it_changes_no_conclusion_and_is_stil: This is a milder fault than a shifted index: it does not manufacture a relationship, it makes an existing one look better estimated than it was, and it runs in the direction that would INFLATE a result. The four conditions returned flat while enjoying that advantage, so the null is if anything conservative. Documented in the script with the fix named -- expanding-window re-estimation so bar t sees only bars <= t -- and explicitly marked as not done. If those features are ever used for a positive claim, that work comes first.
sessions.AND_A_FALSE_ALARM_I_CAUSED: The first run failed agreement and dispersion too. Both were my test harness: it built synthetic component columns with np.roll, which WRAPS, so index 0 received data from the end of the series. The harness was the look-ahead, not the features. Fixed to pad-lag instead, and both pass. Worth recording because a causality checker that fails on correct code is worse than none -- it is the same failure mode as the C3.2 guard heuristic that over-reported compliance, only in the opposite direction.
sessions.THE_EXEMPTION_STATED_RATHER_THAN_ASSUMED: Forward returns are excluded and declared in the output. They look forward BY DEFINITION -- that is what makes them labels -- and the discipline is that features may not while labels must. Confusing the two is the exact error being guarded against, so the exemption is printed rather than silently applied.

sessions.AND_MY_EXPLANATION_FOR_THOSE_MISMATCHES_: WARRANT#292 attributed the 1-in-200 mismatches to bars where the live signalDir is 0 -- MTF and momentum exactly cancelling, which zeroes volatility, volume and session by design while the calibration side has no such rule. sessions.THE_BUG: Every multi-timeframe read passed the CHART's bar index straight into an iMA call on a HIGHER timeframe. The chart is M5. The export scans indices up to 50,000. Asking for the 40,000th D1 bar -- or H4, or H8 -- requests something that does not exist; MT4 returns 0 for an out-of-range index, both moving averages come back 0, the comparison 0 > 0 is false, and the timeframe silently reports BEARISH.
sessions.why_the_existing_guard_missed_it: iBars(PERIOD_D1) >= 55 asks whether enough D1 bars EXIST, then requests index 40,000 of them. Availability is a COUNT; the failure is an INDEX, expressed in another timeframe's units. The guard was checking a different question from the one that fails.
sessions.THE_MEASUREMENT: comp_mtf sits at exactly -36.00 -- its maximum negative, all five timeframes bearish -- for 39,636 of 50,000 bars (79.3%), releasing only in the most recent bars where the indices finally fall in range. Mean score -23.99, median -26.2: the score is not centred on zero. 88.7% of bars score SHORT, over a sample in which the market rose 2.4%. That is not a bearish model, it is a stuck one.

IT_EXPLAINS_MOST_OF_WHAT_WAS_FOUND_TODAY.conviction is anti-predictive: high |score| means strongly negative means short, in a rising market. The monotone win-rate decline across conviction bands is the pin, not a property of conviction.

That is a coherence break deeper than C1.3's: both paths ran the same code, and only one was fed valid inputs. C1.3's parity test could never have caught it either -- it samples 200 bars from index 30 upward with a stride, so it compares two paths that are both wrong in the same way.
