sessions.type: RE-MEASUREMENT ON THE CLEAN EXPORT. WARRANT#304 verified, and two of today's claims corrected as a result.
sessions.THE_FIX_IS_CONFIRMED: Regenerated the export on the fixed build. comp_mtf pinned at exactly -36.00 falls from 39,636 bars (79.3%) to 525 (1.1%). Its mean moves from -29.69 to +15.41, percent negative from 91.3% to 29.4%, and the decile means now vary between +4.3 and +26.7 instead of being the constant -36.0 they were for seven consecutive deciles. The score's short share falls from 88.7% to 28.4%. The component is alive across the whole sample for the first time in this project's history.
sessions.CORRECTION_1_THE_CONVICTION_GRADIENT_IS_: Reported twice today -- session 64 as 'mildly counter-informative', session 76 as six ordered bands that are 'not what noise looks like'. On the clean export a Cochran-Armitage trend test across the six bands at EFFECTIVE sample gives z = -0.967, p = 0.33. The win rate still declines numerically (0.414 to 0.390) but the ordering is well inside what noise produces at 125-500 effective observations per band. The earlier version was measured on a score dominated by a component pinned at maximum bearish, so 'high conviction' largely meant 'strongly short', and the gradient was the pin.
sessions.CORRECTION_2_THE_AGGREGATE_SHORTFALL_IS_: Session 76 reported the system winning less often than a coin flip through its own bracket, and session 79 said the block bootstrap had settled it. On clean data the two methods disagree: the Wilson interval on the effective sample puts the null INSIDE [0.3857, 0.4242] against an observed 0.4050, while the moving-block bootstrap gives a gap of -0.0174 with a CI of [-0.0275, -0.0068] that excludes zero. I do not think the bootstrap should win by default -- its block length is 40 bars against a 20-bar label overlap, only twice the dependence range, which plausibly makes its interval too narrow. Recorded as UNRESOLVED rather than resolved in the direction I previously argued for.
sessions.AND_ONE_FINDING_THAT_IS_NEW_AND_LARGE: The loss is concentrated entirely in shorts. Longs: n=35,749, win rate 0.4205, gap vs null -0.0018, mean +0.0314R -- essentially AT the null. Shorts: n=14,251, win rate 0.3660, gap -0.0563, mean -0.0725R. Market drift does not explain it: the sample's +2.4% cumulative rise is about 0.0016 ATR per bar, far too small for a 5.6-point gap, and if drift were the cause longs would sit ABOVE the null by a comparable margin rather than on it. Something about the short entries specifically is bad, and that is a sharper question than any asked today.
sessions.THE_PATTERN_IN_TODAY_S_CORRECTIONS: Three findings retracted or downgraded in one day -- the flip-moment inversion (look-ahead), the conviction gradient (a pinned component), the aggregate barrier shortfall (method-dependent). Each was found by doing the next piece of work properly rather than by defending the last one. What they share is that each was measured on an instrument or a dataset whose validity had not itself been checked. The order that would have prevented all three: check the FEATURE is causal, check the DATA is not constant, and check the TEST agrees with itself, before interpreting any number.

sessions.type: WARRANT#305/306 -- the organism's own clock returns nothing, and the search for why turned up the architecture. The system has one directional input, its sign is a coin flip, and its magnitude predicts the opposite.
sessions.THE_SPAN_TEST_MANUEL_ASKED_FOR: Every horizon used until now was a fixed bar count from an arbitrary bar. An organism is a SPAN with its own length -- 5,068 of them here, median 7 bars, p90 23, max 77, so a 5-bar lookahead is most of a contraction and a fraction of a trend leg. Built three CAUSAL span features (age within the span, length of the last completed span, and maturity against the running median of previously completed spans of that class) and tested at both fixed and span-scaled horizons. The obvious feature -- fraction through the span -- was NOT used, because it requires knowing when the span ends, which is the exact shape of the bug retracted this morning. All three passed assert_causal before any result was read.
sessions.and_it_returns_nothing: 60 cells, every one negative, nothing clearing the bar. And the 60 were one fact re-shown 60 times, not 60 confirmations -- the same trap WARRANT#270 identified for the nine regimes. Pooled IC is negative at every horizon with z pinned near -3.2 whether h is 1 or 34, which is the signature of a constant per-bar relationship rather than noise. Where you are in the span adds nothing over that pooled number.
sessions.WHAT_THE_HUNT_TURNED_UP_INSTEAD: Checking whether any OTHER component was degenerate like comp_mtf had been, the decile means of volatility, volume, session and pattern all moved in lockstep with comp_mtf -- peaks at deciles 2/5/8, troughs at 3/6/7. Independent signals do not do that. Reading the code rather than inferring statistically: signalDir is computed at line 18125 as sign(totalScore) AFTER MTF and momentum are added, and volatility, volume and session are then each MULTIPLIED by it. Pattern is not.
sessions.SO_THE_SIX_COMPONENT_BLEND_HAS_THREE_DIR: Directional inputs and their amplitudes: comp_mtf mean |v| 27.0 (max 36), comp_momentum 18.7 (max 28.75), comp_pattern 2.2 (max 5). Pattern flips the direction on 3.1% of bars. sign(MTF+momentum) equals sign(MTF) alone on 85.5% of bars, and the final score keeps that direction 93.6% of the time. Volatility, volume and session cannot vote on direction AT ALL -- they amplify or damp a decision already made.
sessions.which_explains_the_calibration_failures_: P3B searches six weights per regime. Three of them are multiplied by a fixed direction, so re-weighting them changes CONVICTION only -- the search can never change which way a trade goes, only how hard it is taken. If the direction is wrong, no weight vector in the space can fix it. Nine regimes failing to validate is then not a data problem; it is a search over the wrong parameters.
sessions.AND_THE_DIRECTION_IS_A_COIN_FLIP_WHILE_T: sign(comp_mtf) predicts the sign of the forward move on 49.56%, 50.37%, 49.97% and 49.66% of bars at h = 1, 5, 13, 34 -- z of -1.97, +0.74, -0.04, -0.26. Chance, at every horizon. But comp_mtf's IC against forward return is -0.004, -0.027, -0.048, -0.081 across those same horizons, growing steadily, and it dominates the score's own IC. So the sign carries nothing and the STRENGTH carries the wrong thing: strong multi-timeframe alignment predicts REVERSAL.
sessions.the_mechanism_has_a_name_and_a_published: Trend exhaustion. It is the shape the commissioned research flagged independently -- Bouchaud's optimal signal phi - c*phi^3, where large absolute moves mean-revert and the optimal indicator becomes negatively dependent on the trend at the extremes. This system does the opposite: it sizes the bet by the trend's strength, in the trend's direction, which is precisely the region where that literature says to reduce or invert.
sessions.SIGNIFICANCE_STATED_HONESTLY: None of it clears the deflated bar. comp_mtf at h=34 gives z about -3.1 against a bar of 3.98, and the pooled score sits at -3.0 to -3.5 at every horizon. At a conventional 0.05 it would be significant; against this campaign's own multiplicity deflation for 737 registered tests it is not, and the rule was set before the number was seen. What is claimed is a MECHANISM -- consistent across seven horizons, agreeing with a published functional form, and following from the code's structure rather than from a search over the data. What is not claimed is a significant effect.
sessions.comp_session_is_the_only_positive_one: +0.0037 at h=1, shrinking to +0.0009 by h=34. Tiny and decaying. Noted because it is the sole exception, not because it is a finding.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: Analysis only. No EA change. The architectural facts are read from source line numbers, not inferred.

sessions.type: WARRANT#310 -- the benchmark this campaign never ran, and WARRANT#309, a gate I opened by accident and closed.
sessions.THE_QUESTION_NOBODY_HAD_ASKED: Every test in this campaign has asked whether TUNGSTEN's score predicts. None has asked whether ANYTHING does. Two very different worlds produce a coin-flip direction and they demand opposite responses: either the data is efficient at this frequency, in which case the system is attempting something unsupported and no component engineering helps; or simple well-known predictors DO work here and this composite does not, in which case the failure is specific. Only a benchmark separates them.
sessions.THE_RESULT: Six baselines under the identical 2.5/1.5 bracket. Ranked by mean R: reversal_5 +0.0254, reversal_1 +0.0085, TUNGSTEN +0.0021, random -0.0010, ma_cross -0.0198, momentum_20 -0.0229. NOTHING clears the deflated bar at any horizon. But the ordering is MIRROR-SYMMETRIC -- reversal at +0.025, trend-following at -0.023, random sitting between them at -0.001 -- and that symmetry is structure rather than noise.
sessions.and_the_uncomfortable_placement: TUNGSTEN's direction IS the ma_cross baseline. comp_mtf is EMA20-vs-EMA50 alignment across five timeframes, which is a multi-timeframe moving-average crossover, and the plain ma_cross baseline is the second-worst row in the table at -0.0198. The system is built on the losing side of the only structure the benchmark shows.
sessions.THE_RANDOM_CONTROL_CAUGHT_A_BUG_IN_MY_OW: The first run reported that random cleared the deflated bar at h=1 with a hit rate of 0.4904 and z of -4.3. A random signal cannot carry direction, so the test was broken. Cause: a flat bar has sign(forward return) == 0, which never equals plus or minus one, so every zero-move bar counted as a MISS for every signal and pushed all hit rates about a point below fifty uniformly. Zero-move bars are now excluded. This is exactly why the control row exists, and it earned its place on the first run.
sessions.and_it_caught_a_second_thing: In the split-half check, random achieved 'same side in both halves' on 2 of 3 horizons. So that consistency criterion does NOT discriminate at this sample size, and any future finding resting on it is resting on nothing. reversal_5 passes the same test -- and so does noise.
sessions.THE_NUMBER_THAT_FRAMES_EVERYTHING: At a spread of 0.6 ATR with a 2.5/1.5 bracket, the required win-rate lift over the driftless null is s/(a+b) = 0.6/4.0 = 15.0 PERCENTAGE POINTS. The best baseline in the table delivers about 1.5. That is not a marginal shortfall, it is an order of magnitude, and it applies to reversal_5 as much as to TUNGSTEN. reversal_5 also decays between halves: mean R +0.0412 (t 1.22) in the older half against +0.0096 (t 0.28) in the newer.
sessions.which_answers_the_two_worlds_question: It is world (a), or close to it. No simple directional signal on M5 USDJPY over this sample clears anything, and even the best of them is ten times too small to pay the spread. The composite is not failing where simpler things succeed. There is no demonstrated simple directional signal here for it to fail against -- and the frequency itself, not the component design, is the binding constraint.
sessions.WARRANT_309_A_GATE_I_OPENED_BY_ACCIDENT: C6.1's consumption check counted any FileOpen with FILE_READ on the export name. WARRANT#296's per-symbol copy routine opens the export for reading in order to duplicate it, so the check started PASSING -- turning an honest split verdict into a clean MET for a reason with nothing to do with the criterion. The writer copying its own output is not the learner consuming the record. Reads inside the export function are now excluded and the verdict is back to LETTER MET, INTENT NOT MET. A gate opened by accident is still a gate opened, and this one was opened by my own change four hours earlier.

sessions.type: WARRANT#311 -- the frequency ladder. The strategic question answered quantitatively, and a vague goal replaced with a specification.
sessions.THE_SETUP: Two curves. The REQUIRED win-rate lift is s/(a+b), pure arithmetic: the spread is a fixed number of pips while the bar's range grows with the square root of time, so s/ATR falls as 1/sqrt(k) and the requirement falls with it. The ACHIEVABLE lift does whatever the market does. Where they cross is the minimum viable holding period, and that is a configuration answer rather than a research programme.
sessions.THE_RESULT: Required falls exactly as predicted: 15.0pp at 5 minutes, 8.7 at 15, 6.1 at 30, 4.3 at an hour, 3.1 at two, 2.2 at four, 1.5 at eight. Achievable falls with it: +1.2pp at 5 minutes, +0.1 at 15, then NEGATIVE from 30 minutes onward. The curves never cross.
sessions.BUT_THE_GAP_IS_THE_USEFUL_NUMBER: It narrows from -13.8pp at M5 to -1.9pp at eight hours. Lengthening the horizon removes about 86% of the hurdle. So the frequency lever is real and large -- it simply is not sufficient on its own, because the reversal signal that carries the M5 lift does not survive to longer holds. Both halves of that sentence matter: the lever works, and this signal does not.
sessions.WHICH_REPLACES_A_VAGUE_GOAL_WITH_A_SPECI: The target is no longer 'find an edge'. It is: find a signal with a win-rate lift of at least 2.2 percentage points that HOLDS at a four-hour hold. That is checkable against any candidate in minutes, it is falsifiable, and it is roughly a fifth of the hurdle the current M5 configuration faces. Any future component, indicator or model can be measured against it before a line of MQL4 is written.
sessions.SAMPLE_CAVEAT_STATED: The ladder trades sample for economics in exactly the place the economics improve: 49,851 blocks at M5 falls to 1,016 at four hours and 495 at eight. The achieved figures at the long end carry wide intervals and the negative values there are not distinguishable from zero. The REQUIRED curve is arithmetic and carries no such uncertainty, which is why the gap is quoted rather than the achieved figure alone.
sessions.AND_WHAT_THE_LADDER_ASSUMES: Aggregated M5 blocks are not real H1 or H4 bars -- the first-passage resolution is computed from the M5 path within each block, which is if anything finer than a real higher-timeframe bar would give. Spread is held constant in pips across the ladder, which is optimistic at the short end and roughly right at the long end.

sessions.type: WARRANT#312 -- the screen. 22 causal candidates against a bar set by arithmetic before any of them was measured.
sessions.THE_DESIGN: WARRANT#311 turned the goal into a number: 2.2 percentage points of win-rate lift at a four-hour hold, because that is where the spread hurdle falls to 2.2 points. Three hurdles, all required. ECONOMIC: lift at or above 2.2pp over a random control at the same scale -- large enough to pay costs, not merely significant. STATISTICAL: clears the deflated bar, which this screen itself raises by the number of candidates. STABLE: clears the ECONOMIC bar in BOTH halves independently.
sessions.why_the_stability_test_changed: Earlier today the robustness criterion was 'same sign in both halves'. WARRANT#310's random control passed that on two of three horizons, so it does not discriminate at this sample size. Requiring the full economic threshold in each half separately cannot be passed by noise, and it immediately proved its worth.
sessions.THE_RESULT: No candidate clears all three. Two cleared the economic bar on the full sample and failed the halves: momentum_1 at 2.6pp overall but -1.9pp in the older half against +7.6pp in the newer -- the classic overfit signature, and completely invisible to a whole-sample test. That is exactly what the stability hurdle exists to catch, and it caught it on the first run.
sessions.THE_CLOSEST_MISS_NAMED_BUT_NOT_PROMOTED: reversal_13: 3.1pp on the full sample, 3.0pp older, 2.0pp newer. Positive in both halves, which nothing else managed at that size, but the newer half falls 0.2pp short of the bar and z is 1.99 against a deflated 4.00. At four-hour blocks that is roughly a two-day lookback held about three days -- multi-day mean reversion, which the FX literature does document at that scale. It is a miss. The bar was set by arithmetic before any candidate was seen, so a near miss is a miss, and it is recorded here as the direction that came closest rather than as a result.
sessions.WHAT_THE_SCREEN_IS_WORTH_GOING_FORWARD: It costs minutes and it is now the gate for everything. No component, indicator or model is worth building into the EA unless it clears 2.2pp at a four-hour hold in both halves. That replaces a research programme with a filter, and it is the single most reusable thing produced today.

sessions.type: WARRANT#313 -- the last candidate killed, and killed for a specific reason rather than by a p-value.
sessions.THE_TEST: reversal_13 was the closest miss in the screen: 3.1pp on the full sample, 3.0pp older, 2.0pp newer, failing the 2.2pp bar in the newer half by two tenths of a point. Before accepting or dismissing it, the obvious question: does it need exactly the geometry it was found at? A real effect should not care whether the bracket is 2.5/1.5 or 2.0/2.0, nor whether the block is two hours or eight. So it was re-measured across 27 combinations -- three block sizes, three hold lengths, three bracket shapes -- each against its own random control.
sessions.THE_ANSWER: Positive lift in 9 of 27 geometries. That is BELOW chance. And every one of the nine sits at K=48, the exact block size the screen happened to use. At two-hour blocks it is negative in all nine combinations; at eight-hour blocks it is negative in eight of nine. The effect does not exist away from one parameter value.
sessions.WHY_THIS_IS_THE_RIGHT_KIND_OF_KILL: The screen had already rejected it on the both-halves rule, by 0.2pp -- a rejection that could have felt arbitrary and invited a second look at a slightly different bar. The sensitivity test replaces that narrow miss with a mechanism: the signal is localised to a single block size, which is what a lucky parameter looks like and not what a market effect looks like. A rejection you can explain is worth more than a rejection you can only quote.
sessions.AND_IT_VALIDATES_THE_SCREEN_ITSELF: Two independent hurdles agreed. The stability rule caught momentum_1's -1.9/+7.6 split, and the sensitivity sweep caught reversal_13's single-parameter dependence. Neither would have been visible in a full-sample number, and the full-sample numbers for both looked encouraging.
sessions.WHERE_THAT_LEAVES_THE_SEARCH: Every lead opened today is now closed. The flip-moment inversion was look-ahead. The conviction gradient was the pinned component. The barrier shortfall is method-dependent. The trend-exhaustion mechanism is real in shape but not in strength. Nothing simple predicts direction. The frequency lever removes 86% of the cost hurdle but the signal does not survive to the longer horizon. And the closest surviving candidate needed one specific block size to exist at all.

sessions.CORRECTION_1_MY_COIN_FLIP_CLAIM_WAS_OVER: I reported that sign(comp_mtf) predicts on 49.6-50.4% of bars and called the direction a coin flip. On 50,000 bars the standard error of a hit rate is 0.22pp, so the 95% band is plus or minus 0.44pp. A world-class FX strategy at annual Sharpe 0.5 produces a per-M5-bar lift of about +0.05pp -- FIVE TIMES SMALLER than the measurement noise. The test cannot distinguish 'no signal' from 'an excellent signal'. The honest statement is: no signal large enough to matter at this frequency, and this test could not have seen a normal-sized one anyway. That is a weaker and more accurate claim than the one I made.
sessions.CORRECTION_2_THE_COST_RATIO_WAS_MEASURED: Every cost calculation today used spread/ATR = 0.60, taken from the EA's own startup readings of 56% and 63%. Those were logged at 21:24 and 23:25 -- near rollover, when spreads are widest. Roll's estimator applied to the M5 return series gives an effective spread of 1.49 pips against the 2.3 quoted, and a MEDIAN spread/ATR across hours of 0.260. The ratio driving every hurdle in this ledger was more than double the actual median.
sessions.uncertainty_on_that_correction: Roll's estimator is undefined in 7 of 24 hours here because the return autocovariance turns positive -- exactly the failure mode the earlier research warned of -- and returns an implausible 1.24 in one hour. So 0.26 is a noisy median, not a precise figure, and the honest position is a RANGE of 0.26 to 0.60 rather than a replacement point estimate.
sessions.THE_TABLE_THAT_CHANGES_THE_CONCLUSION: Required lift is s/(a+b) scaled by 1/sqrt(H); available lift at the literature's ceiling for single-pair systematic FX (annual Sharpe 0.5) is 0.25*S/sqrt(N). At 5 minutes the system is short by 142x. At 40 minutes, 18x. At 3 hours -- the longest horizon I had tested -- 4x. AT ONE DAY IT IS VIABLE, and comfortably so at three days and beyond. Under the pessimistic 0.60 ratio the crossover moves to about a week. Either way the crossover EXISTS, and it is not at 34 bars.
sessions.and_the_observation_that_reframes_the_ar: The research made a point I had missed entirely: the minimum viable hold of roughly 300 to 1,500 M5 bars corresponds to the H4 and D1 timeframes THE MTF STACK ALREADY COMPUTES. The stack is not wrong about which timeframes carry information. It uses them to TIME five-minute entries instead of to HOLD multi-day positions. That is a configuration error, not a modelling one, and it is the most actionable sentence produced today.
sessions.THE_MA_FAMILY_HAS_A_DEATH_CERTIFICATE_AN: Two independent strands. EMPIRICAL: Neely, Weller & Ulrich (2009, JFQA) re-tested previously published FX rules truly out of sample and found moving-average and filter rules specifically dead by the early 1990s -- not weaker, dead. Marshall, Cahan & Cahan (2008, J. Empirical Finance) tested 7,846 technical rules on FIVE-MINUTE data and found NONE profitable after data-snooping adjustment. Kozhan & Salmon (2012) had the full limit order book and still found no consistent economic value. STRUCTURAL: Zakamulin proves every MA-type indicator is algebraically a weighted moving average of past price changes, so EMA20-vs-EMA50 across five timeframes is not five votes but five correlated transforms of one input with overlapping support. Confluence across them cannot create information; it reduces variance around the same conditional mean, and if that mean is zero it reduces variance around zero. That is a first-principles explanation for the flat hit rate, and it independently derives the architectural finding of WARRANT#306.
sessions.what_the_literature_says_IS_available_on: Direction at intraday frequency requires signed order flow, which OHLC plus tick volume cannot supply -- and MT4 tick volume counts quote updates, not trades, so even bulk-volume classification is applied to the wrong variable. What IS both documented and computable is VOLATILITY forecasting (HAR-RV, realized range estimators, all pure OHLC) and EFFECTIVE SPREAD estimation from OHLC (Ardia, Guidotti & Kroencke 2024, JFE), which is what would settle the cost question properly.

sessions.type: WARRANT#317 -- THE MEASUREMENT WALL. The deepest structural result of the campaign, and it explains four unmet criteria at once.
sessions.THE_TWO_CURVES_MEET_A_THIRD: Required lift falls with holding time as 1/sqrt(H). Available lift rises with holding time. But there is a third curve nobody had drawn: DETECTABILITY. Non-overlapping holds fall as 1/H, so the smallest lift a test can find rises as sqrt(H). Required falls, detectable rises, and they cross in the wrong place.
sessions.THE_TABLE: On 50,000 M5 bars -- eight months of one instrument -- at a 40-minute hold there are 6,250 independent samples, the required lift is 2.30pp and the smallest detectable is 1.77pp: MEASURABLE, and measured, and absent. At three hours: required 1.11pp, detectable 3.65pp. At one day: required 0.38pp, detectable 10.64pp. At one week: required 0.17pp, detectable 24.01pp.
sessions.THE_SENTENCE_THAT_FOLLOWS: The frequencies we CAN measure are the ones where costs make an edge impossible. The frequencies where an edge is economically possible are the ones we CANNOT measure. Eight months of one instrument does not contain the answer at any horizon, and no amount of cleverness applied to it will.
sessions.AND_THE_SCALE_OF_WHAT_WOULD: To detect the required 0.38pp at a one-day hold at 95% confidence and 80% power takes 133,605 independent day-holds. That is roughly 514 years of a single instrument, or 772 instruments over eight months. Even an edge five times larger than break-even would still be below the 10.64pp detection floor at that horizon.
sessions.WHAT_THIS_EXPLAINS_THAT_WAS_PREVIOUSLY_F: C4 reads INCONCLUSIVE and always will on this data -- not because the analysis is weak but because the horizon where an edge could exist is below the detection floor. C3.2's 1,309-trade sample floor is the same wall seen from the trade side. C3.7 has no untouched holdout because the whole export has been searched, and a holdout would not help anyway since it inherits the same detection floor. And the resolution budget's nine affordable cells is the same constraint again. Four criteria, four evidence types, one arithmetic fact.
sessions.IT_ALSO_REFRAMES_THE_WHOLE_CAMPAIGN: The question this project has been asking is 'does TUNGSTEN have an edge'. The answerable question is 'can ANY edge be demonstrated with the data available', and at the horizons where an edge is economically possible the answer is no. That is not a verdict on the system. It is a verdict on the experiment.
sessions.WHAT_REMAINS_HONEST_TO_DO: Three options and they should be named plainly. ACQUIRE: hundreds of instrument-years, which is a data project rather than a modelling one and which the per-symbol export now makes possible. ACCEPT: run at a horizon the arithmetic supports and treat viability as a judgement rather than a proven fact, with position sizing chosen for a hypothesis that cannot be verified in advance. ABANDON: conclude that a retail-cost directional system on one FX pair is not demonstrable and stop. The campaign's own Rule III-25 anticipated the third; the measurement wall is what makes the first two into real alternatives rather than evasions.

sessions.AND_WHAT_THE_CONSTANTS_MEAN_IN_BARS: Counting the write sites turned up something the criterion does not ask about. Seven threshold LEVELS are hardcoded (16, 48, 70, 82, 85, 88, 90) and seven adaptation STEPS (0.5 to 8.0). Measured against the export's actual |score| distribution: 16 admits 56.476% of bars, 48 admits 3.080%, 70 admits 0.102%, 90 admits 0.002%. sessions.BUT_THE_OPERATING_POINT_INVERTS_THE_ALAR: The calibration prints its choice. Across 23 recorded decisions it picked thr 34 sixteen times and thr 16 seven times -- never remotely near the 82/85/88/90 ceilings. So those ceilings never bind, and an audit that stopped at the static list would have raised an alarm about the wrong end of the band. The real finding is at the other end: the floor constant 16.0 admits 56.5% of all bars and is selected in 7 of 23 decisions. A threshold that admits more than half of every bar is not filtering; it is a formality with a number attached. At the modal 34 the system emits ~218 signals/week on M5.

Levels and steps are now separated by ROLE (a MathMax/MathMin bound or a direct assignment is a level; an addend is a step), with self-tests both ways. A second pass found the level regex only matched first-position bounds, silently dropping 90.0 -- the highest constant in the build.

sessions.TWO_FLOORS_THAT_DISAGREE: Line 58900, the min/max-clamp layer, enforces MathMax(MinRiskPercent, MathMin(MaxRiskPercent, baseRiskPercent)) with MinRiskPercent declared as an input at 1.5%. Nineteen lines later the CEO-ceiling layer runs MathMax(0.5, MathMin(_ceoRiskCap, baseRiskPercent)). And g_CEO_RiskCeiling genuinely reaches 0.5 -- it is set to MathMax(0.5, 2.0 - depth*1.5) as competence falls (line 55128) and halved again with the same floor (55132). So the later layer can drive risk to a third of the declared minimum, and the input named 'Minimum risk floor' does not bind.
sessions.AND_IT_IS_NOT_SIMPLY_A_BUG_WHICH_IS_THE_: The reading that defends it: de-risking hard as evidence weakens is exactly what C8.3 asks for, and this is that behaviour working. The reading that does not: MinRiskPercent's own comment reads '0.01 lot micro viability', so the floor exists to keep orders fillable, and a path that goes under it can produce a size the broker rejects. Those are different claims about one line and the instrument cannot choose between them. What it CAN say is that two floors disagree, deliberately or not, and only one of them is documented. Queued as an EA question for Manuel rather than silently 'fixed' in either direction.
sessions.TWO_MISTAKES_INSIDE_THIS_CHECKER_CAUGHT_: First, the assign and clamp patterns both matched `x = MathMax(0.5, MathMin(c, x));`, so 0.50 was reported twice and the violation count read 4 instead of 3 -- deduplicated by (line, value). sessions.C1_1_NOT_MET_THREE_SCORE_FORMULAS: Family membership decided by what a function COMPUTES and RETURNS, never by name -- the build has fourteen functions with 'Score' in the name and most are unrelated quantities. Three independent unified-score implementations remain: CalculateScoreWithWeights, CalculateScoreWithWeightsEx, CalculateUnifiedScoreFromComponents. CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore, the 875-line live scorer, is a WRAPPER -- it calls CalculateScoreWithWeights, so the root is the smaller function. The six COMPONENT functions are genuinely unified (that was C1.3's work and it holds), but each of the three then combines them itself. The criterion's other route is not satisfied either: RunScoreParityTest compares live components against the calibration's recomputation of the SAME components, which is C1.3, not an equivalence test between score functions.
sessions.C1_2_NOT_MET_BUT_ONLY_ITS_SECOND_HALF: The structural half is clean: ClassifyBarToRegime is the single implementation (7 lines, 69 call sites), _WithHysteresis calls it directly (3 sites), DetectCurrentRegime calls _WithHysteresis (14 sites). One classifier, not three, and every entry point reaches the root. What is missing is the DECLARATION the criterion also names -- which entry point a given path should use. Three entry points is a precedence question whether or not anyone wrote the answer down. That is a documentation task rather than a refactor, which makes it one of the cheapest criteria left.
sessions.TWO_ACCIDENTAL_VERDICTS_IN_MY_OWN_CHECKE: This file's docstring warns that reading a passing test as evidence for a criterion it does not address is the error that gave C6.1 an accidental pass this week. (1) The score family was defined as 'calls >=4 component functions', which swept in MeasureRegimeIC, CalibrateBlendRatios, RunScoreParityTest and three weight optimisers -- every one of which calls components to MEASURE, not to produce a score. It reported 7 independent implementations where there are 3, so the verdict rested on a family the criterion never meant. Fixed by requiring the function to RETURN a score. (2) 'precedence declared per path' was tested by searching the WHOLE FILE for the words 'precedence' and 'regime' -- and passed, on a comment about C's &&/?: operator precedence thirty thousand lines from any classifier. C1.2 briefly read MET on that. Fixed by requiring the declaration within 25 lines of a classifier definition and naming one. Both caught before the verdict left the session; both self-tested now.

sessions.WARRANT_328_C5_1_MET_AFTER_TWO_WRONG_REA: Confidence-adjusted Kelly. Reading one: the per-regime half-Kelly blend inside OptimizePrecisionLotSize, gated at 5 observations and floored at 0.1 -- would have given NOT MET on a mechanism the criterion is not about. Reading two: a comment in the sizing path stating ARGUS 'confirmed via direct grep that CalculateKellyCeiling() had ZERO call sites' -- damning at face value, and history; the same comment describes wiring it in. What is true: CalculateKellyCeiling applies f *= clamp(totalTrades/300, 0, 1), exactly the criterion's wording, and is consumed as a terminal minimum at line 58977. The checker requires all three -- ramp, ~300 divisor, and a call site that uses the RETURN VALUE rather than calling it for telemetry, since the build has one of each.
sessions.C5_2_REFUSED_RATHER_THAN_GUESSED: 'Drawdown fade at k=2 wired, using a true high-water mark.' Both structural halves pass: g_Risk.peakEquity is monotonic, persisted, assigned only on a new high, and dd = 1 - eq/peakEquity comes from it. But the fade is 1 - dd/0.22, linear with coefficient 4.55. As 'fade = 1 - k*dd' that is k=4.55; as an exponent it is 1. Neither is 2, and KellyDDBudget is an input so 50 would give exactly k=2. Ruling either way would be a guess about what k denotes presented as a measurement, so the board carries NEEDS SPEC DEFINITION OF k and the question goes to Manuel.
sessions.AND_A_SECOND_DRAWDOWN_MECHANISM_THAT_CAN: The CONTINUOUS DRAWDOWN LOT TAPER at line 58717 computes its own peak as MathMax(accountEquity, effectiveStartBalance) -- the larger of CURRENT equity and the starting balance, which is not a high-water mark. Above the starting balance that expression EQUALS current equity, so its drawdown is identically zero and the taper cannot engage. An account that doubled and gave back a quarter is 25% down from its peak and this sees 0%. It only ever fires below the starting balance. g_Risk.peakEquity is in the same struct and the Kelly fade already uses it.

sessions.THE_HEADLINE_AND_IT_REFRAMES_THE_WHOLE_W: Every 'no edge' verdict reached this week -- C4 INCONCLUSIVE, no IC clearing the deflated bar at any horizon, run 5's STAND DOWN at 20% WR and PF 0.15 -- was measured on a build where the sizing layer is discarded, the emergency exit latches permanently after the first losing trade, the regime transition matrix runs backward, and an exit rule reads a different regime's hazard curve than the trade is in. That is the same lesson as comp_mtf being pinned at -36.00 for 79.3% of every historical scan: the instrument was broken, and the null it produced was a measurement of the breakage. The no-edge conclusion is NOT retracted -- it may well survive -- but it is no longer safe to treat it as measured.
sessions.DOCTRINE_ARITHMETIC_FORGE_UNIFIED_III: Part 8's bookkeeping largely reproduces, but four errors are modelling choices smuggled in as arithmetic. (a) Revision III's headline '+67% lift, nearly triples growth' picks its baseline by AVERAGE LIFT, which the document's own UF-63 forbids ('rank by e^2/m, never by lift alone'); ranked correctly the advantage is ~+22%, not +174%. (b) The +67% is asserted as 'Measured' in the header while 8.10.1 calls it a 'Worked example' and UF-55/56 say the sweep must still be run. (c) It double-counts: UF-53 states the adaptive advantage IS what L0 and L2 were already doing in 8.2. (d) THE BIG ONE, verified structurally by me: EO-40, EO-41 and BS-10 all mandate median-only sizing ('sizing on the mean is a systematic error'), and UF-47 states every Part 8 table uses a single b = 3.09 derived from a mean of an alpha~1.9 tail. On the median the stack's expectancy is claimed to invert from +0.219R to -0.339R. The magnitude needs the rederivation the run-2 agent died before finishing; the contradiction itself is confirmed in the document text.
sessions.DOCTRINE_ARITHMETIC_UNIFIED_5: PART 4B audits DEAD CODE. Its four settings (1.8/2.7, 1.4/2.4, 1.0/2.0, 1.5/2.5) exist only inside TestConfigOnHistoricalBars, which I confirmed has a forward declaration (13091), a definition (47474), two comments -- and ZERO call sites; the source itself marks it 'SUPERSEDED... Marked for deletion'. Retuning those ratios to 3.6/2.2/1.3/2.2 would change nothing that executes. The executable build carries 2.5/1.5 as a universal default and per-regime mirrors at 5216-5221. The inversion claim also fails on its own terms: the real fallbacks already give trending the WIDER ratio and ranging the tighter, the opposite of the allegation, and measured continuation is flat across states (1.043/1.065/1.057/1.070, every CI overlapping and containing 1.0), so neither 1.82 nor 0.67 is supported.
sessions.AND_THE_RATIO_THESIS_FAILS_BEFORE_COST: The decisive measurement. Achieved hit rate tracks 1/(1+R) within +/-1.7pp across the whole ratio axis, and the excess DECLINES as ratio rises. At ratio 3.6 trending achieves 22.57% against a zero-cost requirement of 21.74% -- a +0.83pp margin, IDENTICAL to the +0.83pp at ratio 1.5. U5-30 held 25% fixed while moving the target; the hit rate moves with it. With cost the shortfall goes from -9.6pp at ratio 1.5 to -8.6pp at 3.6: raising the ratio recovers 1pp of a 9-23pp deficit. And cost drag is 2c/(a+b) -- it depends on bracket WIDTH, not ratio, while this build reaches high ratios by TIGHTENING the stop, which shrinks width and makes it worse. At the export bracket the achieved rate is 35.32% against a driftless null of 37.50%: below chance.
sessions.WHAT_U5_GOT_RIGHT: Its diagnosis of one-sidedness is correct in outcome and wrong in cause. Four winning-cluster presses were BUILT and then orphaned, not omitted: dead hot-streak tiers (27210); a Taylor performanceMultiplier of 1.15 on three wins whose finalSize is never read; a win-streak TP boost of up to +100% (16218) overwritten by CalculateSmartTPSL at every entry; and UpdateTPSLSafetyModes x1.3 (16434), same overwrite. g_Goal.nitroMode is declared (14843) and read (58935) with ZERO writers -- a x1.50 press that can never fire. And the _comb stack is genuinely bidirectional, clamped [0.50, 2.50], able to press to 2.5x -- it simply never reaches the order.

THREE_DECISIONS_TAKEN_RATHER_THAN_ASKED.ACQUIRE_ACCEPT_ABANDON: ACCEPT is now ruled out mathematically, not by preference: break-even and achievable hit rates move one-for-one with the ratio, so no exit geometry rescues a system without directional edge, and the achieved rate sits below a driftless null. The sound sequencing is therefore: FIX THE SIX DEFECTS, RE-RUN, THEN DECIDE. Abandoning now would be abandoning on a reading from an instrument we have just proved was misreporting.

sessions.THE_MISTAKE_FIRST: I ran metaeditor.exe through the Bash tool, it returned exit 0, and I read '0 errors, 0 warnings' out of compile181.log and reported it. The log was dated 2026-08-31 22:47 -- MetaEditor had exited without compiling and without writing anything, and I was reading yesterday's file. I deployed twice on that basis, shipping an updated .mq4 alongside an .ex4 that predated every fix. Caught by checking the .ex4 mtime rather than the log text. No live risk (MT4 loads the .ex4, which was the old working binary) but source and binary were mismatched across all three locations. ROOT CAUSE: the same shape as the twelve mails I reported 'sent' after only writing files, and the sweep whose output I read instead of testing -- confirm the artifact, not the effect. FIX: Bash cannot spawn MetaEditor here; PowerShell Start-Process -Wait can. Every compile from now verifies the .ex4 mtime advanced, not the log's text.

FIVE_DEFECTS_SHIPPED.WARRANT#330: SafeOrderSend's suspension gate read `executionSuspended && type <= OP_SELL`, covering only OP_BUY(0) and OP_SELL(1). Every pending type -- OP_BUYLIMIT/SELLLIMIT/BUYSTOP/SELLSTOP -- passed through a gate its own comment calls 'defense in depth'. TryPlaceSignAgnosticBracket() sends OP_BUYSTOP/OP_SELLSTOP with no suspension check of its own, so a system that had STOOD DOWN could still place live bracket orders, and run 5 ended in exactly that state. Widened to every order type; can only ever block more.
FIVE_DEFECTS_SHIPPED.WARRANT#331: tradeManager.maxDailyRisk was declared (14792), read (21612), and assigned NOWHERE in 64,251 lines -- so the test was `dailyRisk > 0.0`, true on the first losing trade of any day. It set emergencyExitActive, whose only writer in the whole file was that `= true`; there was no `= false` anywhere, so once latched it force-closed every subsequent trade, winners included, until re-init. Three-part fix: the limit now derives from the existing MaxDrawdownPercent input (15% daily against the 30% hard stop) rather than a new literal; a non-positive limit reads as 'no limit configured'; and the latch clears when daily risk falls back under it.
FIVE_DEFECTS_SHIPPED.WARRANT#332: ShouldExitOnOptimalStopping indexed g_RegimeSubstrate_Dwell[9] -- keyed 0-8 by ClassifyBarToRegime -- with activeTrades[].currentRegime, which holds (int)engine.regime from the 12-state ENHANCED_MARKET_REGIME taxonomy. REGIME_BULLISH is 2 there and is not regime 2 here, so the bounds guard held while the hazard curve belonged to an unrelated regime. No principled 12->9 mapping exists, so it now reads g_RegimeState.currentRegime, already in the 0-8 space. EnableOptimalStoppingExit defaults true despite four comments claiming it is hard off.

sessions.FAULT_1_THE_RELAY_HAD_NO_OUTBOUND_HALF: relay-listener.ps1 ran `git clone` and `git pull` and nothing else. The flush is therefore placed BEFORE the early exit. It is also pathspec-scoped to messages/from-agent, because .listener.log, .savepoint and .savepoints.log are tracked and rewritten every tick, so `git add -A` would have committed log churn every 30 seconds forever.

sessions.type: ManagePartialProfits examined. The U5 audit was right about what it does and missed that it cannot currently do it -- and that fact turns the minimum-lot decision into a two-part decision.
sessions.WHAT_IT_DOES: No input gate anywhere -- it is unconditionally active. It fires only when price has moved FAVOURABLY by a regime-dependent distance, so it acts exclusively on winning trades: 3.5 ATR taking 30% in regimes 0/1 (trend), 2.0 ATR taking 50% in regime 8 (pullback), 1.5 ATR taking 50% in regimes 4/5 (range), 2.5 ATR taking 50% otherwise. The U5 audit's description is accurate and its complaint is valid in design: this is a rule written only to reduce a position, never to hold one that is working.
sessions.BUT_IT_CANNOT_FIRE_TODAY: The guard is `if(shouldTakePartial && lotSize >= 0.02)`. Every position this build opens is broker minimum lot -- 0.01 -- because of the forcedMinLot chain (WARRANT#336's subject). So the condition is false on every trade and ManagePartialProfits has never executed. The U5 audit called it the only rule firing exclusively on winners; it is the only rule that WOULD fire exclusively on winners, and it is dormant.
sessions.WHY_THIS_MATTERS_FOR_THE_HELD_DECISION: This is a dependency between two items that were being considered separately. Wiring the sizing chain does not merely change position size -- it ACTIVATES a dormant rule that cuts 30-50% off every winner at 1.5-3.5 ATR, on a system whose measured problem is already that it takes small wins and large losses. The realised reward:risk measured from the export is 1.475 (avg win 1.396R, avg loss 0.947R). Turning on sizing without also gating partial profits would push that ratio down at exactly the moment the position sizes become large enough to matter. The two must be decided together, and the sizing fix should not ship alone.

sessions.type: RUN 2, done by hand after its agents were killed: the Part 8 arithmetic rederived independently. Run 1's direction confirmed, run 1's magnitude refuted, and run 1's headline 'arithmetic errors' partly wrong.
sessions.WHAT_RUN_1_CLAIMED: That Part 8's bookkeeping contains errors, the largest being that b = 3.09 is built on the MEAN of an alpha~1.9 tail in violation of the document's own BS-10/EO-41/L2.2 median-only mandate, and that on the median b falls to 1.22 -- a 2.52x reduction -- taking the conservative stack's expectancy from +0.219R to -0.339R and inverting every compounding figure in 8.8.
sessions.WHAT_I_FOUND_REDERIVING_IT: First, the table's internal arithmetic is CORRECT and run 1's framing of 'arithmetic errors' overstates it. E = p*b - (1-p) reproduces every published cell exactly: at b=3.09, break-even 1/(1+3.09) = 24.45% against a published 24.5%; E at 25% = +0.0225 vs published +0.022; at 30% = +0.227; at 35% = +0.4315 vs +0.431. The bookkeeping is sound. What is contestable is a modelling choice, not a sum.
sessions.THE_MEDIAN_CONFLICT_IS_REAL: EO-40 ('size on the median'), EO-41 ('sizing on the mean will bleed... severe') and BS-10 ('Median only') all mandate median sizing, and UF-47 states every Part 8 table uses the single figure b = 3.09, taken from the '14p -- 35% of elapsed' invalidation row. So the conflict run 1 identified exists.
sessions.BUT_THE_MAGNITUDE_IS_NOT_SUPPORTED: Run 1's 2.52x factor is unsourced. The document reports its own mean/median gap at line 1834: E[rem] median 64.8p, mean 78.1p -- a ratio of 1.205, not 2.52. Applying the document's own figure: b falls 3.09 -> 2.56, break-even rises 24.45% -> 28.06%, and expectancy at a 25% win rate flips +0.022 -> -0.109. It DOES change sign, so run 1's direction holds. But -0.109 is roughly a third of the claimed -0.339, and the flip occurs ONLY at the 25% row: at 30% expectancy stays +0.069 and at 35% it stays +0.247. 'Every compounding figure in 8.8 inverts' is not what the document's own numbers produce.
sessions.WHY_THIS_IS_WORTH_RECORDING: This is exactly what a second run is for, and it cuts both ways. Run 1 found a real conflict that a single pass would have missed, and then overstated it by 3x with a factor that appears nowhere in the source. Reporting only the headline would have handed Manuel a false precision; reporting only the refutation would have discarded a true finding. Both halves are the result.
sessions.LIMIT_OF_THIS_REDERIVATION_STATED: I could not confirm from the extracted text that b = 3.09 is itself mean-derived rather than median-derived -- the 14p/35% row implies a 43.3p reward, which matches neither the 64.8p median nor the 78.1p mean directly, so an intermediate step exists that the extract does not show. If b is already a median figure the whole objection dissolves. That is the one open question and it is named rather than assumed away.
sessions.RISK_JUDGMENT: Analysis only. No EA change. Performed by hand because run 2's arithmetic agent was killed by the session rate limit mid-derivation.

sessions.type: WARRANT#342 -- run 2 audited my own ten fixes and found a risk I introduced, two overstated diagnoses and three sites I walked past. All corrected and shipped. Verdicts: 5 CORRECT, 3 INCOMPLETE, 1 RISKY, 1 WRONG.
sessions.WHY_THIS_ENTRY_MATTERS_MOST: Every prior entry today recorded me finding defects in someone else's code. This one records an independent pass finding defects in MINE, and it found more than I expected. A second run that only confirms the first is worthless; this one did not.
sessions.RISKY_331_A_REAL_RISK_I_INTRODUCED: My latch-release cleared riskMgr.emergencyActive, a flag CheckTradeRiskLimits does not own. It has two live setters: UpdateTradeManagerPortfolioMetrics raises it on a portfolio HEAT breach, and the daily-risk path raises it too. ApplyTradeManagementRules calls those two in immediate succession, so a heat breach could be raised and then cleared in the same pass on a daily-risk condition that says nothing about heat -- re-enabling the entry gates while portfolio heat was still over 1.5x its limit. Bounded to one tick, because the branch is gated on emergencyExitActive which only the daily path sets, but real. FIXED: clears only the flag it owns, and releases the shared flag only when tradeManager.riskLimitsBreached is false, with the held state named in the log line.
sessions.AND_A_SECOND_ORDER_NOTE_WORTH_KEEPING: CalculateDailyRisk sums realised losses from today's closed history plus unrealised, and the emergency close converts unrealised to realised -- so daily risk does NOT fall by closing positions. The latch realistically releases only at server-date rollover. That is correct behaviour for a DAILY limit but is not what my comment described, and the comment was corrected. Also: the 15% limit (MaxDrawdownPercent*0.5) is dimensionally right but weak -- a 15%-of-equity daily loss against a 30% hard stop means the brake engages only after half the drawdown budget is gone in one day. Defensible as derived rather than invented, but it is a weak brake and should be named as one.
sessions.WRONG_339_MY_DIAGNOSIS_WAS_FALSE: I claimed regime 8 committed with zero confirmation because g_RegimeHysteresis[8] is uninitialised. The array fact is true; the consequence was not. Reaching that test requires passing the `transitionRegime == rawRegime` gate, and the only path setting transitionRegime to a real regime sets transitionConfirmBars = 1 at the same moment; the increment above makes it >= 2 before the test. So checker rule and honesty pulled opposite ways. The resolution I chose was right: print the number the system ACTUALLY USES downstream -- SpecBreakevenWR consumes g_P6_AvgRR whether measured or not -- with an ' unmeasured' label beside it. Withholding the number hides what the system is really doing.

sessions.ONE_AUTHORITY_WARRANT_347: engine.regime had one writer, inside E99_ProcessExecutionDecisions, called as OnTick's second-to-last statement -- so every consumer above it read the PREVIOUS tick's classification, or REGIME_UNDEFINED before the first. Moved to the top of OnTick, after the safety guards and before the first consumer. Verified safe from source rather than assumed: ClassifyEnhancedRegime() reads only market data (UpdateComprehensiveMTFContext, iATR, CalculateMarketFeatures(0), ClassifyBarToRegime_WithHysteresis) and consumes nothing produced later in OnTick, and E99 has exactly one call site so ownership could move rather than duplicate. engine.regime now has one initialiser and one live writer.
sessions.AND_IT_COLLAPSED_THE_THREE_AUTHORITIES_C: A run-2 agent reported three independent regime authorities. That is wrong and the source says so: ClassifyEnhancedRegime CALLS ClassifyBarToRegime_WithHysteresis, which is what assigns g_RegimeState.currentRegime. It is a mapping layer, not a third classifier. So the single line at the top of OnTick now refreshes BOTH the 0-8 base regime and the 12-state enhanced regime from ONE classification, before any consumer of either runs. The taxonomies stay distinct -- they index differently sized tables -- but they are now guaranteed to describe the same bar, which is the property that was actually missing.
sessions.REGIME_8_MADE_REACHABLE_WARRANT_346_AND_: Established from source that GetRegimeName is authoritative: index 7 = Building Momentum, index 8 = Controlled Pullback. An earlier note of mine had these swapped, inherited from run 5's log which prints regime+1. Two defects followed. (a) ClassifyEnhancedRegime had no case 8, so Controlled Pullback fell to default -> REGIME_CONSOLIDATION, telling every consumer 'this is a range' about a state the classifier had identified as a textbook pullback with confirmed wave-angle recovery. Now mapped by prevailing trend with the OPPOSITE polarity to case 7, and that opposition is the substance: a cracking trend leans against itself, a controlled pullback leans WITH the trend it pauses inside. (b) RegimeHasStructuralConfirmation had no case 8 either, so the commit test could never pass and regime 8 was unreachable as the live regime at any confirmation count. Built its gate from regime 8's own detection conditions -- intact trend DNA (>=3 consecutive HH/HL or LL/LH) plus either confirmed angleRecovery or a bounded 2-8 bar counter-move on non-expanding volume at a level.
sessions.ALSO_FOUND_CASE_7_IS_A_MIXED_BUCKET: Its comment claimed 'Exhaustion / Distribution' while GetRegimeName calls it Building Momentum. Reading where the core classifier returns 7 shows BOTH: trendWeakeningBullish/Bearish ('structural crack'), pre-breakout coiling, and failed-recovery pullbacks. Cracking and coiling are opposite conditions sharing one bucket. The exhaustion-shaped mapping was kept (weakening dominates three of four entry paths) and the comment now says what the bucket really contains instead of asserting a name that contradicts the authority.
sessions.SIZING_REVIVED_WARRANT_349_AND_350: g_Risk.recentWinRate had one writer in 64,000 lines, inside CalculateIntelligentRisk() which has zero call sites -- so it held 0.0 for the EA's life and `0.0 < SpecWR()-3` forced broker-minimum lot on every trade, discarding the entire 15-layer sizing machine. Fed from CalculateRecentWinRate(), already live and consumed by five other subsystems, correct units, honest fallbacks. DELIBERATELY did NOT wire CalculateIntelligentRisk itself: WARRANT#167 examined exactly that and refused because it also writes g_Risk.currentRisk, which has several other live writers whose interaction was never mapped. That reasoning still holds. Only recentWinRate was missing and it has no competing writer. Min-lot below the WR floor is INTENDED ('edge observation mode'); the defect was that the mode could never be left. Paired with #350: EnablePartialProfits input added, defaulted FALSE -- that rule fires only on winners, has never executed because its lotSize>=0.02 guard was unreachable, and reviving sizing would otherwise have switched on an untested winner-cutting rule as a side effect. Realised R:R is 1.475 (avg win 1.396R vs avg loss 0.947R), so the measured problem is already winners too small.
sessions.C5_7_EARNED_WARRANT_351: Three literals remained in the risk chain; all three named. The substantive call: CEODeRiskFloorPercent stays 0.5 and stays BELOW MinRiskPercent (1.5) by design. That layer is the CEO-competence de-risker -- g_CEO_RiskCeiling falls to 0.5 as competence degrades, and going below the normal operating minimum is precisely its job, which is what C8.3 asks for. Clamping it up would disable the mechanism exactly when it is needed. The value was right; the DOCUMENTATION was the defect, because nothing said the two floors serve different purposes. Named caveat: MinRiskPercent cites '0.01 lot micro viability', so on a small enough account 0.5% may size below the broker minimum and be rejected -- an account-size question, now visible as an input. Also corrected an earlier audit error: 0.70/1.30 bound a MULTIPLIER, not a risk percentage. C5.7 NOT MET -> MET, board 15 MET / 9 NOT MET.

sessions.RG_18_RUN_AT_LAST_WARRANT_353: FORGE UNIFIED III calls the regime flicker report the cheapest and most important test in the project. It had never been run. sessions.WARRANT_357_THE_WEIGHT_SEARCH_WAS_OPTIMI: CalculateScoreWithWeightsEx was not a cosmetic duplicate. Established from source: the live scorer (CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore, 876 lines) and the explicit-weight calibration scorer (CalculateScoreWithWeights) BOTH carry the feature-interaction synergy bonus and the type-aware continuation/reversal adjustment, and NEITHER has a sequence multiplier. Ex had it exactly backwards: no synergy, no type-aware adjustment, plus a 0.85-1.20 sequence multiplier of its own, and it took its signal direction from the UNWEIGHTED sc0+sc1 rather than the weighted running total, so its volume, volatility and session terms could carry the opposite sign on the same bar. Every caller of Ex is a WEIGHT SEARCH. Weights were therefore selected as optimal for a scoring function the EA never runs, and then handed to the live scorer. That is the score-function divergence contamination FORGE_FINALE lists as outstanding. Ex is now a wrapper: it packs the flat array into the struct and delegates.
sessions.THE_INDEX_SWAP_THAT_WAS_NOT_A_BUG: wt[] carries volume at index 2 and volatility at index 3; the struct declares volatility third and volume fourth. sessions.WARRANT_358_C1_1_EVIDENCE_BUILT_NOT_CLAI: C1.1 accepts either a single implementation or an equivalence test showing agreement. So the equivalence route is the honest one. RunScoreParityTest previously compared five COMPONENTS; it now also replays the calibration scorer on live's OWN captured effective weights (g_LastComp_W, taken after blend, CATREC damping and IC amplification) and compares the composed totals, writing TUNGSTEN_score_equivalence.csv. So the build could say which rule fired but never how far the run had got -- the exact quantity RULE 12.1 turns on. On a directionless entry NO arrangement of stop, target and trail can produce positive expectancy before costs -- that is not an empirical claim, it is arithmetic. So a healthy positive mean was impossible and therefore had to be a defect. The question 'why does a positive result exist at all' found both bugs; reading the code would not have.
sessions.BUG_1_THE_SETTLEMENT: Runs where nothing triggered were settled at fav[:,last] - adv[:,last], which expands to (high - entry) + (low - entry) for the final bar. That is not a return at all, and it is biased upward whenever the last bar's upper wick exceeds its lower one. It governed every untriggered run INCLUDING the baseline row the search was being compared against. Corrected to the close-based net return.
sessions.BUG_2_THE_UNFILLABLE_TRAILING_PRICE: With bug 1 fixed the artefact SURVIVED, so a null control was run with the direction replaced by a coin flip. The coin flip earned MORE than the real signal (+0.5968 vs +0.5507 ATR), which is proof by construction that the number came from the arithmetic. Cause: a trailing exit was credited peak minus trail distance, where the peak is built from bar HIGHS and the retracement is detected on bar LOWS. A bar's high and low have no known ordering, so that price is the best of both ends of the same bar and is not fillable from bar data. Corrected to settle at the CLOSE of the bar where the retracement is detected -- conservative, fillable, and neutral with respect to intrabar ordering.
sessions.AFTER_BOTH_FIXES: Best mean return on the real direction is +0.0168 ATR per run; the coin flip is +0.0326. Both are indistinguishable from zero, which is the arithmetically correct answer and confirms the scoring is now sound. Trailing no longer helps -- the top rows carry no trail or a wide one. NO exit configuration in the 320-cell grid produces expectancy on this entry. Second clean negative of the day, per FP-50.
sessions.AND_THE_COST_COMPARISON_ENDS_IT: +0.0168 ATR per run is gross. On USDJPY M5 that is a small fraction of one pip, against round-trip costs of roughly one to two pips -- the same 19-41x cost-to-edge ratio this campaign measured before, arrived at independently.
sessions.I_ALSO_FIXED_MY_OWN_VERDICT_LOGIC: The null control had only two verdicts, artefact or real, so it labelled the corrected run an artefact when both arms were correctly near zero. A near-zero pair is neither -- it is the right answer. Three outcomes now, with a materiality floor, so a correct null is not mislabelled as a bug.
sessions.WHY_C4_IS_NOT_BEING_CALLED: Two clean negatives now exist -- entry conditions (Stage 1) and generic exits (this search) -- both control-validated. That is real evidence toward no-edge, but it is NOT the C4 decision, for three reasons stated plainly. First, RULE 12.1's question is still unanswered: which of TUNGSTEN's own ten exit rules closes each trade and how far it had travelled. That is built (WARRANT#359/#360) but needs a run, and the terminal is blocked. Second, this search used a SYNTHETIC entry (sign of agreement_score) and a simplified exit model, not TUNGSTEN's actual entries and not its ten rules -- so it answers 'is there a generic exit edge on this instrument', not 'is TUNGSTEN cutting its winners short'. Third, the detection floor is r >= 0.0435 and effects at 0.02-0.03 remain invisible at 3,410 effective runs. Calling no-edge on this would be claiming more than was measured.

sessions.WARRANT_365_TUNGSTEN_HAD_NEVER_BEEN_BACK: Three separate blockers, found in order. (1) My first launch used MT5-style config keys (Expert=, Symbol=), so the tester never started; MT4 requires TestExpert=, TestSymbol=, TestFromDate=. That launch instead auto-attached the EA to a live chart before the account had connected, failed Phase 0 on $0 equity, and ShutdownTerminal closed everything -- which is what Manuel saw. (2) The real tester run then failed check [04] 'history | 1001 bars | need 5,000+': MT4 hands the EA about a thousand bars at init and grows history as the test advances, while the same build on a live chart reports 65,000. (3) Then check [12], which requires StartingBalance >= AccountBalance()*0.1 -- impossible with a $100 base unit against a $10,000 tester deposit. Both guards are correct LIVE and wrong under test, so #365 relaxes them under IsTesting() only; live behaviour is bit-for-bit unchanged. Result: 'READY | 12/12 | all systems operational'. The EA had never once run in MT4's own engine, which is why every result this project holds comes from forward runs or the offline research layer, and why FINGERPRINT task 1 has had no data.
sessions.I_TOLD_MANUEL_A_WRONG_ROOT_CAUSE_AND_COR: I named the 5,000-bar guard as the cause of the FIRST failure before reading the log. It was not: that failure was on a live chart which reported 65,000 bars and failed on $0 equity. The bar guard was the cause of the SECOND failure, in the tester proper. Both facts are true and I stated them in the wrong order; corrected to Manuel in the same message that carried the finding.
sessions.THE_BACKTEST_ANSWERED_A_DIFFERENT_AND_BI: Over 8,395 scored bars across roughly 40 simulated days, TUNGSTEN opened ZERO trades. Measured from its own BAR-EVENT lines: |blended| median 13.9, p90 37.6, p99 59.5, max 77.1, against a threshold of 57 -- so 90 of 6,807 bars (1.32%) DID reach the entry threshold. The entry gate is therefore not the blocker. Something downstream rejected all ninety, and nothing in the log said what.
sessions.THE_SILENT_GATE: Traced from source. Entries funnel through ValidateFlexibleGates(isBuy, regime, scoreDistance, signalStrength, timingPass, opportunityPass); if it returns false, ExecuteHighFrequencySignal is never called and NOTHING is written. That function is 42 lines with ZERO TLog and ZERO Print calls and a single silent 'return false' on gate 1. So the single most consequential decision the EA makes -- whether a qualifying signal becomes a trade -- was the least observable thing in the entire 64,000-line build. Its structure: gate 1 (score distance) is always required and returns immediately; gates 2 (signal strength), 3 (timing) and 4 (opportunity) are counted against g_CustomGates[gateIndex].requiredGates.
sessions.WARRANT_366: Instruments it. A rate-limited GATE-REJECT line naming which gates failed with their inputs, a separate line for gate 1 (which returns before any tally and would otherwise stay invisible), and a periodic GATE-TALLY of how many signals reached the gates and which gate failed most. Rate-limited so a permanently closed gate cannot flood the log. Not yet compiled -- the tester holds the .ex4.
sessions.WHY_THIS_MATTERS_MORE_THAN_TASK_1: FINGERPRINT task 1 asks which exit rule closes each trade. That question presumes trades. This build opens none, so task 1 is not merely unanswered -- it is unanswerable until the entry gate is understood. RULE 12.1 ranks task 1 above everything; the honest amendment is that a prior question sits above it, and the backtest found it in under an hour after being impossible for the whole campaign.
sessions.CONSISTENT_WITH_EVERYTHING_ELSE_TODAY: The live run placed two pending orders in forty minutes and closed nothing. The build's own portal-audit measured the live scorer qualifying 1 bar in 500 against calibration's 132. The backtest now shows 1.32% of bars clearing the threshold and none surviving the gates. Three independent observations of the same thing: this system almost never trades, and until today nothing in it could say why.

sessions.type: ANSWERED: why TUNGSTEN does not trade. The EA's own REACHABILITY diagnostic says it plainly. My three-warrant instrumentation chase was unnecessary and I should have found this line first.
sessions.THE_ANSWER_IN_THE_EAS_OWN_WORDS: From the backtest log: 'REACHABILITY | UNREACHABLE: every regime threshold (min 50) exceeds the highest score the live scorer produced (7.1) -- this configuration cannot open a trade', followed by its human line 'This setup cannot place a trade at all. -- The entry bar is set higher than the scoring system can ever reach. -- This is the main thing to fix.' The entry bar sits roughly seven times above the maximum the scorer produced over the window.
sessions.WHY_MY_INSTRUMENTATION_NEVER_FIRED: WARRANT#366 (four flexible gates), #366b (probability gate), #367 (the entry comparison) and #368 (the ValidateExecution gate) all recorded ZERO hits across a full simulated month. That is consistent rather than contradictory: E99_ProcessExecutionDecisions returns at ValidateEdge or ValidateRisk long before any of them, because the score never approaches the threshold. Every one of those instruments is still worth having -- they are permanently silent decisions that now speak -- but none of them was the answer.
sessions.WHAT_I_SHOULD_HAVE_DONE: The REACHABILITY line existed in the build the whole time and appeared in BOTH runs today. In the live run it read 'max |score| observed 82.7 | regime thresholds 50-50' -- reachable. In the tester it read 7.1 against a minimum threshold of 50 -- unreachable. I read past it twice while tracing call chains through four levels of source. The correct order was to read what the system already says about itself before instrumenting what it does not.
sessions.A_CORRECTION_I_OWED_MANUEL: I reported '141 of 10,036 bars (1.40%) cleared the entry threshold of 57'. That was wrong. I compared g_LastBlendedScore, which the BAR-EVENT line prints and which is SIGNED -100..+100, against a threshold living in NORMALISED 0..100 space where 50 is neutral. engine.unifiedScore -- the value the entry actually tests -- is the normalised one, and its own initialiser says so at line 23536. Two different quantities. Corrected to him in the same message. This is the second time today I reasoned from a derived number instead of the variable the code actually uses; the first was the exit search's fake +0.54 ATR.
sessions.AND_A_NEW_NUMERIC_DEFECT: In the same block, Phase 3B prints its validation win rate as 'val -6483658065252796229739138252800.0%' -- about -6.5e30 percent -- repeatedly, across scan-wide, scan-mid, scan-fine, scan-ext, grids-done and both ascent passes for Strong Bull. A win rate is bounded 0-100 by definition, so this is an uninitialised or divide-by-zero path in the holdout validation, and every P3B decision downstream of it is being made against a meaningless number. Not yet fixed; recorded with its exact value.

sessions.type: WARRANT#370-373 via three parallel investigator agents. Two of my own claims corrected, one dangerous edit prevented, and the real explanation for the score collapse found.
sessions.WHY_THE_SCORER_COLLAPSES_THE_ACTUAL_MECH: The 7.1-vs-82.7 spread is not a scale mismatch. mtfScore alone is structurally never smaller than +-20, so a maximum |score| of 7.1 across thousands of bars can only be compression. The chain: the IC noise gate multiplies EVERY weight by (0.40 + 0.60*sqrt(|ic|/noiseFloor)), which floors at 0.40 when all ICs are near zero -- precisely the state 'all 9 regimes regularized, no per-regime edge' describes. Then totalScore is multiplied by seqMult, by ceusDamp (min 0.80), by bayesDamp (min 0.65) and by 0.92 in a contested value area, and finally normalised against a reference recomputed from the SAME attenuated weights. Compounded that is roughly 0.10 of raw. So the system throttles its own score BECAUSE it diagnosed no edge, and is then judged against a 50-point floor that assumes an un-throttled scorer. A self-reinforcing shutdown: the more certain it is that it has no edge, the less able it is to ever produce a score that could prove otherwise.
sessions.THE_REACHABILITY_VERDICT_IS_SOUND: I suspected the UNREACHABLE line might itself be a units bug comparing signed against normalised. It is not. It compares |CalculateEnhancedUnifiedScore| against g_RegimeOptimalThresholds, both signed-margin magnitudes, and that is IDENTICAL in form to the authoritative live entry gate. The verdict can be trusted.
sessions.CORRECTION_1_MY_INSTRUMENTATION_IS_IN_A_: WARRANT#366, #366b and #367 were placed at the buySignal/sellSignal assignment and the gates around it. That whole block is the LEGACY PRE-CALIBRATION path, made unreachable once calibration completes by 'if(_calibDone) return;' where _calibDone = isComplete && weightsOptimized && probabilityDatabaseBuilt. So their zero hits were not evidence about the gates at all -- nothing reached them because the block is skipped after calibration. The post-calibration entry gate is a different comparison entirely. The instruments are still correct and still worth keeping for pre-calibration runs, but I drew a conclusion from their silence that their placement could not support.
sessions.CORRECTION_2_THE_CHART_WAS_NEVER_STRIPPE: I reported that MT4 had stripped the EA from chart02.chr and that it must be restored before any live run. Wrong. The EA is attached, current and correct on chart03.chr -- MT4 renumbers chart0N.chr by window order on save, and the id field proves the same chart simply moved: chart03.chr carries the same id and comment as the older chart02 backups, with window_num incrementing monotonically across 33 backups. Worse, the file I saved as chart02.chr.bak_task1 carries chart01's id, which is where my 'the backup is also empty' conclusion came from -- I backed up the wrong file and then reasoned from it. Had I 'restored' the expert block into chart02.chr, both charts being USDJPY M5 and the block specifying MagicNumber 21001, the result would have been TWO concurrent SLS(181) instances on one symbol sharing one magic number: double calibration, double order flow, and mutual interference in every order loop that filters on OrderMagicNumber. The investigation prevented a genuinely harmful edit.
sessions.WARRANT_370_SAMPLE_FLOOR: The IC stage enforces n<500 citing Standing Prohibition #5, 'never update a weight from a cell with n<500'. The Phase 3B weight search gated at 50. The file's own history proves the contradiction: a systematic n>=500 sweep reached every other power gate -- session cell, volatility cell, Stage 4 threshold count, Stage 5 accept, final sparse guard -- and missed only the entry gates. CRITICALLY, there are TWO such gates and the bare 'if(barCount < 50) {' matches both, which is exactly the double match that refused an earlier edit today; and the SOFT path is the one that actually runs, because UseSoftMembershipFitting defaults to true, so fixing only the hard path would have changed nothing. Both raised to 500. Newly excluded: Range (~207 training bars) and Controlled Pullback (~102), plus Bullish Reversal and Building Momentum by inference from their 100.0% and 0.0% validation rates. Excluded regimes fall to the existing inheritance-or-neutral path, which is defined and safe.
sessions.WARRANT_370_BOUNDS_WERE_NOT_A_DEFECT: The 'weights outside 0.5-1.5' finding I recorded earlier was wrong as a defect. The real legal range for the six grid-searched fields is [0.05, 4.0], declared by WARRANT#112 and enforced inline at every stage; session 2.36/3.36, momentum 0.05 and volatility 2.50 are all IN bounds. One comment block was serving two different contracts -- 0.5-1.5 is correct for the older ghost-trade search fields and for currencyStrength, and was never right for the grid fields. Comment corrected, no behaviour changed. A genuine residual WAS found in the same sweep: one stage clamped to [0.30, 2.50] while every sibling used [0.05, 4.0], firing precisely on the weak regimes and undoing Stage 3.5's legitimate boundary extension. Fixed.
sessions.WARRANT_371_TESTER_SAFE_BUDGET: Every calibration budget is denominated in TimeCurrent(), which under the Strategy Tester is simulated time. CalibrationTimedOut() alone is the abort condition for roughly twenty long-running loop guards, so one line repairs all of them. TimeCurrent() is CORRECT for live and is left untouched there -- the per-regime durations recorded in this file (Strong Bull 738s) could only have been measured by a clock that advanced. A separate uint wall-clock anchor was added rather than re-basing calibrationStartTime, which has other consumers. Arithmetic kept in uint so it survives the 49.7-day wrap.
sessions.WARRANT_372_TWO_UNBRIDGED_UNIT_CROSSINGS: Found and fixed TOGETHER on purpose, because each alone moves the system in the opposite direction. (a) g_LiveAdaptive.liveOptimalThreshold, normalised 0..100, was blended straight into g_RegimeOptimalThresholds, signed-margin -- pulling the threshold up, then doubled by the 50+thr/2 bridge, so it could only ever suppress entries. (b) The mirror: g_CurrentThreshold, signed, was seeded straight into that same normalised field, which loosened the live gate. Fixing one without the other would have left the net direction unknown.
sessions.WARRANT_373_THE_MOST_MISLEADING_NUMBER_I: BAR-EVENT printed g_CurrentThreshold as 'thr='. That variable does not gate entries at all -- its only consumers are a boot-time seed that is overwritten every tick, and the ghost-mode gate. The value that decides an entry is g_RegimeOptimalThresholds[regime]. This is why three numbers (57, 28, 50) looked contradictory in one run: they were simply different variables, and the log was showing the one that matters least. Both are now printed, each labelled with whether it gates anything.
sessions.BOARD: 17 automated MET / 7 NOT MET / 6 ambiguous / 12 unautomated. WARRANT#330-373 shipped; eighteen clean compiles today, each verified by .ex4 mtime advancing AND being newer than the .mq4, deployed byte-identical to all three locations.
sessions.CRITICAL_PATH_next: Re-run the backtest on the fixed build and read the new gate_thr/cur_thr line. The 50.0 threshold floor is the real lever on tradeability, but the codebase carries an explicit evidence-backed decision NOT to lower it -- at a reachable threshold of 40 the measured bar-level expectancy is negative -- so lowering it converts a silent halt into a measured-negative-expectancy system. That is a decision for Manuel, not a defect to fix.

sessions.WARRANT_369_VALIDATED: Zero remaining garbage validation percentages. The '-6483658065252796229739138252800.0%' lines are gone; every P3B DONE line now carries a bounded number.
sessions.WARRANT_370_VALIDATED_AND_ITS_COST_IS_VI: All nine regimes now complete in 0s at 0.0% WR with budget 0% -- the 500-bar floor correctly excludes every regime in a ONE-MONTH window, because no regime accumulates 500 training bars in a month of M5. That is the exact risk the investigator flagged and it is working as designed, not a defect: on a full-history run the trending regimes sit in the thousands. It does mean a short backtest can no longer fit any weights at all, which is the honest consequence of refusing to fit six free parameters on ~100 bars.
sessions.WARRANT_373_NOT_YET_OBSERVED: No gate_thr= line appeared, because BAR-EVENT never fired in this run -- the window is consumed by calibration and its retries. Not evidence against the fix; simply unexercised.
sessions.C2_2_WAS_A_CHECKER_DEFECT_NOT_A_REGRESSI: The board showed C2.2 falling from MET to NOT MET after my edits, and my first instinct was that WARRANT#373's format-string change had broken it. It had not. The audit failed on DUPLICATES, and the duplicates were blocks 1-8 appearing three times because TUNGSTEN_live.log is APPEND-ONLY ACROSS SESSIONS: BLOCK 1 appears at 2026.08.31 23:42, 2026.09.02 19:06 and 2026.09.02 20:09, with eight EA INIT boundaries in one file. The checker audited the whole file as though it were one run.
sessions.AND_THE_CHECKER_ALREADY_KNEW: Its own docstring says 'a sequence audit across two runs is meaningless' -- but its only protection was a build-id check, which cannot separate two runs of the SAME build. Every run here is SLS(181). The stated intent was right and the implementation could not deliver it.
sessions.THE_FIX_AND_WHY_IT_IS_NOT_A_WEAKENING: The checker now segments on the EA INIT marker and audits the newest run that actually emitted blocks -- not the newest boundary, because that is often a failed or still-starting run whose emptiness would hide a real audit one run earlier. Within that run the sequence is CLEAN: starts at 1, no gaps, no duplicates, every block on the shipped build. The self-tests that plant a gap and a duplicate still pass 4/4, so a genuine defect inside a run still fails. The verdict is now PARTIAL RUN rather than MET, because no FULL run exists in the current log and the criterion says 'in a full run' -- the criterion is NOT awarded on a prefix.
sessions.WHAT_THIS_MEANS_FOR_THE_BOARD: C2.2 is not restored to MET and should not be. The honest state is that the sequence is sound within a run and no completed run is available to award on. Re-running the board after a full calibration completes is what would settle it.
