sessions.type: C2.1 EARNED -- 841 direct Print calls routed through the emitter. And the change blinded two checkers, producing a FALSE MET that I caught and reversed.
sessions.C2_1_EARNED: 843 call sites converted: 600 PrintFormat wrapped as TLog(StringFormat(...)), 224 Print passed straight through as TLog(...), and 19 multi-argument Print calls concatenated via StringConcatenate. Outside the emitter is now ZERO, down from 841. The criterion asks for zero and now gets it.
sessions.WHY_THIS_WAS_SAFE_WHERE_A_PAST_ATTEMPT_W: Every transformation is a PURE WRAP -- the format string is never edited and the argument list is never reordered or re-typed. That matters because a global replace earlier in this campaign edited 65 format strings when 9 were intended and broke 56 of them into runtime mismatches that compiled at 0 errors. A wrap cannot introduce a format/argument mismatch. The converter also balanced parentheses ACROSS NEWLINES: a first line-wise version silently skipped 301 multi-line calls and would have left the criterion unmet while appearing to succeed.
sessions.THE_COMPILER_CAUGHT_MY_ERROR: First apply produced 12 errors, all 'StringFormat - wrong parameters count': PrintFormat("a literal with no args") became StringFormat("...") with nothing to format, which MQL4 rejects. Restored from backup, taught the converter to pass single-argument calls straight through, re-applied, 0 errors. This is the compile-verify discipline earning its keep rather than a near miss.
sessions.COMPANION_CHANGE_THAT_WAS_NOT_OPTIONAL: TLog self-resets the log file at 5MB. Routing 843 more calls through it would have hit that mid-calibration and silently restarted the log -- destroying exactly what C2.2 audits (a FULL run in one file) and discarding the first half of any diagnosis. Ceiling raised to 25MB; the reset still exists so the file cannot grow without bound.
sessions.AND_THEN_IT_PRODUCED_A_FALSE_MET: The board after the conversion showed C3.1 flipping from NOT MET to MET. That was impossible on its face: C3.1 asks that every reported rate carry n AND realised net b, 94 sites lacked net b, and renaming Print to TLog cannot add net b to anything. The cause: rate_report_linter.py finds report sites by FUNCTION NAME, scanning for PrintFormat and Print. After the rename it found 1 site instead of 118, so 'lacking net b: 0' was vacuously true. A criterion passed because its instrument had gone blind.
sessions.AND_A_MIRROR_FALSE_FAIL: C5.6 flipped MET to NOT MET at the same moment, and announced itself: its verdict line said NOT MET while its own explanatory text still read 'so this is MET as written'. The detector was 'any("_rlLine" in l and "Print" in l)' -- the literal word Print. Verdict and reasoning disagreeing is the signature of an artefact rather than a finding.
sessions.BOTH_REPAIRED_AND_C3_1_IS_STRICTER_NOW: rate_report_linter.py now treats TLog and HLog as first-class report sites alongside Print/PrintFormat, so C2.1 and C3.1 can no longer trade against each other. C3.1 returned to NOT MET with 131 sites and 104 lacking net b -- MORE sites than the 118/94 it saw before, because the emitter calls it previously ignored are now counted. The repair made the criterion harder, not easier. C5.6 returned to MET with its verdict and reasoning agreeing again.
sessions.THE_RULE_THIS_EARNS: A criterion that flips in the same edit that could mechanically blind its checker is an artefact until proven otherwise. Check the DIRECTION of the flip against the change: C2.1 improving from a Print-to-TLog conversion is causal; C3.1 improving from it is impossible, because nothing about that rename supplies a realised net b. Impossible improvements are the ones to chase.
sessions.BOARD: Recomputed after the repairs. C2.1 genuinely earned; C2.2 honestly NOT MET (run-segmentation gives PARTIAL RUN, and the criterion is not awarded on a prefix); C3.1 correctly NOT MET; C5.6 correctly MET.

sessions.type: FOUR INSTRUMENTS WERE MEASURING THE WRAPPER, A COMMENT, AN INDEX, AND NOTHING AT ALL. Plus two recorded fixes that never ran, one of them disabled by a single invisible byte.
sessions.HOW_THIS_STARTED: Session 126 repaired rate_report_linter.py after the Print-to-TLog conversion blinded it, and recorded the rule: a criterion that flips in the same edit that could blind its checker is an artefact until proven otherwise. That repair was applied to ONE of the three instruments that find rate-reporting sites. This session checked the other two and found them still blind -- and then found three further defects underneath.

WARRANT_375_THE_SITE_FINDER_IS_NOW_ONE_D.what: mql_source.py: shared newest_build / blank_comments / find_calls / report_sites, imported by rate_report_linter.py, c31_site_analysis.py and c32_floor_guard_audit.py. Self-tested at import; refuses to load rather than load wrong.
WARRANT_375_THE_SITE_FINDER_IS_NOW_ONE_D.defect_1_name_blindness: c31_site_analysis.py and c32_floor_guard_audit.py still searched only for PrintFormat and Print. After WARRANT#374 routed 843 calls through TLog, c32 audited ONE site in a 65,000-line build and c31 audited ZERO. C3.2's stored NOT MET verdict rested entirely on that single site.
WARRANT_375_THE_SITE_FINDER_IS_NOW_ONE_D.defect_2_comment_blindness: That single site was a COMMENTED-OUT PrintFormat at line 22960 -- '// regime in flux: handled by PULSE (was per-tick noise) // PrintFormat(...)'. Silenced code, inside a comment, graded as a live unguarded rate report. C3.2 was failing on dead text. Measured exactly: 131 sites in raw text, 130 live, the difference being that one line.
WARRANT_375_THE_SITE_FINDER_IS_NOW_ONE_D.defect_3_string_blindness: The paren matcher counted brackets inside string literals, so a message containing ':)' or '(see below' could truncate or overrun its own call. Fixed with a string-aware scanner.
WARRANT_375_THE_SITE_FINDER_IS_NOW_ONE_D.defect_4_the_wrapper_was_being_measured: WARRANT#374's conversion was a pure wrap: PrintFormat(fmt, args) became TLog(StringFormat(fmt, args)). Every downstream instrument reads a call's arguments as 'format string first, then its arguments', which the wrap makes false -- argument zero is now the text 'StringFormat(...'. 64 of 130 sites came back UNKNOWN for that reason alone. unwrap_emitter() unwraps StringFormat when it IS the whole argument, and leaves StringConcatenate and multi-argument calls alone.

WARRANT_376_THE_GUARD_MATCHER_WAS_CREDIT.defect_5_array_indices_counted_as_sample: base_name() extracted every identifier in a denominator expression, INCLUDING the array subscript. For g_RegimeCorrelations[_pr2].signalTotal it returned {g_RegimeCorrelations, _pr2, signalTotal}, so any enclosing 'for(_pr2 = 0; _pr2 < 9; ...)' satisfied the floor test. Three sites were GUARDED on bounds checks reading 'ba<0', 'hour<0' and 'regime<0' -- index sanity checks credited as sample-size floors.
WARRANT_376_THE_GUARD_MATCHER_WAS_CREDIT.defect_6_the_struct_matched_instead_of_t: After stripping subscripts the dotted path was still split, leaving the CONTAINER in the name set. A guard on g_RegimeCorrelations[_dr].compSampleN then matched a rate whose denominator was g_RegimeCorrelations[_pr2].signalTotal -- different field, different element. Six more GUARDED verdicts were resting on this. The name kept is now the whole member path.
WARRANT_376_THE_GUARD_MATCHER_WAS_CREDIT.defect_7_braceless_guards_were_invisible: enclosing_conditions() recovers blocks by brace matching and is therefore structurally incapable of seeing 'if(cond)' followed by a single unbraced statement -- the commonest guard shape in this build. Line 6330 is genuinely gated by 'if(...signalTotal>=30)' one line above and the audit could not see it; it had been passing that site for the WRONG reason (the loop index) and would have failed it once that was fixed. braceless_guards() added for both the preceding-line and same-line forms.
WARRANT_376_THE_GUARD_MATCHER_WAS_CREDIT.defect_8_declared_counts_in_the_middle_o: WARRANT#253 trusted a DECLARED count over an inferred one, but only recognised the declaration in one position: a trailing '(int)(EXPR)'. Most of this build declares it inline -- 'WR %.0f%% (%dT)', '%d trades | WR %.1f%%'. count_arg() recognises those, filtered three ways so it cannot invent a denominator: the label must be a sample-size unit, must not be a budget word (until/min/need/remaining), and the credited argument must itself be count-shaped. 33 sites credited, each listed with the exact text that justified it.
WARRANT_376_THE_GUARD_MATCHER_WAS_CREDIT.new_class_FIXED_N: Six sites divide by a numeric LITERAL (30, 30, 30, 60, 60, 60) and were graded UNKNOWN, i.e. 'population could not be determined', when the source states it outright. Checked by hand against the three computations behind them: 28186 sits under 'tradesSinceRecal < 50 return' with a MathMin(totalTrades,30) loop, 28252 under 'totalTrades < 30 return' with a fixed 30-iteration loop, 30876 under 'totalTrades < 100 return' with MathMin(totalTrades,60). All three constants are exact. NOT folded into GUARDED: a constant 30 cannot fall below a floor, but it also does not clear one derived at 1,309.
WARRANT_376_THE_GUARD_MATCHER_WAS_CREDIT.defect_9_a_dead_regex_branch: COUNT_WORD_ANY contained a stray 0x08 byte between 'obs' and the following '|', so the 'obs' alternative could only match text containing a literal backspace -- it has never matched anything. Found by reading the bytes, invisible in any editor. Also added the bare 'n %d' idiom, adjacency-strict, which line 44834 uses.

WARRANT_377_THE_VERIFIER_THAT_WAS_NAMED_.context: Session 55 held back the C3.2 enforcement decision because StringFormat and PrintFormat are variadic: a format asking for four values and handed three compiles at 0 errors and prints garbage. The campaign has been burnt by this once, when a global replace broke 56 format strings that all compiled clean. The stated prerequisite was a verifier checking every conversion specifier against its argument. It did not exist.
WARRANT_377_THE_VERIFIER_THAT_WAS_NAMED_.built: format_arity_check.py. Arity is exact (%% consumes nothing, %*d and %.*f each consume an extra int, adjacent string literals are concatenated). Type checking is deliberately NARROW -- only arguments whose type is unambiguous from the text (literal, explicit cast, string-returning built-in); everything else is reported UNCHECKED rather than guessed. Self-tests plant one mismatch of each kind and require both to be caught.
WARRANT_377_THE_VERIFIER_THAT_WAS_NAMED_.result: 1,191 calls with a literal format string checked, 8 not statically checkable, 0 findings. The build is clean, and the blocker on the C3.2 enforcement decision is now removed.

sessions.AUTHORISATION: Manuel: 'finish stop waiting'. Taken, as at session 55, as authority to proceed on the pending decisions with the recommendations already on record -- option (b) for C3.2, and a bar-label consumer for C6.1 that measures and reports without touching live decisions.

WARRANT_379_C3_2_ENFORCEMENT_SHIPPED.the_decision: Option (b): withhold the RATE below the derived floor, print the COUNT and the floor, so the line survives and says why it is silent.
WARRANT_379_C3_2_ENFORCEMENT_SHIPPED.the_floor: C3_RATE_FLOOR_N = 1309, derived by research_layer/rate_floor.py from this build's own constants -- P3B's 2.5/1.5 ATR bracket gives RR 1.6667, SpecBreakevenWR gives 0.3750, P6's 0.10R quarantine floor gives a minimum tradeable 0.4125, so the edge to detect is 0.0375 at 95/80. Every floor the codebase actually used was at or below 500, where the 95% interval is still +/-0.043 and cannot separate a barely-tradeable edge from break-even.
WARRANT_379_C3_2_ENFORCEMENT_SHIPPED.why_an_accessor: WRStr(ratePct, n, digits) rather than 130 separate guards. A guard has to be written correctly at every site and rechecked whenever the site moves; the accessor cannot be got wrong at a call site because the call site no longer decides, and it FAILS SAFE -- a site that passes no real count passes 0 and its rate is withheld.
WARRANT_379_C3_2_ENFORCEMENT_SHIPPED.the_prerequisite_that_now_exists: Session 55 refused this exact transformation because StringFormat is variadic: converting a %f to a %s and passing a string is not a compile error, it prints garbage. format_arity_check.py (WARRANT#377, built earlier today) is that verifier. It was not decoration -- see below.
WARRANT_379_C3_2_ENFORCEMENT_SHIPPED.first_apply_failed_and_that_was_the_syst: 10 compile errors. Two causes, both the same mistake: assuming something about a call site that had not been checked. (1) Rebuilding a multi-line call onto one line moved a trailing // comment into the middle of the argument list. (2) A TRACED denominator was handed to the compiler as _dd2, declared in a nested scope. Reverted whole, then narrowed to sites whose denominator the call ALREADY PASSES as one of its own arguments -- provably in scope by construction -- plus numeric literals. 104 sites converted, 0 errors, 0 warnings.
WARRANT_379_C3_2_ENFORCEMENT_SHIPPED.and_then_it_blinded_my_own_instruments: Converting 'WR %.1f%%' to 'WR %s' meant RATE_TOKEN no longer matched: the site count fell 130 -> 27 and C3.1's 'lacking net b' fell 100 -> 23 in the same instant. That is the session-126 vacuous-improvement pattern, caused this time by my own edit. RATE_TOKEN now treats WRStr as a first-class rate site, and rate_report_linter imports it instead of keeping a third copy. Site count back to 130, lacking net b back to 100 -- the check that proves nothing was bought.

WARRANT_380_C6_1_EARNED.what_was_wrong: 50,000 bars scored and labelled with realised outcomes, and nothing in 65,000 lines had ever read the file back. C6.1's checker called it 'letter met, intent not met' and was right: the record existed only for offline analysis while the LEARNER stayed blind to its own counterfactual.
WARRANT_380_C6_1_EARNED.built: LoadHistoricalScoreLabels() -- reads the export, resolves its column indices FROM THE HEADER rather than by assumption, and accumulates would-trade versus declined outcomes at four thresholds. Called immediately after RunHistoricalScoreExport and deliberately OUTSIDE it: WARRANT#309 already had to unwind a criterion that passed because a self-copy routine was counted as a consumer.

THE_VERIFIER_CAUGHT_THREE_BUGS_ON_ITS_FI.two_of_them_mine: WARRANT#382 and #383 each changed an ARGUMENT to WRStr(...) and left the format string reading %.1f%% or %.0f%%. THE_VERIFIER_CAUGHT_THREE_BUGS_ON_ITS_FI.one_of_them_pre_existing_WARRANT_384: The APEX status heartbeat chose between TWO format strings with a ternary and fed both ONE argument list. It compiled clean and has done for as long as it has existed. format_arity_check could NOT catch this one: a ternary format is not a literal, so it lands in the 'not statically checkable' bucket the verifier REPORTS rather than hides -- and reporting it is what led to reading the site. C1_1_ROOT_CAUSE_IS_NOT_THE_MUTATIONS.the_real_count: 45 mutations, not the 54 carried in prose: 33 additive, 6 multiplicative, 4 clamps, 2 whole-score replacements, plus 5 terminal statements and 2 twin-only writes CEUS lacks.
C1_1_ROOT_CAUSE_IS_NOT_THE_MUTATIONS.the_actual_cause: CEUS ends with a rescale the twin has no counterpart for -- _norm = totalScore * (88.0/_refMax), which at the weights in force is 88/169 = 0.5207. Counterfactuals over 49,999 exported bars: as shipped the mean gap is 18.36; making the twin apply all 45 mutations makes it WORSE at 18.99 (the mutations push WITH the signal at mean +0.94 while the rescale shrinks it -- they were partially cancelling); making the twin apply the RESCALE cuts it to 4.31, a 77% reduction. K is identified from the data, not assumed: 6.45% of bars land exactly on one of the four ratios K x {0.82, 1.00, 1.10, 1.25} against 0.96% by chance.
C1_1_ROOT_CAUSE_IS_NOT_THE_MUTATIONS.and_it_is_the_trade_suppression_mechanis: Calibration fits thresholds on the twin's scale; live applies them to CEUS's half-scale output. At signed threshold 55 the twin qualifies 26.5% of bars and live qualifies 1.3% -- reproducing the portal audit's 132-vs-1 from the scale factor alone. The build's own portal audit has been LOGGING that ratio ('mean |enhanced|/|linear| 0.616') on the same line as the collapse for a month without naming it.
C1_1_ROOT_CAUSE_IS_NOT_THE_MUTATIONS.recommendation: (b) extract CEUS's tail into a shared helper both call, behind ScorerIdentityNormalise defaulting OFF, the WARRANT#226 pattern -- about 25 lines. It breaks every stored threshold (fitted on the unnormalised scale, wrong by ~1.9x TOWARD TRADING MORE), so it cannot ship without a recalibration. (a) is rejected on measurement: 22 of the 45 mutations are shift==0-only and are not well-defined in a scorer that scans bars out of order.

WARRANT_394_THE_SELECTION_TEST.question: Do the bars this system would TAKE resolve better than the ones it declines?
WARRANT_394_THE_SELECTION_TEST.method: Welch plus a 20,000-iteration permutation test on mean R, with a null control (score replaced by a coin flip: p=0.4724, no effect found) and a planted control (+0.10R added to taken bars: recovered at gap +0.0856, p=0.0002). The script refuses to print a verdict if either control fails.
WARRANT_394_THE_SELECTION_TEST.result: thr 28 gap -0.0144 p=0.286 | thr 40 +0.0050 p=0.823 | thr 55 +0.0406 p=0.451 | thr 70 +0.0601 p=0.688. At NO threshold does selection differ from declining by more than chance.
WARRANT_394_THE_SELECTION_TEST.reading: The filter is not selecting -- neither for nor against. Every bucket has negative expectancy, so this measures SELECTION, not viability. The apparent inversion at thr 28 does not survive a permutation test, and saying so is the result.

THE_ENTRY_CHAIN_QUESTION_IS_CLOSED.how_it_was_run_down: WARRANT#413 instrumented gates 2 and 3 (ValidateEdge, ValidateRisk) after the tester measured EXEC-BLOCKED = 0 AND EXEC-PASSED = 0 -- both zero means the bar never ARRIVED, not that the gate rejected it. Those two also measured zero. WARRANT#414 instrumented the silent decision-rate limiter. Zero. Then the beehive block message: zero. So E99_ProcessExecutionDecisions was never CALLED. Then the two log emitters immediately above its call site -- LogSafeguardsStatus and LogMarketNarrative -- also produce zero output while REGIME (1867) and LIVE (799) produce plenty, which localised the return to a narrow band of OnTick.
THE_ENTRY_CHAIN_QUESTION_IS_CLOSED.THE_ANSWER: Line 58286: `if(g_Calibration.executionSuspended) { ...manage existing positions...; return; }  // never open new trades while suspended`. All three tester windows ended STAND DOWN (OVERFIT, MIXED, EXECUTION-COST) and window 3 set the flag explicitly: 'P6 | edge -0.16R, PF 0.68 -- below viability | live execution suspended | ghost observation only'.
THE_ENTRY_CHAIN_QUESTION_IS_CLOSED.what_it_means: THIS IS NOT A DEFECT. The entry path is never reached because the system measured no edge and refused to trade, exactly as designed. WARRANT_426_427_THE_CLAIM_TESTED.why_every_prior_result_could_not_see_it: Stage 1's ten families, the 320-exit search, the per-regime component ICs and WARRANT#394's taken-vs-declined test were ALL computed on `r_continuous` -- the realised R under ONE fixed bracket. WARRANT_426_427_THE_CLAIM_TESTED.AND_MY_FIRST_VERSION_OF_THE_TEST_WAS_WRO: It counted a win whenever MFE >= TP and the MAXIMUM-excursion bar index was earlier, treating the bar of the maximum as the bar the level was first crossed. Those are different things: with a 0.4 ATR stop against a median MAE of 1.63, a trade stopped out in bar one still scored a win. The result was +0.23945 and it was hindsight.
WARRANT_426_427_THE_CLAIM_TESTED.the_control_caught_it_and_my_pass_rule_n: The sign-flip control returned +0.22607 for the INVERTED trade against +0.23945 forward -- the same number twice. My pass rule was 'flip < forward', which a 6% gap satisfies. A 6% gap is not a directional edge. The rule is now: the inverted trade must be unprofitable, or earn less than a third of the forward one.
WARRANT_426_427_THE_CLAIM_TESTED.the_conservative_reconstruction: The export records MAXIMA and the bars they occurred on, not first-crossing times, so for any stop below the observed MAE the ordering is unknowable. The only honest reconstruction is a lower bound: a win requires MFE >= TP AND MAE NEVER reaching SL (no ordering assumption needed); anything touching SL is charged as a loss even if TP was also reached. This UNDER-counts wins, which is the correct direction to be wrong in.

WARRANT_428_IT_SURVIVES_OUT_OF_SAMPLE.method: Chronological splits with a 180-bar embargo at each boundary. Bracket chosen on the training portion only, scored unchanged on the held-out portion. Six folds: 50/50, 70/30, and four expanding-window walk-forwards.
WARRANT_428_IT_SURVIVES_OUT_OF_SAMPLE.result: Positive on EVERY fold. min +0.15157, median +0.17498, max +0.23581. In-sample median +0.20908, so shrinkage is only -0.034 -- modest and healthy.
WARRANT_428_IT_SURVIVES_OUT_OF_SAMPLE.and_the_geometry_is_stable: All six folds independently chose TP 2.5 ATR / SL 2.0 ATR. A grid fitting noise does not agree with itself six times.
WARRANT_428_IT_SURVIVES_OUT_OF_SAMPLE.the_uncomfortable_half: The SCORE adds nothing. Median out-of-sample lift from requiring |score| >= 28 is +0.00944 on a +0.32 base. The edge is in the EXIT GEOMETRY, not in the entry signal this project has spent its entire life calibrating. That is consistent with every no-edge result ever measured here -- those results were about the SIGNAL and they were right.

WARRANT_429_AND_THEN_THE_SPREAD_TAKES_IT.the_arithmetic: Risk is measured in R and R is the stop distance. Median M5 ATR on USDJPY is 0.04150, so a 2.0 ATR stop is 0.083 in price -- about 8.3 pips. At the tester's configured 20 points (0.020) the spread is 0.257 R PER TRADE, against an edge of 0.175 R.
WARRANT_429_AND_THEN_THE_SPREAD_TAKES_IT.measured: 20 points: in-sample +0.01225, out of sample -0.11648. 25 points: -0.03266 / -0.18453. 35 points: -0.12248 / -0.32064. Cost was charged per bar using that bar's own ATR, and the bracket search was re-run WITH cost in it, because cost is fixed in price and therefore systematically favours wider stops -- selecting without cost and charging afterwards would understate what is achievable.
WARRANT_429_AND_THEN_THE_SPREAD_TAKES_IT.verdict: The edge does not survive costs on M5. The pre-cost result is real and irrelevant at this bar size.

WARRANT_430_THE_REFRAME_THAT_MATTERS.the_distinction: An ABSENT edge means the signal is worthless. An edge BELOW COSTS means the signal is fine and the ARENA is wrong. This is the second, and it is a different problem with a different solution.
WARRANT_430_THE_REFRAME_THAT_MATTERS.the_derivation: cost_R = spread / (SL x ATR). The spread is fixed in price; ATR is not, and scales roughly with the square root of bar duration. Requiring the edge to be at least TWICE the cost: at 20 points the needed ATR is 0.11430, which is 2.75x the M5 median and implies bars of about 38 minutes.
WARRANT_430_THE_REFRAME_THAT_MATTERS.the_table: At 20 points -- M5 cost 0.241 R net -0.066 (negative) | M15 cost 0.139 net +0.036 | M30 cost 0.098 net +0.077 | H1 cost 0.070 net +0.105 (clears with margin) | H4 net +0.140 | D1 net +0.161. At 25 points H1 is still the first to clear with margin.
WARRANT_430_THE_REFRAME_THAT_MATTERS.the_recommendation: H1. It is the first standard timeframe where the toll stops dominating at both realistic spread assumptions.
WARRANT_430_THE_REFRAME_THAT_MATTERS.stated_as_a_requirement_not_a_prediction: The edge's MAGNITUDE was measured on M5 bars. Whether an excursion asymmetry of the same size exists on H1 is an open question -- longer bars mean fewer trades, different microstructure, possibly a different asymmetry or none. What the arithmetic establishes is that M5 CANNOT work at this spread however good the signal is, and where to look next.
WARRANT_430_THE_REFRAME_THAT_MATTERS.the_test: Re-export at M15 and H1 and re-run WARRANT#428's folds. RunHistoricalScoreExport produces the export and the tester config takes a TestPeriod key -- this needs a config change and a run, not new code.

WHAT_THIS_CHANGES_ABOUT_THE_PROJECT.1: The standing no-edge conclusion is CORRECT ABOUT THE SIGNAL and was never about the exit. Both halves can be true at once and they are.
WHAT_THIS_CHANGES_ABOUT_THE_PROJECT.2: The shipped bracket is not merely suboptimal -- it INVERTS a positive quantity into a negative one, -0.060 against +0.175 on the same bars. That is the single largest measured defect in the build.
WHAT_THIS_CHANGES_ABOUT_THE_PROJECT.3: Calibration has been searching entry weights and thresholds. The measured edge is in exit geometry, which calibration does not search in this way. That is a strategy-level misallocation, not a bug.
WHAT_THIS_CHANGES_ABOUT_THE_PROJECT.4: M5 was never viable at this spread. Every result this project has produced was measured inside an arena where the toll exceeds the prize.

NEXT: 1. Real exports at M15 / M30 / H1 are running -- they replace the sqrt-scaled ATR estimate with measurement, and WARRANT#428's fold machinery then runs unchanged on each.
2. If the excursion asymmetry holds at M30 after real costs, the exit geometry becomes the thing to calibrate and the entry score becomes a filter that must justify itself rather than be assumed.
3. If it does not, the asymmetry is an M5 microstructure artefact that does not generalise -- also worth knowing, and it closes the question.
4. Agents running on C6.3/C6.4 (learning reframed as measurable discrimination) and C1.5/C8.4/C8.6.

RULES_EARNED.A_CONTROL_IS_ONLY_AS_GOOD_AS_ITS_PASS_RU: The sign-flip control produced exactly the right number -- the inverted trade earning the same as the forward one -- and my threshold let it pass anyway. Design the pass rule to fail the thing you are afraid of, not merely to compare.
RULES_EARNED.AN_EDGE_BELOW_COSTS_IS_NOT_AN_ABSENT_EDG: They demand opposite responses: one says abandon the signal, the other says change the arena. Conflating them would have thrown away a real result.
RULES_EARNED.MEASURE_THE_PATH_NOT_ONLY_THE_VERDICT: A fixed bracket is a lossy summary of what a trade did. Four columns describing the run had sat unused in every export this project ever produced.

sessions.NEXT_SENTENCE: The signal was never the problem and the exit always was, and both facts were sitting in the same file the whole time.

WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.his_words: 'we shouldnt be limited to h1, m15 and m39 works well enough'
WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.what_I_got_wrong: WARRANT#430 recommended H1 on two errors. FIRST, it ranked timeframes by R PER TRADE and ignored frequency -- a timeframe with half the edge and four times the trades earns more. This is the IDENTICAL mistake WARRANT#415 had corrected for entry gates two days earlier ('a gate that doubles expectancy while cutting frequency by 90% is a bad gate'), and the lesson was not carried across a different problem. SECOND, it imposed a 'clears with margin' bar meaning net >= edge/2, a factor chosen in that script and nowhere derived, then reported M15 and M30 as merely 'positive' and effectively dismissed them. They were positive. Positive with four times and twice the trade count is a LARGER result, not a lesser one.
WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.the_corrected_ranking_at_20_points: R per day = net R x trades per day. M5 -11.351 (negative net, excluded). M15 +2.056. M30 +2.196. H1 +1.511. H4 +0.502. D1 +0.096. With a 3-position concurrency cap the ordering is unchanged: M30 +1.547, M15 +1.449, H1 +1.065.
WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.at_25_points_the_picture_sharpens: M30 +1.491 and H1 +1.262 hold, but M15 collapses to +0.062 -- its per-trade net falls to +0.0011, so it is almost entirely spread-sensitive. M30 is therefore the ROBUST choice and M15 the fragile one, which per-trade ranking could not have shown either.
WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.conclusion: M30 first, M15 second, H1 as a control. M5 stays excluded -- not by any margin rule but because its net after cost is NEGATIVE at every spread level tested.
WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.the_limits_carried_forward: ATR at other timeframes is EXTRAPOLATED from M5 by sqrt(duration); the 60.2% live-trade share is assumed constant; and trades are assumed takeable, which at M5's 172/day is plainly false and is why a concurrency cap is reported alongside. Real exports at M15/M30/H1 were launched to replace the extrapolation with measurement.
WARRANT_431_MANUEL_CORRECTED_MY_RECOMMEN.rule_earned: RANK BY WHAT THE ACCOUNT ACCUMULATES, NOT BY WHAT ONE TRADE EARNS -- and when a lesson has already been learned on one problem, check whether the next problem is the same shape. It was, and I missed it.

sessions.type: RETRACTION. The path edge of session 132 was an artefact of a truncated column, and I found it by disagreeing with myself. Plus WARRANT#434: two more criteria that were failing because their CHECKERS were wrong.

THE_RETRACTION.what_was_claimed: Session 132 (WARRANT#426-431) reported that reconstructing outcomes from each trade's excursion path turned -0.05999 R into +0.19188 R, surviving out of sample on 6 of 6 folds at a stable TP2.5/SL2.0 geometry, with a sign-flip control at -0.25858. It was reported to Manuel as the most important result of the campaign.
THE_RETRACTION.how_it_was_caught: Two instruments computing the same quantity and disagreeing. A recomputation of MFE/MAE from raw highs and lows over a full 20-bar window gave the OPPOSITE SIGN from the export's own columns at the same timeframe on the same bars. The diagnostic that settled it: at a 10-bar window my medians matched the export's (1.310 vs 1.340) while at the export's stated 20-bar horizon they did not (1.863 vs 1.340) -- the export's excursions correspond to roughly half its own horizon, which is exactly what an early break produces. Correlation between the two was 0.709, not 1.0, so the definitions differ materially rather than by a scale factor.
THE_RETRACTION.the_untruncated_numbers: Best bracket per timeframe over a full 20-bar path, BEFORE costs: M5 TP2.5/SL2.5 -0.09945 | M15 TP2.5/SL2.5 -0.13849 | M30 TP2.5/SL2.5 -0.10047 | H1 TP2.0/SL2.5 -0.09948. The SHIPPED bracket earns -0.05999 on the same bars. NO BRACKET BEATS THE SHIPPED ONE AT ANY TIMEFRAME, before costs are even charged.
THE_RETRACTION.what_this_voids: WARRANT#426, #427, #428 (the out-of-sample folds), #429 (the cost analysis), #430 (the H1 recommendation) and #431 (the M30 correction of it) all rest on those columns and are VOID. The 6-of-6 fold agreement and the stable geometry were real properties of a truncated dataset, which is precisely why fold agreement is not proof of anything if the underlying measurement is wrong.
THE_RETRACTION.what_survives: The score's DIRECTION carries information -- direction equals sign(score) on 99.80% of bars, and inverting it made every version of the test sharply worse. Its MAGNITUDE does not: requiring |score| >= 28 lifted +0.00944. That distinction is independent of the truncation and is consistent with WARRANT#415's finding that no entry gate on |score| beats a random gate of equal selectivity. Keep the direction; stop believing the confidence.
THE_RETRACTION.and_manuels_claim_is_UNTESTED_not_refute: 'Edge is per trade run' remains the right question. The data used to test it cannot answer it, because the only record of the run is truncated by the exit being questioned. A real test needs excursions tracked to a FIXED horizon regardless of resolution -- a small EA change: keep the resolution loop and its break, but let the MFE/MAE tracking continue the full 20 bars alongside it rather than sharing the break.

THE_LESSON.rule: READ HOW A COLUMN IS COMPUTED BEFORE BUILDING A CONCLUSION ON IT. Four columns were used across six warrants and two sessions without anyone reading the fifteen lines that produce them.
THE_LESSON.why_the_controls_did_not_save_me: The sign-flip and null-selection controls both PASSED, and both were correct -- they test whether a result is directional and whether selection is real. Neither can detect that the INPUT is a truncated measurement, because both operate on the same truncated input. A control validates an inference; it cannot validate a measurement. That needs a second instrument computing the same quantity a different way, which is what eventually caught it.
THE_LESSON.what_worked: The habit of recomputing a quantity independently rather than accepting it. It cost one extra instrument and it overturned a two-session headline.

WARRANT_434_TWO_MORE_CHECKER_DEFECTS.C8_4_now_MET_with_zero_build_edits: The two 'illegible' fault sites were correct all along. HLog renders `decided + ' -- ' + why + ' -- ' + meaning`, and ' -- ' is one of the checker's own separators -- but the checker built the string it graded by pulling every literal out of the call and JOINING THEM WITH A SPACE, collapsing a three-field human line into one field. Both lines sit in the retained tester log rendered correctly with their separators, naming subject and consequence. Rewriting them would have DEGRADED two correct lines to satisfy a broken test. The checker now composes each emitter's arguments the way that emitter composes them; site set identical at 89, zero legible->illegible flips, and STRICTER in one place (LB_Human's machine-side derivation can no longer lend a consequence to its human line). Self-tests 7 -> 11.
WARRANT_434_TWO_MORE_CHECKER_DEFECTS.C1_5_the_orphaned_count_measured_the_wro: It graded ORPHANED as 'reaches a log, no decision'. C1's own closing sentence says 'reaches a consumer OR A LOG', and telemetry_integrity_scan.py -- the very artefact C1.5's evidence column names -- had already settled this in WARRANT#261: 'log-only is NOT orphaned under the document's own definition'. WARRANT#377 fixed its predecessor's blindness and silently re-adopted the definition #261 had rejected. Corrected, and CRUCIALLY the correction does not flip the board on its own -- a self-test asserts grade(18,29) must still fail. That is the test of a correction rather than a convenience.
WARRANT_434_TWO_MORE_CHECKER_DEFECTS.C1_5_the_real_work: Silent computations 18 -> 5. Thirteen wired across 11 edits. Highest value: g_RegimePBOEstimateSamples -- the FORGE scorecard printed a PBO estimate WITH NO n, and that number feeds ForgeRatchetPromote's promotion bar; the sample size was in a global written at both PBO sites and read by nobody. Five named for deletion rather than wiring, all checked against Save/LoadSystemState for positional file I/O: g_MetricsCount (only write is = 0), g_CatastrophicReasonCode (duplicate of text already logged), g_TimeOffsetDetected (unread AND wrong -- set true even on the path where detection FAILED and fell back to hard-coded UTC+2), g_LastRecalibrationCheck, g_BlendCalibrated.
WARRANT_434_TWO_MORE_CHECKER_DEFECTS.C8_6: One of three closed structurally. The expected-worst-streak formula was REJECTED because it needs a win rate and this build has none above its own floor (n = 0, 1, 4 against C3_RATE_FLOOR_N 1309) -- that would have been the invented number. Instead the ghost validator already walks a non-overlapping OOS path at live thresholds and brackets and calls it 'the honest equity curve', then throws the shape away. Five edits keep the shape: deepest peak-to-trough in R, each move divided by ITS OWN stop distance (the price-vs-equity unit trap), withheld below FLOOR_GHOST_MIN_TRADES -- and the withheld line deliberately OMITS the phrase the C8.6 locator keys on, so a sentinel can never pass as a measurement. Forecast sites 0 -> 4. The other two facts need a live run and data respectively.

sessions.type: THE MEASUREMENT WAS ASKING THE WRONG QUESTION. Manuel reframed edge as skill-at-reading-the-moment rather than average-over-all-moments, and under the corrected framing the opportunity is large, measured for the first time, and almost entirely unread.

MANUELS_CORRECTION.his_words: there are genuinely good trading moments within history runs with various bar counts per regimes, the edge lies in reading when these moments are and the conditions that took place during them cross correlated to all available intel we had indicators included ... we are reporting how good it becomes at that as edge not edge as an overall sum of all our losses plus wins
MANUELS_CORRECTION.why_he_is_right: Every number this campaign has produced -- the -0.041 net, the 27x cost gap, the fair-win-rate excesses -- is mean R over ALL BARS. That quantity is near zero BY CONSTRUCTION because it averages the good moments into the overwhelming majority of bars that are noise. Reporting it as 'there is no edge' was a category error: it measures the market, not the ability to read the market.
MANUELS_CORRECTION.the_replacement_metric: capture = (model_topk - base) / (oracle_topk - base). 0% = no skill, 100% = perfect foresight. Trainable, watchable across attempts, and the only framing under which 'trial and error until unimaginably good' has a scoreboard.

WARRANT_442_ENTRY_SELECTION_SKILL.ceiling_floor_capture: CEILING (best 10% of moments with perfect foresight) +1.44980 R/trade. FLOOR (take every moment) -0.47160 R. The gap of 1.92 R is the first honest measurement of headroom this project has made -- nobody had ever computed the oracle, so no capture ratio had a denominator.
WARRANT_442_ENTRY_SELECTION_SKILL.what_the_build_reads: CAPTURE 2.3%, out-of-sample AUC 0.5252 on 41 no-lookahead features, gradient boosting, chronological split with a 3x-median-span embargo.
WARRANT_442_ENTRY_SELECTION_SKILL.the_control_that_matters: A model trained on SHUFFLED LABELS also scored ~2% capture (AUC 0.4966). So the honest statement is NOT '2.3% skill' -- it is 'reading skill is not yet distinguishable from zero'. Reported that way to Manuel rather than as a positive.
WARRANT_442_ENTRY_SELECTION_SKILL.what_it_would_take: At TP2.5/SL1.5 the fair win rate is 37.5% and cost is 0.31 R, so the reader must reach 49.2% -- a +11.7 percentage point lift. Current lift is under one point.
WARRANT_442_ENTRY_SELECTION_SKILL.diagnosis: The model leans on `hour` first, then `score`, then crude range/vol stats. The export contains NO actual indicators -- six comp_* aggregates, a regime label, a score. The reader has not failed to learn; it has been handed almost nothing to learn from.

WARRANT_443_EXIT_HEADROOM.the_question: Manuel's second half -- 'where the most profitable tps are without losing your gains and minimum loss without triggering sl before tp gets hit'. Both are exact per-trade path quantities and no warrant had ever asked for either.
WARRANT_443_EXIT_HEADROOM.not_the_retracted_measurement: Recomputed from raw high/low over 600 bars ignoring the shipped exit entirely -- this IS the fix ledger session 133 named as required after retracting the truncated mfe_atr/mae_atr columns.
WARRANT_443_EXIT_HEADROOM.THE_MARKET_GIVES_1_TO_1_FREE: Median favourable run before the stop is hit: SL1.0 -> 1.02, SL2.0 -> 2.00, SL3.0 -> 2.96, SL4.0 -> 3.79. Almost exactly 1:1 at every width, which is the signature of a driftless walk and independent confirmation of the fair-win-rate finding. EVERY R-MULTIPLE ABOVE 1:1 MUST BE BOUGHT WITH SELECTION. It is never free.
WARRANT_443_EXIT_HEADROOM.the_stop_distribution_is_fat_tailed: To reach a 2.5 ATR target the MEDIAN winner needed only a 2.03 ATR stop, but keeping 90% of winners needs 10.34 ATR -- a 5x spread. A fixed stop is structurally mismatched to that shape: it either amputates the tail or pays for it on every trade.
WARRANT_443_EXIT_HEADROOM.headroom: Best FIXED bracket TP2.0/SL4.0 at -0.13028 R. PER-TRADE ORACLE bracket +1.42785 R. Headroom for adaptive exit design +1.55812 R per trade.
WARRANT_443_EXIT_HEADROOM.but_unreachable_with_current_intel: Correlation of the required stop with every pre-entry feature the EA computes: atr -0.1135 (strongest, 1.3% of variance), abs_score +0.0343, comp_session -0.0411, everything else under 0.03. The headroom is real and NOT reachable with these features.

sessions.TWO_INSTRUMENTS_ONE_CONCLUSION: WARRANT#442 (entry, ceiling +1.45, capture 2.3%) and WARRANT#443 (exit, headroom +1.56, best predictor r=-0.11) were built independently and measure different things. Both land on: the opportunity is very large and the current feature set reads almost none of it. That is a far better position than 'there is no edge' -- the headroom is proven, and reading is the part that responds to trial and error.

WARRANTS_436_TO_441_THE_ROAD_HERE.436_timeframes: The resolution method run at M5/M15/M30/H1 with each timeframe's own ATR. Cost falls exactly as predicted (0.156 -> 0.083 -> 0.056 -> 0.038) and net improves monotonically, but no bracket is positive after cost at any timeframe.
WARRANTS_436_TO_441_THE_ROAD_HERE.437_grid_boundary: SL 3.0 won at EVERY timeframe in #436 -- which meant the GRID BOUNDARY was the finding, not the market. Extended to SL 8.0: pre-cost expectancy rises monotonically with stop width and CROSSES ZERO at H1 for SL>=4.0, best TP4.0/SL5.0 at +0.02061 pre-cost, 0.023 cost, -0.00213 net.
WARRANTS_436_TO_441_THE_ROAD_HERE.438_the_folds_killed_it: Fold spread -0.19 to +0.31, SE 0.063, the effect 0.3 SE from zero, 2 of 6 folds positive, random-direction control z=+1.69. EFFECTIVE SAMPLE 116, not 4,104 -- 36-hour spans on 4,166 candles overlap almost completely. The +0.0206 was the best of 90 cells measured on 116 observations.
WARRANTS_436_TO_441_THE_ROAD_HERE.439_hst_reader: MT4 .hst history read directly: 438,891 M5 bars across EURUSD/USDJPY/GBPUSD/USDCHF/EURJPY vs 50,000 of one pair in the export. Self-tested on OHLC invariants and monotone timestamps.
WARRANTS_436_TO_441_THE_ROAD_HERE.440_fair_win_rate: The reframe that untangles geometry from direction from cost: p_fair = SL/(TP+SL). On 5,820 INDEPENDENT trades pooled across 5 instruments, NO simple direction rule clears Bonferroni (|z|>2.81). Momentum is significantly NEGATIVE (-2.39%, z=-2.61). Random sits at ~0 exactly as it should, which validates the machinery.
WARRANTS_436_TO_441_THE_ROAD_HERE.441_per_regime: Exit sweep per regime with the SWORD IV admissibility floor. NO cell clears the multiplicity bar; largest |z| in 97 cells is 3.02 against an expected-max-of-noise of 3.02.

sessions.A_METHOD_ERROR_I_CAUGHT_IN_MY_OWN_TEST: WARRANT#441's first verdict said 'regimes differ by 4.8 SE'. Wrong test: I compared the MAXIMUM excess per regime across regimes whose n differed by 67x, and the maximum of a noisy sample grows as 1/sqrt(n). The ranking was perfectly monotone in 1/sqrt(n) -- regime 4 (n=66) +14.85%, regime 0 (n=4241) +0.55%. Corrected to compare z, and the verdict flipped to 'regimes do NOT want different exits; the adaptive-exit machinery is decoration'. Same class of error as the session-133 retraction, caught within one run this time.

FORGE_UNIFIED_EXTRACTION.the_reframe: FORGE UNIFIED III never charges cost in R -- every cost figure in it is spread/move, while the wall is spread/invalidation. Different denominators. The document does not contain a solution to the cost wall because it never met the wall.
FORGE_UNIFIED_EXTRACTION.the_load_bearing_finding: SWORD IV derives an admissibility floor: SL >= 2 spreads, TP >= 4 spreads. At 20 points that is SL >= 0.935 ATR -- so the ENTIRE SL=0.8 COLUMN IS INADMISSIBLE, and that column held 4 of the 6 pre-cost-positive brackets including the best. The session-long paradox ('the profitable brackets are exactly the unaffordable ones') was never a cruel coincidence; it was a rule violation. Below the floor a bracket resolves inside the noise band of the spread itself.
FORGE_UNIFIED_EXTRACTION.adopted: The floor is now enforced in WARRANT#441 and #443.

sessions.NEXT_SENTENCE: The market hands out 1:1 for free and charges skill for everything above it, so the only question worth measuring is how much of the 1.9 R between blind and perfect the system can actually read -- and today that number is 2.3%, which is honestly indistinguishable from zero.

sessions.type: WHY TUNGSTEN HAS NEVER OPENED A TRADE. Two nested deadlocks, both found at source level and both fixed. C1.5 and C2.2 earned.
sessions.THE_HEADLINE: This build has never opened a trade in the project's history, and four criteria (C6.3, C6.5, C6.6, C4) have been waiting on that single fact. The cause was not a threshold, a score or an edge problem. It was two interlocking control-flow defects that together guaranteed the system tore down its own calibration before it could ever trade, and could then never restart it.

WARRANT_446_DEADLOCK_ONE_CALIBRATION_CAN.the_chain: Entry is gated by `if(!g_Calibration.isComplete) return;`. WARRANT#420 had instrumented that and watched it fire 500 times reading `phase 0 - calibrating no` -- note BOTH halves: not complete AND not calibrating. Stopped, not stuck mid-way.
WARRANT_446_DEADLOCK_ONE_CALIBRATION_CAN.mechanism: Every calibration abort path clears isCalibrating and returns false WITHOUT setting isComplete -- the clearest is line 43189, `if(Bars < 600)`, whose own comment says it is mirroring 'the normal exit contract' (the normal exit is only safe because it ALSO sets isComplete). Meanwhile the only site that sets isCalibrating = true to START a calibration lives inside `else if(initPhase == 8)`, a one-shot progressive-init branch; initPhase advances to 9 and never returns. So: abort clears the flag, and nothing can ever set it again.
WARRANT_446_DEADLOCK_ONE_CALIBRATION_CAN.the_proof_it_is_a_bug_not_a_design: That one-shot block contains `g_Calibration.calibrationAttempts++` and `if(calibrationAttempts >= 5) { give up }`. A retry counter and a five-attempt cap are MEANINGLESS inside a block that executes once -- the counter can only ever reach 1. The code was written to be reachable repeatedly and was placed where it cannot be. Two further sites confirm the intent and have never been serviceable: line 58216 clears both flags under 'Reset calibration - force full recal on new TF', and 58595 clears both and sets calibrationAttempts = 0 for a 'fresh attempt count'. That is the 'four sites request a recalibration and none can get one' noted in c55_retry_plan.md, now confirmed at source.
WARRANT_446_DEADLOCK_ONE_CALIBRATION_CAN.fix: Hoisted the same condition, counter and cap out of the one-shot branch to run on any post-init tick, plus a loud stand-down that finally READS g_CalibFailReason (written by every abort path, read by nobody). A silent freeze is indistinguishable from a healthy idle system, which is the failure being fixed.

WARRANT_447_DEADLOCK_TWO_DRIFT_FIRES_ON_.what_the_fix_revealed: Immediately after that first-ever successful calibration: `CATREC| recalibrating drift source: multiple drift factors | anti-bias active`. TriggerCatastrophicRecalibration sets isComplete = false and isCalibrating = false -- discarding the calibration that had just succeeded. Before WARRANT#446 that froze the run permanently; after it, the run merely restarts. Either way no trade is ever reached.
WARRANT_447_DEADLOCK_TWO_DRIFT_FIRES_ON_.the_arithmetic_with_zero_trades: double liveWR = g_Risk.recentWinRate (0 with no trades); double livePF = (liveWR > 50) ? (...) : 1.0 (falls to 1.0). Then bool _wrDrift = (liveWR < calibWR - 5.0) -> 0 < calibWR-5 -> TRUE. bool _pfDrift = (livePF < 1.30) -> 1.0 < 1.30 -> TRUE. bool _regimeDrift = (signalTotal < 10) -> thin at startup -> TRUE. Three flags on a system that has never traded, and the reason code is derived as `(_wrDrift && _pfDrift) ? 4`, where 4 is 'multiple drift factors' -- exactly the string the log printed. The diagnosis is confirmed by the build's own output, not inferred.
WARRANT_447_DEADLOCK_TWO_DRIFT_FIRES_ON_.why_it_is_unambiguously_a_defect: Fifteen lines ABOVE, in the same function, the sibling checks are sample-guarded: `_calWeak = (_calWR < 0.62 && _tot >= 8)` and `_liveWeak = (g_RegimeStats[_r].trades >= 8 && _livWR < 0.55)`. Those refuse to call a rate weak without a sample. The drift flags below them do not. Same principle this campaign already settled for REPORTING a rate (WRStr / C3_RATE_FLOOR_N withhold a percentage and print the count when the sample is thin) -- and ACTING on a rate deserves at least as much care as printing it, since a catastrophic recalibration purges ProbDB, resets live threshold drift and discards the calibration.
WARRANT_447_DEADLOCK_TWO_DRIFT_FIRES_ON_.fix: New #define CATREC_MIN_LIVE_N 20. The two LIVE-derived flags may only be raised once that many live trades exist; a held check logs `drift check held | N live trades of 20 needed`. _ageOld and _regimeDrift are deliberately left ungated -- they describe the calibration's own age and coverage rather than live outcomes, and either alone leaves _driftFlags at 1, which routes to the mild recalibration branch instead of the catastrophic one. Floor is 20 rather than the neighbours' 8 because those gate a cheap reversible per-regime block while this gates a full teardown.
WARRANT_447_DEADLOCK_TWO_DRIFT_FIRES_ON_.verified_in_run: `CATREC| drift check held | 0 live trades of 20 needed | no live result to compare against yet` -- the teardown is now held instead of firing.
WARRANT_447_DEADLOCK_TWO_DRIFT_FIRES_ON_.failure_mode_if_wrong: A genuine mid-life WR collapse is ignored until 20 live trades accumulate. That is the correct trade against the shipped behaviour, which is that the system destroys its calibration before taking a single trade, forever.

sessions.OPEN_DECISION_FOR_MANUEL_C5_5: Not a code problem -- a genuine conflict, so it is not being guessed. The sizing chain has two LEGITIMATE paths to a tiny size: CEODeRiskFloorPercent = 0.5 sits deliberately below MinRiskPercent = 1.5 (that is C8.3's de-risking mandate), and forcedMinLot is an intentional 'edge observation mode'. But two things are straightforwardly wrong: (a) `if(lotSize < minLot && baseRiskPercent <= 1.5) { targetRiskPercent = 2.5; ... }` INFLATES risk to 2.5% precisely when the reducers decided it should be small; (b) `lotSize = MathMax(minLot, MathMin(maxLot, lotSize))` turns a computed size of ZERO into one minimum lot, so C5.1's Kelly-at-low-n and C5.2's drawdown fade cannot actually stand the system down. The build's own comment already admits the logged size and the sent size differ. RECOMMENDATION ON RECORD: quantise size to {0} union [minRisk, inf) -- either at least minRisk or no trade -- and delete the 2.5% inflation. That satisfies C5.5, makes C5.1/C5.2 effective, and fixes the log/reality mismatch. It reduces trade frequency, which is why it is Manuel's call and not this layer's.

FIX_A_REFMAX_EVERY_SCORE_WAS_COMPRESSED_.the_defect: _refMax = 42*wM + 25*wMo + 18*wV + 14*wVo + 10*wS + 22*wP + 20 + 18 (=169 at unit weights), and _norm = rawTotal * (88/_refMax). Those six constants are supposed to be each component's maximum contribution. Measured over the 50,000-bar export, NONE of them was right, and they were wrong in BOTH directions: comp_mtf assumed 42.0 / actual 36.00 (86%); comp_momentum 25.0 / 28.75 (115%, EXCEEDS its cap); comp_volatility 18.0 / 15.00 (83%); comp_volume 14.0 / 19.50 (139%, EXCEEDS its cap); comp_session 10.0 / 10.00 (100%); comp_pattern 22.0 / 5.00 (23%, structurally dead).
FIX_A_REFMAX_EVERY_SCORE_WAS_COMPRESSED_.the_consequence: Sum of assumed caps 131.0 against 114.25 jointly reachable, so _refMax read 169.0 where the components support 152.25 and K = 88/_refMax was 0.5207 instead of 0.5780. EVERY SCORE IN THE BUILD WAS COMPRESSED BY 11%. That matters because the entry threshold floor is MathMax(60.0, ...) at four sites while the score's own 99th percentile was +55.69 -- THE FLOOR SAT ABOVE THE 99TH PERCENTILE OF THE THING IT GATES, so under 1% of bars could ever fire. Corrected, p99 lands near +61.8 and clears that floor for the first time.

FIX_A_REFMAX_EVERY_SCORE_WAS_COMPRESSED_.single_source_verified: ScoreNormaliseRefMax is the only definition; its three callers are the normaliser (7293), the inverse (7308) and the parity test (7416). No second copy of the coefficients exists, so the change is consistent across every path.

FIX_B_THE_GHOST_GATE_NOW_CONSULTS_HISTOR.the_defect: The recovery ghost demands 5 live paper trades before it will judge. FIX_B_THE_GHOST_GATE_NOW_CONSULTS_HISTOR.why_it_did_not_fire_in_the_verification_: The run logged `fresh parameter search`, i.e. hasHistoricalInsights was FALSE. Reason: testBars = MathMin(10000, Bars - 100), and MT4 hands the tester only ~1,001 bars at init, so the sweep runs on ~900 bars and finds nothing. The earlier run that DID produce 864 signals got them because the calibration deadlock kept re-running calibration at later simulated times, by which point 10,000 bars had loaded. THE DEADLOCK WAS ACCIDENTALLY FEEDING THE HISTORICAL BACKTESTER THE HISTORY IT NEEDS, and fixing the deadlock removed that side effect. FINDING_COMPOSED_TOTAL_PARITY_DIVERGES_W.what: The build's own PARITY-SCORE test reports mean |diff| 19.49 and max |diff| 52.31 with 195 of 197 bars beyond its 0.50-point tolerance. Across six runs today the figure was 19.09 / 19.65 / 21.70 / 20.34 / 21.70 / 19.49 -- INCLUDING RUNS BEFORE ANY OF TODAY'S EDITS, so this predates WARRANT#449 and the _refMax change did not cause it (19.09 before, 19.49 after, inside the run-to-run spread).
FINDING_COMPOSED_TOTAL_PARITY_DIVERGES_W.and_C1_3_is_NOT_a_false_pass: C1.3 grades COMPONENT-level sign-exact parity -- six components through one implementation, 0 mismatches each, verified this run. That verdict is sound and correctly scoped. But the COMPOSED TOTAL diverging by ~19 points while all six components agree sign-exact means the defect is in the COMPOSITION step (weights, normalisation, or the +20+18 tail), not in the components. FINDING_COMPOSED_TOTAL_PARITY_DIVERGES_W.why_it_matters: A 19-point mean divergence on a 0..100 score is roughly a third of the distance from the score's median to its 99th percentile. Any calibration conclusion expressed in composed-total units is therefore not directly comparable to a live composed total.

sessions.type: THE ADAPTIVE BRACKET, THE PROVING GROUND, AND BELT L4. The system now picks its own TP/SL per moment and decides when to sit out -- and its chosen trades are profitable BEFORE cost in 4 of 5 unseen proving periods.

WARRANT_453_ADAPTIVE_BRACKET.the_reformulation: Every prior warrant asked 'which single bracket is best on average', which forces one answer onto every market condition. Replaced with a decision under uncertainty evaluated per bar BEFORE the trade runs: EV(b|x) = p(win|x,b)*(TP/SL) - (1-p) - spread/(SL*ATR_x); take argmax_b EV if positive, else SIT OUT. Three consequences, all of them what Manuel asked for: the bracket is chosen per moment; the sit-out decision is FREE (it is the same arithmetic declining, not a second system with its own threshold); and cost enters the DECISION at this bar's volatility rather than being charged afterwards, so WARRANT#451's 4.2x volatility lever is exploited automatically.
WARRANT_453_ADAPTIVE_BRACKET.features: 121 total -- 112 from indicator_battery.py (causality self-test: max deviation 0 across 24 probe indices, planted canary caught, so the test is not vacuous) plus 9 EA live columns. Side-dependent features are multiplied by the trade's direction using the battery's own `signed`/`center` metadata, so a long and a short in mirror conditions look identical to the model.
WARRANT_453_ADAPTIVE_BRACKET.results_out_of_sample: best FIXED bracket -0.17784 R | adaptive never-sits-out -0.21365 | adaptive+sit-out -0.12645 | adaptive+sit-out+selectivity (EV floor 0.20) -0.06152 at 24.8 trades/day, 50.5% WR | random bracket at same rate -0.30769 | ORACLE +0.41772 | shuffled-label control collapses to 17 trades and 99.8% sit-out.
WARRANT_453_ADAPTIVE_BRACKET.what_each_piece_is_worth: choosing the bracket +0.18 R vs random at the same rate; sitting out +0.087 R; selectivity a further +0.065 R. It uses ALL EIGHT brackets (TP4.0/SL2.5 42%, TP3.0/SL4.0 25%, TP3.0/SL2.5 15%) so the adaptivity is real rather than one bracket in disguise.
WARRANT_453_ADAPTIVE_BRACKET.capture: 2.3% -> 19.5% of the fixed-to-oracle span in one session.
WARRANT_453_ADAPTIVE_BRACKET.the_selectivity_curve_has_a_real_optimum: Expectancy improves monotonically as the EV bar is raised -- -0.126 at floor 0.00, -0.062 at 0.20 -- and then DEGRADES again (-0.093 at 0.30, -0.148 at 0.40). The peak sits at 24.8 trades/day. Past it the model is being asked to trust its most confident predictions, which are the most overfitted. Manuel's intuition that 'theres a perfect optimum' is correct and it is located.

WARRANT_454_THE_PROVING_GROUND_BELT_L4.manuels_framing: 'training will consist of a training period and a prooving period where it tests how much its learnt - until it reaches a threshold we are happy with like a robot machine learning to walk and run and then run a certain speed and do backflips'. Built as a graded ladder over 5 walk-forward folds with a 3x-median-span embargo; a belt is earned only if it holds in a MAJORITY of folds.
WARRANT_454_THE_PROVING_GROUND_BELT_L4.belts: L1 CHOOSES (beats random bracket at same rate) 5/5 EARNED. L2 ADAPTS (beats best fixed) 3/5 EARNED. L3 SITS OUT (beats its own never-sit-out variant) 5/5 EARNED. L4 PROFITS PRE-COST 4/5 EARNED. L5 BREAKEVEN AFTER COST 0/5. L6 AT SPEED 0/5. BELT REACHED: L4 of 6.
WARRANT_454_THE_PROVING_GROUND_BELT_L4.THE_HEADLINE: L4 means that on bars the model had never seen, in 4 of 5 proving periods, THE TRADES IT CHOSE WERE PROFITABLE BEFORE THE SPREAD WAS CHARGED. The system can find winning moments; it cannot yet pay the toll. Those are different problems and the second is far more tractable. Every remaining lever is now a COST lever -- volatility selection, wider stops, instrument/broker spread, limit-order entry -- not a signal lever.
WARRANT_454_THE_PROVING_GROUND_BELT_L4.it_is_NOT_improving_with_data: Proving score vs log(training size): slope -0.062960, correlation -0.877. Later folds do WORSE. Tested whether stale data was the cause: a rolling 6,000-entry window beat the expanding window in only 2 of 5 folds and by -0.02667 R on average. So RECENCY IS NOT THE LEVER -- the later periods are genuinely harder, not the older data heavier. More history will not fix this, which is worth knowing now rather than after another 50,000 bars.

A_GRID_BOUNDARY_ERROR_I_REPEATED_AND_MAN.what: Manuel: 'im worried about the tp sl ratios ... they saved our capital over time while requiring a low win rate and sitll compound significant gains'. My bracket grid topped out at a 1.6 payoff ratio (TP4.0/SL2.5) -- I never tested 3:1 or 4:1. Concluding 'high ratios are worse' from that grid is EXACTLY the boundary error WARRANT#437 already made once, where SL=3.0 won at every timeframe because it was the widest tested.
A_GRID_BOUNDARY_ERROR_I_REPEATED_AND_MAN.and_the_deeper_error: I ranked brackets by MEAN R, which is the ARITHMETIC mean. Manuel's argument is about COMPOUNDING, which is governed by the GEOMETRIC mean, where variance and drawdown are first-order costs rather than footnotes. Two brackets with identical mean R can compound completely differently, and a low-win-rate/high-payoff bracket is exactly the case where the two diverge most. His capital-preservation claim was being tested in the wrong units.
A_GRID_BOUNDARY_ERROR_I_REPEATED_AND_MAN.action: Agent dispatched to extend ratios to 6:1 and rank by expected log-growth E[ln(1+f*R)] at Kelly and half-Kelly, with drawdown distribution, longest losing streak, and terminal wealth -- the units the claim is actually made in.

EXIT_ENGINEERING_CLOSED_FIVE_WAYS_THEN_R.the_algebra: With fair = 1/(1+m) and actual = fair x (1+lift), E[R] = fair(1+lift)(m+1) - 1 = lift FOR EVERY BRACKET m. Expected R equals the timing lift regardless of the target multiple.

EXIT_ENGINEERING_CLOSED_FIVE_WAYS_THEN_R.WARRANT_456_A_BUG_I_CAUGHT_MYSELF: My first trail simulation reported +0.22 R and a 75% win rate. It was WRONG -- I detected the trail being hit with favR[k], derived from the bar's HIGH, when a trailing stop is taken out by the LOW. What exposed it was an internal contradiction: the measured median pullback is 0.744 of the run's own peak, so a 0.2R trail cannot possibly survive. Corrected: +0.008.
EXIT_ENGINEERING_CLOSED_FIVE_WAYS_THEN_R.WARRANT_457_NO_ARM_POINT_EXISTS: E[final | peak reached p] vs banking p: +0.121 vs 0.10 at p=0.1, +0.506 vs 0.50 at p=0.5, +0.902 vs 0.90 at p=0.9. Holding beats banking at EVERY level, so Manuel's condition 'never before it benefits us' is never met. The excess IS the timing edge and it decays from +0.021 to +0.002 -- the edge is FRONT-LOADED.
EXIT_ENGINEERING_CLOSED_FIVE_WAYS_THEN_R.WARRANT_458_BUT_MANUEL_WAS_RIGHT_ABOUT_T: The neutrality proof assumes lift is CONSTANT across brackets. Conditioning on entry quality, it is not: with the stop fixed, lift by target on the top confidence decile runs +6.75% (TP1.0), +12.65% (TP2.0), +20.02% (TP5.0) -- the optimal target MOVES OUTWARD with confidence, from ~2.5-3.0 on all bars to 5.0 in the top decile. My neutrality reading was an artefact of averaging over every bar. A high-confidence entry is one where a large move is expected, so a distant target becomes reachable.
EXIT_ENGINEERING_CLOSED_FIVE_WAYS_THEN_R.WARRANT_459_THE_STOP_DOES_NOT_ADAPT: Manuel proposed tight stops on medium confidence. Measured: the optimal stop is 4.0 ATR in EVERY confidence band, and net R improves monotonically as the stop widens in all four bands. A tighter stop does NOT reduce the loss (sizing is computed from the stop, so a loss is -1R either way) -- it multiplies the spread's share of risk. The way to risk less on a medium trade is a SMALLER POSITION, not a tighter stop.

WARRANT_461_THE_PARADIGM_MANUEL_NAMED.his_words: 'theres a paradigm somewhere youre missing compare various risks per situations too'
WARRANT_461_THE_PARADIGM_MANUEL_NAMED.the_error: Every number in the campaign is expressed in R -- multiples of the risk taken -- which silently assumes the risk is THE SAME ON EVERY TRADE. Under that assumption the only decision left is binary: take it or skip it. So the whole campaign solved a SELECTION problem when the actual problem is ALLOCATION. Expectancy ranged from -0.27 R to +0.26 R across situations while the same stake rode on each.
WARRANT_461_THE_PARADIGM_MANUEL_NAMED.and_the_discipline_that_followed: 49 cells were net-positive on the point estimate; exactly TWO survived a 95% Wilson lower bound, and the best stake collapsed from 20.5% of capital to 1.7%. A single cell had printed x1080 over a year -- that is what Kelly does with an edge estimated on 86 observations, not a discovery.

WARRANT_462_THE_EDGE_TRANSFERS.method: Five instruments, both directions offered as separate candidates so the model picks side, leave-one-instrument-out, REAL timestamps from the .hst files.
WARRANT_462_THE_EDGE_TRANSFERS.result: Positive lift over the driftless fair rate on EVERY held-out pair: EURJPY +8.0%, EURUSD +10.3%, USDJPY +12.7%, GBPUSD +16.2%, USDCHF +28.4%. Not one was trained on. This is the strongest evidence in the campaign that the model learned something general about price structure rather than USDJPY's particular character.
WARRANT_462_THE_EDGE_TRANSFERS.but: Net after cost positive on only 3 of 5, and only USDCHF survives the 95% lower bound. Cost decides who is profitable, not the signal -- EURUSD has BETTER lift than USDJPY and worse net, purely on spread-to-ATR.

sessions.WARRANT_463_THE_HONEST_ACCOUNT: One account, all five instruments, time-ordered, positions holding capital until they resolve, sized by the survival rule. Cap 10: +15.2% CAGR, 27.9% max drawdown, 3.4 trades/day, 471 trading days. TRADING ONE POSITION AT A TIME LOSES MONEY (-8.7%) -- at cap 1 you take whichever signal arrives while free, and you are free most often right after a FAST trade, which is disproportionately a quick loss. Concurrency removes a selection bias, not just a throughput limit. At cap 1, 83% of signals were declined for a full book: throughput is the constraint, not signal count.

WARRANT_464_THE_BIGGEST_SINGLE_GAIN.manuels_idea: 'mulitple trades on the best timed ones at slightly different points' -- read correctly, that is LIMIT PLACEMENT, and a limit order does not cross the spread.
WARRANT_464_THE_BIGGEST_SINGLE_GAIN.result: market -0.161 R vs limit at 1.0 ATR back -0.025 R. Counting unfilled as zero: market -0.1605 vs limit -0.0163 PER SIGNAL RECEIVED. Worth +0.136 R, by far the largest single improvement found.
WARRANT_464_THE_BIGGEST_SINGLE_GAIN.and_the_honest_decomposition: Gross edges are nearly identical (-0.0305 market vs -0.0253 limit). ESSENTIALLY 100% OF THE GAIN IS THE TOLL NOT PAID, not better entries. The +13.3pp win-rate difference is a mechanically easier bracket (entering 1 ATR lower on a long puts the target 2 ATR away instead of 3), and it washes out in R.
WARRANT_464_THE_BIGGEST_SINGLE_GAIN.caveats: Fill-on-touch is assumed; real queue position can miss. Zero spread assumes the exit does not cross either. The half-spread variant is -0.091, still far better than -0.161.

WARRANT_467_THE_MOST_CONSEQUENTIAL_TABLE.why_it_is_violently_nonlinear: A lower spread does not merely improve each trade -- it makes far more trades pass the sizing test at all. Edge per trade and number of admissible trades rise TOGETHER.
WARRANT_467_THE_MOST_CONSEQUENTIAL_TABLE.and_it_kills_the_limit_workaround: At low spread MARKET entry is BETTER than limit: market tier-A wins 60.0% (lower bound 59.1%) against limit's 58.2% (57.1%). The pullback entries select worse signals. The entire limit-order apparatus, with its unverifiable queue assumption, was a workaround for an expensive broker.
WARRANT_467_THE_MOST_CONSEQUENTIAL_TABLE.commission_warning: A raw-spread account advertising 0.6 pips typically also charges ~$7/lot round turn, roughly 0.7 pips, so the EFFECTIVE spread is ~1.3. The question to put to a broker is the all-in round-turn cost per standard lot, not the advertised spread.

WARRANT_468_DIVERSIFICATION_MANUEL_WAS_R.his_words: 'multiple trades can leverage us here compounding is meant to be tons more powerful than youve claimed it to be'
WARRANT_468_DIVERSIFICATION_MANUEL_WAS_R.my_error: Every concurrency sweep used the SAME per-trade fraction regardless of cap, so raising the cap raised total risk and concurrency looked like a trade-off. For N positions at correlation rho, Var = N f^2 sigma^2 [1 + (N-1) rho] -- at low rho that is N f^2, NOT (N f)^2. Holding risk constant means staking f/sqrt(N) and carrying f*sqrt(N), so GROWTH SCALES AS sqrt(N).
WARRANT_468_DIVERSIFICATION_MANUEL_WAS_R.measured_rho: +0.077 across the five pairs' daily P/L -- far lower than the 0.3+ I expected. Effective independent positions saturate at 1/rho = 13.
WARRANT_468_DIVERSIFICATION_MANUEL_WAS_R.what_it_buys: At constant stake-scaled risk, growth is flat but DRAWDOWN COLLAPSES: 13.7% at cap 1 to 3.3% at cap 50. Drawdown room is the binding constraint. Levering every row to the same 40% allowance: cap 1 gives +2.6% CAGR, cap 30 gives +17.6%. DIVERSIFICATION IS WORTH ~6.8x ON COMPOUNDING AT IDENTICAL RISK -- from many small simultaneous positions and then spending the room they free, not from betting more per trade.

WARRANT_469_THE_MAXIMAL_CONFIGURATION.spec: $100, 100 trading days, <=20 trades/day, 0.5 pip spread, all survival paths.
WARRANT_469_THE_MAXIMAL_CONFIGURATION.best: TP4.00/SL4.00, tiers at the 90th/60th percentile with half stake on tier B, cap 10. 10.3 trades/day, win rate 53.2%, 4,833 trades in sample. UNLEVERED +19.1% CAGR at 7.1% max drawdown. Levered 5.6x to the 40% allowance: +100.8% CAGR. 100 DAYS FROM $100 -> $131.86 (unlevered $107.20).
WARRANT_469_THE_MAXIMAL_CONFIGURATION.tight_stops_still_lose: Every one of the top 15 uses SL 3.0-4.0 ATR. At SL 0.5 the toll is still ~1.7 R even at half a pip, because M5 ATR is small relative to any spread. Tight stops need a HIGHER TIMEFRAME, not a cheaper broker -- the quantity that matters is SL x ATR in absolute price.

WHY_5_PERCENT_A_DAY_IS_NOT_AVAILABLE.the_decomposition: full Kelly on the measured edge ~2.1%/day; x the survival rule (c=0.20, growth scales as c(2-c)=0.36) -> ~0.76%/day; x sizing off the Wilson lower bound rather than the point estimate -> ~0.28%/day. Two thirds of the loss is Manuel's own >=60% capital rule, and it is not waste: full Kelly on this edge carries a 60% chance of eventually being down 60%.
WHY_5_PERCENT_A_DAY_IS_NOT_AVAILABLE.and_why_sizing_cannot_fix_it: Kelly growth scales with the SQUARE of the edge. Going from +0.28%/day to +5%/day is 18x, needing sqrt(18) = 4.25x the edge. Current edge 2p-1 = 0.064 (53.2%); required 0.27, i.e. A 63.5% WIN RATE. +5%/day is not a leverage, frequency or compounding problem -- it is a 10-point win-rate problem.
WHY_5_PERCENT_A_DAY_IS_NOT_AVAILABLE.what_is_available_today: Sizing on the point estimate rather than its pessimistic bound roughly DOUBLES the 100-day result, $132 -> ~$210. That is a real decision with a real risk and it is Manuel's to make.
WHY_5_PERCENT_A_DAY_IS_NOT_AVAILABLE.the_diversification_ceiling: At rho = 0.077, +0.5%/day (~34 trades/day) is reachable; +1.0%/day would need ~134 trades/day which exceeds the 13-effective-position ceiling. Diversification alone tops out near +0.5-0.6%/day.
